Core idea in one paragraph + +HippoRAG 2 builds a cheap, LLM-extracted *provenance graph* over a corpus — passage nodes, entity ("phrase") nodes, and three edge kinds (fact co-occurrence, passage-contains-entity, embedding synonymy) — and at query time it does **not** ask the LLM to reason over the graph. Instead it (1) embeds the query and dense-retrieves *triple facts* (`query_to_fact`), (2) optionally lets a small LLM "recognition memory" filter (`DSPyFilter`) prune the candidate facts, (3) converts the surviving facts' subject/object phrases into personalised reset weights on entity nodes, adds a small dense-passage prior (`passage_node_weight=0.05`) on every passage node, and (4) runs **Personalized PageRank** (igraph `prpack`, damping 0.5) on the undirected weighted graph. The PPR mass that lands on passage nodes is the final ranking; the top-k passages are handed to a plain reading-comprehension prompt. The design goal is "memory-like" multi-hop associativity with a single embedding call plus one small LLM call per query, and a *continual* index that can be grown or shrunk without re-running extraction. + +## 3. Indexing pipeline, step by step + +Entry point: `HippoRAG.index(docs)` in `HippoRAG.py` (line ~499). The method is idempotent over chunk hashes and incremental by design. + +### 3.1 Chunking / preprocessing +* `preprocessing.py` defines `BaseTextPreprocessor` and the default `TextPreprocessor`, which **does not split documents**: it keeps one `Chunk` per input string (`Chunk(content, source_id, metadata)` dataclass in `utils/misc_utils.py`). You are expected to chunk upstream or inject your own preprocessor (`text_preprocessor=` constructor arg; `text_preprocessor_class_name`, `preprocess_chunk_max_token_size`, `preprocess_chunk_overlap_token_size=128`, `preprocess_chunk_func` exist in `BaseConfig` but the default class ignores them). +* Chunk IDs are `compute_mdhash_id(content, prefix="chunk-")` (MD5 of content). Chunk metadata (`source_id`, user metadata) is persisted separately in `chunk_metadata.json`. + +### 3.2 OpenIE: two LLM calls per chunk +Module: `information_extraction/openie_openai.py`, class `OpenIE` (used for any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint; `openie_vllm_offline.py` / `openie_transformers_offline.py` are the local variants selected via `openie_mode`). + +1. **NER** — `OpenIE.ner(chunk_key, passage)` renders prompt template `ner` (`prompts/templates/ner.py`): a one-shot system/user/assistant exchange ("Radio City" example) asking for `{"named_entities": [...]}`. Output cap `openie_ner_max_tokens=2048`. +2. **Triple extraction** — `OpenIE.triple_extraction(chunk_key, passage, named_entities)` renders template `triple_extraction` (`prompts/templates/triple_extraction.py`): "construct an RDF graph … each triple should contain at least one, but preferably two, of the named entities … resolve pronouns". Output `{"triples": [[s, p, o], ...]}`. Output cap `openie_triple_max_tokens=4096`. +3. `OpenIE.batch_openie(chunks)` runs all NER calls on a `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=openie_max_workers)` (default 8), fails hard if any NER call errored, then runs all triple calls. Responses are parsed by `_extract_json_list_field` / `_parse_bare_json_string_list` with tolerant JSON extraction. +4. Results are merged into `all_openie_info` (list of `{idx, passage, extracted_entities, extracted_triples}`) and persisted to `openie_results_ner_.json` in `save_dir` (`save_openie_results`). `load_existing_openie()` means re-indexing only extracts for chunks without stored OpenIE output. `openie_mode='offline'` runs `pre_openie()` which extracts, saves, then deliberately raises so you can rerun online with cached results. + +All LLM calls go through `llm/openai_gpt.py::CacheOpenAI`, which caches responses in an SQLite file (`save_dir/llm_cache/_cache.sqlite`) guarded by `filelock`, and *fails closed* if the endpoint does not return `usage` token counts. + +### 3.3 Normalisation and node/fact extraction +* `utils/misc_utils.py::text_processing()` casefolds, strips non-alphanumerics to spaces, collapses whitespace. All triples are normalised this way before becoming graph keys (so "Radio City" and "radio city" collapse). +* `extract_entity_nodes(chunk_triples)` yields the set of subject/object phrases; `flatten_facts()` yields the set of unique triples. + +### 3.4 Embeddings: three stores +`embedding_store.py::get_embedding_store()` creates three namespaces, each keyed by MD5 hash with prefix: + +| Store | Namespace / prefix | Text embedded | +|---|---|---| +| `chunk_embedding_store` | `chunk-` | raw passage text | +| `entity_embedding_store` | `entity-` | normalised phrase | +| `fact_embedding_store` | `fact-` | `str((s, p, o))` tuple string | + +`insert_strings()` only embeds hashes not already present (`get_missing_string_hash_ids`). Default backend is Parquet (`vdb_.parquet` under `save_dir/_/`). Embedding model is selected by `embedding_model/__init__.py::_get_embedding_model_class()` (NV-Embed-v2 default, GritLM, Contriever, OpenAI `text-embedding-*`, Cohere, `Transformers/`, `VLLM/`, or explicit `embedding_provider`). Instruction-tuned models get task instructions from `prompts/linking.py::get_query_instruction()`. + +### 3.5 Graph construction (igraph) +Graph lives in `self.graph` (`igraph.Graph`, undirected by default `is_directed_graph=False`), pickled to `graph.pickle`. + +1. `add_fact_edges(chunk_ids, chunk_triples)` — for each triple adds an entity–entity edge key `(entity-hash(s), entity-hash(o))`, weight incremented by 1 per occurrence, and records `_fact_edge_source_counts[edge][chunk_id]` for provenance. Also fills `ent_node_to_chunk_ids`. +2. `add_passage_edges(chunk_ids, chunk_triple_entities)` — for each *new* chunk adds `(chunk-id, entity-id)` edges with weight 1.0 (`_passage_edge_sources`). +3. `add_synonymy_edges(query_node_keys)` — KNN (`utils/embed_utils.py::retrieve_knn`, batched dot products) of **new** entity embeddings against all entity embeddings, `k=synonymy_edge_topk` (2047), keep neighbours with cosine >= `synonymy_edge_sim_threshold` (0.8), max 100 per node, skip phrases shorter than 3 alphanumerics. Edge weight = similarity score. Only new entities are queried, so incremental cost is `O(new x all)`. +4. `augment_graph()` -> `add_new_nodes()` (vertices from entity + chunk stores, attribute `name` = hash id, plus `content`) and `add_new_edges()`, which merges contributions by logical `(source_key, target_key)` so re-indexing never creates parallel edges. Edge attributes: `weight`, `edge_kind` (`fact`, `synonym`, `fact+synonym`, `passage`), `fact_source_counts`, `synonym_score`, `passage_source`, `source_key`, `target_key`. Graph-level attribute `hipporag_edge_schema=1` marks the source-aware schema; older pickles are rejected for further indexing/deletion. +5. `save_igraph()` pickles. `index_manifest.json` (`utils/state_utils.py::validate_or_create_index_manifest`) binds the index to LLM name, embedding model/endpoint/normalisation, OpenIE token limits, synonymy settings and `index_identity`; mismatches raise `StateConsistencyError` rather than silently mixing state. + +### 3.6 Flowchart + +```mermaid +flowchart TD + A[docs: str or Chunk] --> B[TextPreprocessor.preprocess
one Chunk per doc by default] + B --> C[chunk_embedding_store.insert_strings
MD5 chunk- ids, embed passages] + C --> D{OpenIE cached for chunk?} + D -- no --> E[OpenIE.ner prompt 'ner'] + E --> F[OpenIE.triple_extraction prompt 'triple_extraction'] + F --> G[openie_results_ner_LLM.json] + D -- yes --> G + G --> H[text_processing normalise triples] + H --> I[entity_embedding_store.insert_strings
fact_embedding_store.insert_strings] + I --> J[add_fact_edges entity-entity w+=1
add_passage_edges chunk-entity w=1] + J --> K[add_synonymy_edges KNN cos>=0.8
only new entities] + K --> L[augment_graph: add_new_nodes / add_new_edges
merge by logical key] + L --> M[save_igraph graph.pickle + index_manifest.json] +``` + +## 4. Graph data model + +| Element | Key | Attributes | Notes | +|---|---|---|---| +| Passage node | `chunk-` | `name`, `content` | one per chunk; also row in chunk Parquet store with embedding; metadata in `chunk_metadata.json` | +| Phrase (entity) node | `entity-` | `name`, `content` | from triple subjects/objects only (NER entities not in any triple are *not* nodes) | +| Fact | `fact-` | stored in fact embedding store only | **not** a graph node; facts are the dense-retrieval unit at query time and map back to entity nodes through `(s, o)` | +| Fact edge | entity–entity | `weight` = #supporting (chunk, triple) occurrences, `fact_source_counts {chunk_id: n}`, `edge_kind='fact'` | predicate text is **not** stored on the edge | +| Passage edge | chunk–entity | `weight=1.0`, `passage_source=chunk_id`, `edge_kind='passage'` | provenance for PPR mass to flow into passages | +| Synonymy edge | entity–entity | `weight = cosine sim`, `synonym_score`, `edge_kind='synonym'` or `'fact+synonym'` when it coincides with a fact edge | weight = `max(sum(fact counts), synonym_score)` after merge | + +Auxiliary in-memory maps built in `prepare_retrieval_objects()`: `node_name_to_vertex_idx`, `passage_node_idxs`, `entity_node_idxs`, `ent_node_to_chunk_ids`, `proc_triples_to_docs` (normalised triple -> chunk ids), plus dense matrices `entity_embeddings`, `passage_embeddings`, `fact_embeddings` loaded fully into RAM. + +## 5. Storage backends supported + +| Concern | Options | Default | +|---|---|---| +| Graph | igraph pickle only (`graph.pickle`). No external graph DB. | igraph | +| Vectors | `vector_store_type` in `{"parquet","qdrant","chroma","milvus"}` (`vector_stores/qdrant_store.py`, `chroma_store.py`, `milvus_store.py`; all subclass `BaseEmbeddingStore`) | `parquet` (local pandas/pyarrow) | +| Remote collection naming | `vector_stores/naming.py`; per-index `vector_store_namespace`, endpoint fingerprinted in `index_manifest.json` | derived from `save_dir` | +| Milvus | `milvus_uri`, `milvus_token`, `milvus_db_name`, `milvus_consistency_level`; Milvus Lite file if no URI | Milvus Lite | +| Qdrant / Chroma | `qdrant_url`/`qdrant_api_key`; `chroma_host`/`chroma_port` | local | +| OpenIE results | JSON file in `save_dir` | — | +| LLM cache | SQLite in `save_dir/llm_cache/` | enabled | + +Note that even with a remote vector store, retrieval still pulls **all** embeddings into numpy arrays (`prepare_retrieval_objects`) and scores by full dot product; the vector DB is persistence, not ANN search. + +## 6. Query / retrieval modes + +### 6.1 Main mode: `HippoRAG.retrieve(queries, num_to_retrieve)` (HippoRAG 2 retrieval) + +1. `get_query_embeddings()` encodes each query twice (or once if the embedding model is instruction-agnostic): with `query_to_fact` and `query_to_passage` instructions. +2. `get_fact_scores(query)` -> min-max-normalised dot products against **all** fact embeddings. +3. `rerank_facts(query, scores)`: take top `linking_top_k` (default **5**) facts, then `DSPyFilter` (`rerank.py`) — the "recognition memory" step. It renders a DSPy-compiled prompt (`prompts/filter_default_prompt.py::best_dspy_prompt`, or a JSON file via `rerank_dspy_file_path`, e.g. `prompts/dspy_prompts/filter_llama3.3-70B-Instruct.json`) with ten few-shot demos; instruction: "select up to 4 relevant facts … only use facts from the candidate list … return `{"fact": [...]}`". Output facts are mapped back to candidate indices. Exceptions degrade to an empty list. +4. If no facts survive -> fall back to `dense_passage_retrieval(query)` (pure DPR ranking). +5. Else `graph_search_with_fact_entities(query, link_top_k, query_fact_scores, top_k_facts, ...)`: + * For each surviving fact, add its score to `phrase_weights[subject]` and `[object]`, **divided by the number of chunks that mention that entity** (`len(ent_node_to_chunk_ids[phrase])`) — a specificity/IDF-style damping of hub entities; then average over occurrences. + * `get_top_k_weights(link_top_k, ...)` zeroes everything but the top `linking_top_k` phrases. + * `dense_passage_retrieval(query)` -> min-max normalised scores x `passage_node_weight` (0.05) assigned to *every* passage node. + * `node_weights = phrase_weights + passage_weights` -> `run_ppr(node_weights, damping=0.5)` -> `igraph.personalized_pagerank(directed=False, weights='weight', reset=..., implementation='prpack')`. + * Passage node PPR scores sorted descending = result. `retrieval_top_k` default 200 (`num_to_retrieve`). +6. `_build_retrieval_result()` returns `QuerySolution(question, docs, doc_scores, doc_metadata, graph_seeds=top_k_facts)`. + +Timing counters (`rerank_time`, `ppr_time`) are logged. Retrieval evaluation (`RetrievalRecall@k`, k in `[1,2,5,10,20,30,50,100,150,200]`) runs if `gold_docs` are passed. + +### 6.2 Other modes +* `retrieve_dpr` / `rag_qa_dpr` — pure dense baseline inside the same class; `StandardRAG.py` is the standalone DPR baseline used by `main.py --rag_type standard`. +* `retrieve_ircot` / `answer_with_ircot` — iterative IRCoT-style multi-step retrieval (`max_qa_steps`, templates `ircot_hotpotqa|musique|2wikimultihopqa`). Default `max_qa_steps=1` disables iteration. +* MCP tools (`mcp_server.py`): `retrieve`, `rag_qa`, `index`, `delete`, `index_stats`; resource `hipporag://config`. + +### 6.3 Sequence diagram (main mode) + +```mermaid +sequenceDiagram + participant U as Caller + participant H as HippoRAG.retrieve + participant E as EmbeddingModel + participant F as fact_embedding_store + participant R as DSPyFilter (LLM) + participant G as igraph PPR + U->>H: retrieve([query], k) + H->>E: encode(query, query_to_fact) / encode(query, query_to_passage) + H->>F: dot(fact_embeddings, q) -> min-max normalise + H->>H: top linking_top_k=5 facts + H->>R: filter facts (<=4, JSON) + R-->>H: surviving facts + alt no facts + H->>H: dense_passage_retrieval -> ranking + else facts found + H->>H: phrase_weights = fact score / #chunks per entity + H->>H: passage_weights = DPR score * 0.05 + H->>G: personalized_pagerank(reset=phrase+passage, damping=0.5) + G-->>H: scores for passage nodes + end + H-->>U: QuerySolution(docs, doc_scores, graph_seeds) +``` + +### 6.4 Parameters that matter +`linking_top_k` (5), `passage_node_weight` (0.05), `damping` (0.5), `retrieval_top_k` (200), `qa_top_k` (5), `synonymy_edge_sim_threshold` (0.8), `synonymy_edge_topk` (2047), `rerank_dspy_file_path`, `embedding_return_as_normalized=True`. + +## 7. Generation / answer synthesis + +`HippoRAG.rag_qa(queries, gold_docs, gold_answers)` = `retrieve()` + `qa()`. + +`qa()` takes the top `qa_top_k` (5) passages, formats each as `Wikipedia Title: \n\n` (the literal prefix is hard-coded and somewhat misleading for non-Wikipedia corpora), appends `Question: … \nThought: `, and renders template `rag_qa_` (only `rag_qa_musique.py` exists; everything else falls back to it). The prompt is a one-shot chain-of-thought reader: system prompt "advanced reading comprehension assistant … start after 'Thought:' … conclude with 'Answer:'". The predicted answer is `response.split('Answer:')[1]`. QA evaluation uses `evaluation/qa_eval.py::QAExactMatch` and `QAF1Score` when `gold_answers` are provided. + +The QA LLM can differ from the extraction LLM (`qa_llm=` / `extraction_llm=` constructor injection). No training is involved anywhere in HippoRAG; the only "learned" component is the DSPy-compiled filter prompt shipped as JSON. + +## 8. LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +**Indexing, per chunk** +* 2 chat completions (NER + triple extraction), run with 8 threads; both cached in SQLite so re-runs are free. +* 1 embedding of the passage; plus embeddings for each *new* entity phrase and each *new* fact string (typically 10-30 strings per chunk). Embedding cost dominates with local 7B encoders (NV-Embed-v2, GritLM-7B), which need a GPU. +* Synonymy KNN is CPU numpy; scales as new_entities x all_entities. + +**Query, per question** +* 1-2 embedding calls (query under two instructions). +* 1 chat completion for `DSPyFilter` (short prompt, ~10 demos + 5 facts). +* 1 PPR over the whole graph (prpack; milliseconds to seconds depending on graph size; the whole fact matrix dot product is also O(#facts x dim)). +* 1 chat completion for QA if `rag_qa` is used. + +So HippoRAG 2 is roughly "2 LLM calls per chunk offline, 1-2 LLM calls per query online", which is why the paper claims indexing is far cheaper than GraphRAG/RAPTOR/LightRAG style summarisation pipelines. No GPU is required if you use OpenAI embeddings (`text-embedding-3-small`) and an API LLM, but the paper results use NV-Embed-v2 (7B, GPU). + +Memory: all three embedding matrices plus the igraph live in RAM at query time. + +## 9. Configuration and extension points + +* **Config object**: `utils/config_utils.py::BaseConfig` dataclass (~70 fields). Constructor kwargs of `HippoRAG(...)` (`llm_model_name`, `llm_base_url`, `embedding_model_name`, `embedding_base_url`, Azure fields, `embedding_provider`, `llm_api_key_env`, `embedding_api_key_env`, `index_identity`) override the config; MCP accepts `--config KEY=VALUE`. +* **Swap LLM**: `llm/__init__.py::_get_llm_class()` routes by model name prefix: gateway prefixes (`orcarouter/`, `atlascloud/` in `llm/gateways.py`), `bedrock-mantle/` (`BedrockMantleLLM`), `bedrock/` (LiteLLM `BedrockLLM`), `Transformers/` (`TransformersLLM`), else `CacheOpenAI` (OpenAI, Azure, vLLM, any OpenAI-compatible base URL). Or inject any `BaseLLM` subclass via `extraction_llm=` / `qa_llm=`. +* **Swap embeddings**: name-based routing or `embedding_provider` (`openai|transformers|vllm|gritlm|nvembed|contriever|cohere`), or inject `embedding_model=BaseEmbeddingModel`. +* **Swap storage**: `vector_store_type`; graph is igraph only. +* **Prompts**: `prompts/prompt_template_manager.py::PromptTemplateManager` loads every module in `prompts/templates/` exposing a `prompt_template` list; add a file to add a template (see `templates/README.md`). Filter prompt via `rerank_dspy_file_path`. +* **Chunking**: inject `text_preprocessor=`. +* **Incremental update**: `index()` can be called repeatedly; chunk hashes, OpenIE results and embeddings are reused, synonymy KNN only runs for new entities, `add_new_edges` merges weights. `delete(docs)` removes chunks, decrements `fact_source_counts`, drops facts/entities that no longer have any source, and deletes vertices — all guarded by `StateConsistencyError` checks (missing provenance, legacy schema). `force_index_from_scratch` rebuilds the graph from stored embeddings/OpenIE; `force_openie_from_scratch` is only allowed in an empty index. +* **Serving**: `hipporag-mcp` (stdio or Streamable HTTP, `--read_only`), Claude Code plugin under `plugins/hipporag/`. + +## 10. Benchmarks reported by the authors + +The repository itself contains no result tables; numbers below are from the HippoRAG 2 paper (ICML 2025) as summarised in the README figure and from recollection of the paper — treat exact decimals as "verify against the paper". + +* **Setup**: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct as LLM, NV-Embed-v2 as retriever, datasets grouped as *factual memory* (NaturalQuestions, PopQA), *sense-making* (NarrativeQA), *associativity* (MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, HotpotQA, LV-Eval). 1,000-question samples; QA F1 and passage recall@5. +* **Headline claim**: HippoRAG 2 beats NV-Embed-v2 dense retrieval, GraphRAG, LightRAG, RAPTOR and HippoRAG 1 on average, with the largest gains on multi-hop sets (roughly +7 F1 average over the strongest dense baseline on associativity tasks) while *not* regressing on simple factual QA where HippoRAG 1 and other graph methods did regress. Reported average F1 across the seven sets is about 60 for HippoRAG 2 vs mid-50s for NV-Embed-v2; LightRAG and GraphRAG were below dense retrieval on most QA sets in their runs. +* **Efficiency claim**: offline indexing ~2 LLM calls per passage vs. community-summarisation pipelines; online cost comparable to dense retrieval plus one small filter call. +* Repo-side evaluation tooling: `main.py --dataset {sample,musique,2wikimultihopqa,hotpotqa,...}` under `reproduce/dataset`, HF dataset `osunlp/HippoRAG_2`; metrics via `evaluation/retrieval_eval.py` and `evaluation/qa_eval.py`. +* **Third-party**: Graph-R1's paper (LHRLAB) uses HippoRAG2 as a baseline and reports it as the strongest non-RL GraphRAG baseline on its six QA sets; LightRAG/GraphRAG-bench style comparisons generally reproduce HippoRAG 2 as competitive on multi-hop QA but note its reliance on a strong instruction-tuned embedding model. (Not read from this repo; flagged as external.) + +## 11. Strengths + +* Very low indexing cost for a graph method (two short extraction prompts per chunk, no community summarisation, no entity description merging). +* Retrieval is deterministic and cheap: one embedding, one small LLM filter, one PPR; latency is sub-second on mid-sized corpora once objects are loaded. +* Principled multi-hop behaviour through PPR over fact/passage/synonym edges, with dense retrieval as a floor (`passage_node_weight`) and as a fallback. +* Genuinely incremental and deletable index with provenance counts, manifests and consistency checks — unusual among research GraphRAG codebases. +* Broad provider support (OpenAI, Azure, Bedrock, Bedrock Mantle, gateways, vLLM, Transformers; OpenAI/Cohere/NV-Embed/GritLM/Contriever embeddings) and four vector stores. +* MCP server and Claude Code plugin make it directly usable as an agent memory tool. +* Tests exist and encode real regressions. + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +* **No chunker**: default preprocessor treats each document as one passage; long documents must be chunked by the caller. +* **Full in-memory scoring**: fact/passage/entity matrices are loaded into numpy and scored by dense dot product; the vector DB backends are only persistence. Memory and per-query cost grow linearly with corpus size. +* **Graph stored as a single pickle**; no concurrent writers; MCP serialises tool calls on one worker thread. +* **Predicates are dropped from the graph** — edges carry only counts/weights; relation semantics live only in fact embeddings. Queries that hinge on relation type rely on the fact-embedding stage. +* `linking_top_k=5` and "up to 4 facts" filter is aggressive; recall for questions with many relevant facts depends on the DSPy filter being right. Filter exceptions silently fall back to DPR. +* Entity nodes come only from triples; NER output is otherwise unused. +* QA prompt hard-codes `Wikipedia Title:` prefix and is tuned for MuSiQue-style short answers; no long-form or summarisation ("global") mode. +* Alpha versioning: `2.0.0a5` changed on-disk identity rules (`index_manifest.json`) — older indexes must be rebuilt. +* Heavy pinned dependencies (`torch==2.5.1`, `transformers==4.45.2`, `litellm==1.73.1`) make it awkward to co-install with other stacks. +* The headline results depend on a 7B instruction-tuned embedder (NV-Embed-v2); with `text-embedding-3-small` expect lower numbers (not quantified in repo). + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +Choose HippoRAG 2 when you need **multi-hop retrieval over a growing factual corpus** (docs, wikis, tickets, agent memory), want graph-level associativity *without* paying for GraphRAG-style summarisation, and can afford a decent embedding model. It is a good fit for an "agent long-term memory" component (MCP server, incremental `index`/`delete`). It is a poor fit for corpus-wide summarisation / thematic questions (no community or global mode), for very large corpora that cannot be held in RAM, or where relation semantics must be queried explicitly. + +## 14. Core idea in one paragraph + +HyperGraphRAG keeps LightRAG's whole pipeline (token chunking, one LLM extraction prompt with "gleaning", description merging, NetworkX + nano-vectordb storage, keyword-driven dual-level retrieval, CSV-table context, a single "rag_response" generation prompt) but changes the **unit of knowledge**: instead of extracting binary `(entity, relation, entity)` triples, the LLM is asked to split each chunk into *knowledge segments* — complete natural-language sentences ("hyper-relations") with a 0-10 completeness score — and then list the entities participating in each segment with a 0-100 importance score. Each segment becomes a **hyperedge node** (`role="hyperedge"`, name prefixed ``), each participant an **entity node** (`role="entity"`), and the hypergraph is stored as a **bipartite graph** hyperedge-node <-> entity-node in NetworkX. Retrieval runs the *same extraction prompt on the query* to get entity names (low-level keywords) and hyper-relation sentences (high-level keywords), vector-matches them against the entity and hyperedge vector stores, expands one hop across the bipartite graph, collects source chunks, and feeds entity/hyperedge/chunk tables to the LLM. The claim is that n-ary facts preserve complete context (e.g. a clinical guideline sentence with 4 participants) that binary triples fragment. + +## 3. Indexing pipeline, step by step + +Entry: `HyperGraphRAG.insert(string_or_strings)` -> `ainsert()` in `hypergraphrag/hypergraphrag.py` (lines ~270-340). Everything is `asyncio` with `limit_async_func_call` concurrency caps. + +### 3.1 Document and chunk dedup (LightRAG-inherited) +* Each document -> `doc-`; skipped if already in `full_docs` KV. +* `operate.py::chunking_by_token_size(content, overlap_token_size=100, max_token_size=1200, tiktoken_model="gpt-4o-mini")` — sliding tiktoken windows; chunk id `chunk-` with `{tokens, content, chunk_order_index, full_doc_id}`. Chunks already in `text_chunks` KV are skipped. +* `chunks_vdb.upsert(inserting_chunks)` embeds every chunk (namespace `chunks`), although the hybrid query path never reads `chunks_vdb` (it is only used by LightRAG's `naive` mode, which is no longer wired into `aquery`). + +### 3.2 Extraction: one prompt per chunk + gleaning (LightRAG mechanics, new schema) +`operate.py::extract_entities(chunks, knowledge_graph_inst, entity_vdb, hyperedge_vdb, global_config)`: + +1. Builds `PROMPTS["entity_extraction"]` (`hypergraphrag/prompt.py`) with delimiters `tuple_delimiter="<|>"`, `record_delimiter="##"`, `completion_delimiter="<|COMPLETE|>"`, language (`addon_params.language`, default English) and three long few-shot examples (`PROMPTS["entity_extraction_examples"]`, adapted from LightRAG's "Alex/Taylor/Jordan" and "Operation: Dulce" passages). The `entity_types` list (`DEFAULT_ENTITY_TYPES = organization, person, geo, event, category`) is computed but **commented out of the prompt context**, so the prompt text never mentions them; the model picks its own types (examples use `person`, `object`, `concept`, `role`, `location`, `event`, `action`). +2. Prompt steps: (1) "Divide the text into several complete knowledge segments … Format each as `("hyper-relation"<|><|>)`"; (2) "Identify all entities in each knowledge segment … `("entity"<|><|><|><|>)`"; (3) list everything separated by `##`; (4) end with `<|COMPLETE|>`. +3. **Gleaning loop** (`entity_extract_max_gleaning=2`): after the first completion, send `PROMPTS["entiti_continue_extraction"]` ("MANY knowdge fragements with entities were missed…") with the chat history, append output; then ask `PROMPTS["entiti_if_loop_extraction"]` ("Answer YES | NO …") and stop unless the reply is `yes`. Worst case 1 + 2x2 = 5 LLM calls per chunk; typical 3. +4. Parsing: records are split on `##`/`<|COMPLETE|>`, the parenthesised body split on `<|>`. `_handle_single_hyperrelation_extraction` turns a `"hyper-relation"` record into `{hyper_relation: ""+segment, weight: completeness (default 1.0), source_id: chunk}` and sets `now_hyper_relation`; each subsequent `"entity"` record (`_handle_single_entity_extraction`) is attached to that current hyper-relation with `weight = key_score` (default 50.0), `entity_name = clean_str(name).upper()`, `entity_type`, `description`. **Membership is purely positional**: an entity belongs to the most recent hyper-relation line above it. Entities emitted before any hyper-relation line are dropped (`now_hyper_relation == ""`). + +Concrete shape of one chunk's LLM output (delimiters as in the prompt; types are free-form): + +``` +("hyper-relation"<|>"Radio City is India's first private FM radio station and was started on 3 July 2001."<|>9)## +("entity"<|>"Radio City"<|>"organization"<|>"India's first private FM radio station."<|>95)## +("entity"<|>"India"<|>"geo"<|>"Country where Radio City operates."<|>80)## +("entity"<|>"3 July 2001"<|>"event"<|>"Launch date of Radio City."<|>70)## +("hyper-relation"<|>"It plays Hindi, English and regional songs."<|>7)## +("entity"<|>"Radio City"<|>"organization"<|>"Plays Hindi, English and regional songs."<|>90)## +<|COMPLETE|> +``` +This yields two hyperedge nodes (3 and 1 member entities), three entity nodes, and four incidence edges; the second description of `RADIO CITY` is appended to the first with ``. + +### 3.3 Merge and upsert (three passes) +* `_merge_hyperedges_then_upsert(hyperedge_name, …)` — graph node keyed by the full `sentence` string; attributes `role="hyperedge"`, `weight = sum(completeness scores)` (accumulates across re-extractions), `source_id` = ``-joined chunk ids. No LLM call. +* `_merge_nodes_then_upsert(entity_name, …)` — graph node keyed by upper-cased entity string; `role="entity"`, majority `entity_type`, `description` = ``-joined distinct descriptions, `source_id` union. If the joined description exceeds `entity_summary_to_max_tokens=500` tokens, `_handle_entity_relation_summary` calls the LLM with `PROMPTS["summarize_entity_descriptions"]` (LightRAG). The hyper-relation *weights* carried on entity records are not stored on the entity node. +* `_merge_edges_then_upsert(entity_name, …)` — for each `(hyper_relation, entity)` pair, upserts a bipartite edge `hyper_relation -> entity_name` with `weight = sum(key_score)` and `source_id`. Edge weights accumulate on repeated insertion of the same chunk content only if chunk dedup is bypassed; normally each pair is seen once. + +### 3.4 Vector stores +* `hyperedges_vdb` (namespace `hyperedges`, id `rel-`, `content = hyperedge_name` i.e. the ``-prefixed sentence, meta `hyperedge_name`). +* `entities_vdb` (namespace `entities`, id `ent-`, `content = entity_name + description`, meta `entity_name`). +* Embedding function default `llm.py::openai_embedding` (`text-embedding-3-small`, 1536-d) wrapped by `limit_async_func_call(embedding_func_max_async=16)`, batched by `embedding_batch_num=32`. Stored by `NanoVectorDBStorage` (`storage.py`) in `vdb_.json` under `working_dir`. + +### 3.5 Persistence +`_insert_done()` calls `index_done_callback()` on every storage: `JsonKVStorage` writes `kv_store_full_docs.json`, `kv_store_text_chunks.json`, `kv_store_llm_response_cache.json`; `NetworkXStorage` writes `graph_chunk_entity_relation.graphml`; nano-vectordb saves its JSON. + +On-disk layout of a `working_dir` after one insert (default backends): + +| File | Written by | Content | +|---|---|---| +| `kv_store_full_docs.json` | `JsonKVStorage` | `doc-: {content}` | +| `kv_store_text_chunks.json` | `JsonKVStorage` | `chunk-: {tokens, content, chunk_order_index, full_doc_id}` | +| `kv_store_llm_response_cache.json` | `JsonKVStorage` | prompt-hash -> LLM response (extraction, gleaning, summaries, answers) | +| `graph_chunk_entity_relation.graphml` | `NetworkXStorage` | bipartite hypergraph with `role` on nodes | +| `vdb_entities.json` | `NanoVectorDBStorage` | `ent-` vectors + `entity_name` | +| `vdb_hyperedges.json` | `NanoVectorDBStorage` | `rel-` vectors + `hyperedge_name` | +| `vdb_chunks.json` | `NanoVectorDBStorage` | `chunk-` vectors (never queried by `hybrid`) | +| `hypergraphrag.log` (cwd) | `set_logger` | run log | + +### 3.6 Flowchart + +```mermaid +flowchart TD + A[insert docs] --> B[doc-md5 dedup via full_docs KV] + B --> C[chunking_by_token_size 1200/100 tiktoken] + C --> D[chunks_vdb.upsert embed chunks] + C --> E[extract_entities per chunk

continue + YES/NO check} + F --> G[parse records on ## and <|>

LLM summary if >500 tokens] + G --> J[_merge_edges_then_upsert

Graph data model + +Single NetworkX undirected graph (`NetworkXStorage`, namespace `chunk_entity_relation`) holding two node roles — the hypergraph is encoded as its **bipartite incidence graph**. + +| Node type | Node id | Attributes | +|---|---|---| +| Hyperedge node | `"" + knowledge segment text` | `role="hyperedge"`, `weight` (sum of completeness scores, 0-10 each), `source_id` (chunk ids joined by ``) | +| Entity node | upper-cased, `clean_str`'d entity name (the raw string, not a hash) | `role="entity"`, `entity_type`, `description` (``-joined, LLM-summarised past 500 tokens), `source_id` | + +| Edge | Endpoints | Attributes | +|---|---|---| +| Incidence edge | hyperedge node — entity node | `weight` (entity key_score, 0-100, summed), `source_id` | + +There are **no entity-entity edges** and no typed relations; the "relation" is the free-text sentence itself. Arity is unbounded (an entity list under one hyper-relation line). Entities are keyed by exact normalised string, so no entity resolution beyond upper-casing is performed. Because hyperedge node ids are whole sentences, two near-identical segments produce two hyperedges. + +Vector-side records: `ent-` and `rel-` in nano-vectordb, `chunk-` in `chunks_vdb` (unused in query), text chunks in KV. + +## 5. Storage backends supported + +Inherited verbatim from LightRAG (`hypergraphrag/kg/*`), selected by string name in `HyperGraphRAG(kv_storage=…, vector_storage=…, graph_storage=…)` via `_get_storage_class()`: + +| Role | Implementations | Default | +|---|---|---| +| KV (docs, chunks, LLM cache) | `JsonKVStorage`, `OracleKVStorage`, `MongoKVStorage`, `TiDBKVStorage` | `JsonKVStorage` (one JSON file per namespace) | +| Vector (entities, hyperedges, chunks) | `NanoVectorDBStorage`, `OracleVectorDBStorage`, `MilvusVectorDBStorge` (sic), `ChromaVectorDBStorage`, `TiDBVectorDBStorage` | `NanoVectorDBStorage` (`nano-vectordb`, brute-force cosine, `cosine_better_than_threshold=0.2`) | +| Graph | `NetworkXStorage`, `Neo4JStorage`, `OracleGraphStorage` | `NetworkXStorage` (GraphML file) | + +Caveats seen in code: `NanoVectorDBStorage.delete_relation()` filters records by `src_id`/`tgt_id` fields that hyperedge records do not have (they have `content`/`hyperedge_name`), so `delete_by_entity()` will not remove hyperedge vectors — a LightRAG leftover. `node2vec` embedding hooks exist on `NetworkXStorage` but `base.py` raises `NotImplementedError("Node embedding is not used in hypergraphrag.")`. The non-default backends were not adapted for the `role` attribute and were not exercised by the authors (no examples/tests). + +## 6. Query / retrieval modes + +Entry: `HyperGraphRAG.query(query, QueryParam)` -> `aquery()` -> `operate.py::kg_query()`. Only `mode="hybrid"` is dispatched in `aquery` (LightRAG's `local`, `global`, `naive` branches were removed; `QueryParam.mode` still lists them and `_build_query_context` still contains the branching, but `aquery` never calls `kg_query` for anything but `hybrid`, so non-hybrid modes silently return `None`). The `evaluation/` copy relaxes this to `["hybrid","global","local"]`. + +### 6.1 Steps in `kg_query` +1. **Cache check** via `handle_cache(hashing_kv, args_hash, query, mode)` (LightRAG; optional embedding-similarity cache governed by `embedding_cache_config`, off by default). +2. **Query decomposition with the extraction prompt** — the very same `PROMPTS["entity_extraction"]` is applied to the *question* text (1 LLM call, no gleaning). Parsed `"hyper-relation"` records become **high-level keywords** (`"" + segment`), `"entity"` records become **low-level keywords** (upper-cased names). If either list is empty the function returns `PROMPTS["fail_response"]` ("Sorry, I'm not able to provide an answer…"). Note this replaces LightRAG's `keywords_extraction` JSON prompt; that prompt is still present in `prompt.py` but unused. +3. **Context building** `_build_query_context([ll_keywords, hl_keywords], …)`: + * **Entity side** `_get_node_data(ll_keywords, …)`: `entities_vdb.query(ll_keywords_joined, top_k=QueryParam.top_k=60)` (one embedding of the comma-joined names), fetch node data + `node_degree` as `rank`; `_find_most_related_text_unit_from_entities` collects chunks from the entities' `source_id`s, boosting chunks also referenced by one-hop neighbour nodes (`relation_counts`), ordered by (entity rank order, -relation_counts), truncated to `max_token_for_text_unit=4000` tokens; `_find_most_related_edges_from_entities` gathers all incident edges, sorts by `(edge_degree, weight)` desc, truncates by `max_token_for_global_context=4000` on the hyperedge text, and for each hyperedge lists all its member entities (`related_nodes = "A|B|C"`). + * **Hyperedge side** `_get_edge_data(hl_keywords, …)`: `hyperedges_vdb.query(hl_keywords_joined, top_k=60)`; fetch hyperedge nodes; `rank = vector distance`; sort by `(distance, weight)`; truncate by hyperedge text length to 4000 tokens; attach member entities; `_find_most_related_entities_from_relationships` pulls those entities (truncated by `max_token_for_local_context=4000` on descriptions); `_find_related_text_unit_from_relationships` pulls source chunks (4000 tokens). + * `combine_contexts` dedups and merges both sides into three CSV tables: `Entities (id, entity, type, description)`, `Relationships (id, hyperedge, related_entities)`, `Sources (id, content)`. +4. `only_need_context=True` returns the CSV context string (used by the evaluation scripts); `only_need_prompt=True` returns the filled system prompt. +5. **Generation** (section 7) and `save_to_cache`. + +### 6.2 Sequence diagram + +```mermaid +sequenceDiagram + participant U as Caller + participant Q as kg_query + participant L as LLM + participant EV as entities_vdb + participant HV as hyperedges_vdb + participant G as NetworkX bipartite graph + participant KV as text_chunks KV + U->>Q: query(text, mode=hybrid) + Q->>L: entity_extraction prompt on the question + L-->>Q: hyper-relation lines (hl) + entity lines (ll) + par low level + Q->>EV: query(ll joined, top_k=60) + EV-->>Q: entity names + Q->>G: get_node, node_degree, get_node_edges + Q->>KV: chunks from entity source_ids + and high level + Q->>HV: query(hl joined, top_k=60) + HV-->>Q: hyperedge names + Q->>G: get_node, get_node_edges -> member entities + Q->>KV: chunks from hyperedge source_ids + end + Q->>Q: truncate each table to 4000 tokens, combine_contexts + Q->>L: rag_response system prompt + query + L-->>U: markdown answer +``` + +### 6.3 Ranking and budgets +* Vector similarity decides the candidate set; graph degree and accumulated weights decide ordering inside the candidate set. There is no PageRank or multi-hop traversal beyond one hop across the bipartite graph (entity -> its hyperedges -> their entities). +* Token budgets (tiktoken, `gpt-4o-mini` encoder): 4000 each for entities, hyperedges, chunks on *each* of the two sides before combination, so the final prompt can reach ~20k+ tokens. +* `top_k=60` on both vector queries. `cosine_better_than_threshold=0.2` filters weak matches. + +## 7. Generation / answer synthesis + +`PROMPTS["rag_response"]` (LightRAG's, unchanged): "You are a helpful assistant responding to questions about data in the tables provided … Generate a response of the target length and format … incorporating any relevant general knowledge. If you don't know the answer, just say so … Style the response in markdown." `response_type` default `"Multiple Paragraphs"`. The LLM call is `llm_model_func(query, system_prompt=sys_prompt, stream=…)`; the response is post-processed by stripping the prompt text if it was echoed (an `hf_model` artefact). A commented-out alternative prompt tuned for "semantic alignment with expected answers" is left in `prompt.py`, suggesting the paper's evaluation used stricter wording in the `evaluation/` copy (not verified here). + +The evaluation harness (`evaluation/script_hypergraphrag.py`) retrieves context only (`QueryParam(only_need_context=True)`) and `evaluation/get_generation.py` generates with `gpt-4o-mini` using its own prompt, so paper generation quality is decoupled from the library's `rag_response` prompt. + +No training anywhere. + +## 8. LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +| Phase | LLM calls | Embedding calls | +|---|---|---| +| Index, per 1200-token chunk | 1 extraction + up to 2 gleaning + up to 1 YES/NO check = 3 typical, 5 max; plus occasional `summarize_entity_descriptions` when an entity's merged description exceeds 500 tokens | 1 chunk embedding + 1 per new hyperedge + 1 per new/updated entity (dozens per chunk; every hyperedge sentence is embedded) | +| Query | 1 (extraction prompt on question) + 1 (answer) | 2 (entity keywords string, hyperedge keywords string) | + +Defaults: `gpt_4o_mini_complete` and `openai_embedding` (`text-embedding-3-small`); `llm_model_max_async=16`, `embedding_func_max_async=16`; LLM cache (`enable_llm_cache=True`) keyed by prompt hash in `kv_store_llm_response_cache.json`. The extraction prompt is long (three multi-hundred-token examples) so input tokens per chunk are ~4-5k on top of the chunk. Compared with LightRAG the per-chunk cost is similar; compared with HippoRAG it is noticeably higher (more and longer calls, many more embedded strings). No GPU needed with API models; `hf_model_complete`/`hf_embedding`/`ollama_*`/`lmdeploy` paths exist for local models. + +## 9. Configuration and extension points + +* All settings are fields of the `HyperGraphRAG` dataclass (`working_dir`, `chunk_token_size=1200`, `chunk_overlap_token_size=100`, `tiktoken_model_name`, `entity_extract_max_gleaning=2`, `entity_summary_to_max_tokens=500`, `embedding_func`, `embedding_batch_num`, `embedding_func_max_async`, `llm_model_func`, `llm_model_name` (only used by HF path), `llm_model_max_token_size=32768`, `llm_model_max_async`, `llm_model_kwargs`, `enable_llm_cache`, `addon_params` (`language`, `entity_types`, `example_number`), `embedding_cache_config`, `vector_db_storage_cls_kwargs`). +* **Swap LLM**: pass any `async def f(prompt, system_prompt=None, history_messages=[], **kwargs) -> str` as `llm_model_func`; ready-made: `gpt_4o_complete`, `gpt_4o_mini_complete`, `azure_openai_complete`, `bedrock_complete`, `hf_model_complete`, `ollama_model_complete`, `zhipu_complete`, `nvidia_openai_complete`, `lmdeploy_model_if_cache`, plus `MultiModel` round-robin (all in `llm.py`, LightRAG). +* **Swap embeddings**: `embedding_func=EmbeddingFunc(embedding_dim, max_token_size, func)`; providers `openai_embedding`, `azure_openai_embedding`, `bedrock_embedding`, `hf_embedding`, `ollama_embedding`, `jina_embedding`, `zhipu_embedding`, `siliconcloud_embedding`, `nvidia_openai_embedding`. +* **Swap storage**: string names in section 5; `vector_db_storage_cls_kwargs` for backend params; env vars for Neo4j/Oracle/Milvus/Mongo/TiDB as in LightRAG. +* **Prompts**: edit `PROMPTS` dict in `prompt.py` (module-level, no injection API). +* **Custom KG**: `insert_custom_kg(custom_kg)` (LightRAG) still exists but expects binary `relationships` with `src_id/tgt_id`, not hyperedges — unclear whether it produces a consistent hypergraph; treat as unsupported. +* **Incremental update**: `insert()` is append-only and idempotent at doc/chunk hash level; new chunks' entities merge into existing nodes (description concatenation + summarisation), hyperedges with identical text merge weights. `delete_by_entity(name)` removes an entity node and its vector (and, buggy, attempts to remove hyperedge vectors); there is no document-level delete and no removal of orphaned hyperedge nodes. Changing the chunk size or prompt after indexing silently mixes schemas. + +## 10. Benchmarks reported by the authors + +From `evaluation/README.md` and the paper (numbers not stored in the repo): + +* **Domains / datasets**: five corpora built by the authors — `hypertension` (medicine: clinical guideline text), `agriculture`, `cs`, `legal`, and `mix`; contexts and question sets are distributed via Terabox, not in the repo. Questions are LLM-generated QA pairs with gold answers. +* **Baselines**: NaiveGeneration (no retrieval), StandardRAG (chunk dense retrieval), GraphRAG, LightRAG, PathRAG, HippoRAG2 (listed in the paper; only `script_standardrag.py` and `script_naivegeneration.py` are in the repo). +* **Metrics** (`evaluation/get_score.py`, `eval_r.py`, `eval_g.py`): answer F1 (`cal_f1`), **R-Sim** (SimCSE `princeton-nlp/sup-simcse-roberta-large` cosine between retrieved knowledge and gold answer), and a **G-E generation score** = average of an LLM-judge 0-100 rating over seven rubrics (`comprehensiveness, knowledgeability, correctness, relevance, diversity, logical_coherence, factuality`) blended with F1 (`(score + f1)/2`). Judge is `gpt-4o-mini` via the apiyi proxy. +* **Headline**: the paper reports HyperGraphRAG as best on average across the five domains on F1, R-Sim and the generation score, with the largest margins over LightRAG/GraphRAG in medicine and legal (multi-entity guideline sentences), and shows that retrieval cost per query is in the same range as LightRAG hybrid mode. Exact table values are in the NeurIPS paper; the repo stores none, and the figure `figs/F1.png` referenced by the README is not in this clone. +* **Third-party**: Graph-R1 (same group) reuses this exact extraction schema and reports HyperGraphRAG-style retrieval as a strong non-RL baseline. Independent reproductions were not found in the repo. Strengths + +* **n-ary knowledge units**: a whole sentence with all participants is retrievable as one object, so multi-entity constraints (dose + population + condition + outcome) are not broken into lossy binary triples. +* Dual retrieval channel: entity-side (specific names) and hyperedge-side (whole propositions) are matched independently and combined, similar to LightRAG local+global but with semantically richer "global" units. +* Reuses LightRAG's mature plumbing: async batching, LLM cache, pluggable KV/vector/graph backends, multilingual `addon_params.language`. +* Simple on-disk artefacts (JSON + GraphML) that are easy to inspect and post-process; `kv_store_hyperedges.json` is directly reusable (Graph-R1 does exactly that). +* Query-time cost is bounded (2 LLM calls, 2 embeddings, one-hop graph lookups). + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +* **Positional membership parsing**: hyperedge membership depends on the LLM listing entities immediately after each hyper-relation line; any reordering silently reassigns entities. No JSON/structured output. +* Hyperedge node ids are the raw sentence string — no dedup/merging of paraphrases, so the hyperedge store grows ~linearly with chunk count and vector search over it dominates query cost at scale (`nano-vectordb` is brute force). +* No entity resolution beyond upper-casing; descriptions grow by concatenation then get LLM-summarised (lossy, extra cost). +* The query-time "keyword" extraction uses the full document-extraction prompt (with three long examples) on a one-line question; it returns `fail_response` if the model produces no hyper-relation or no entity for the question — brittle for short factoid queries. +* Only `hybrid` mode is reachable from `aquery()`; `local`/`global`/`naive` are dead code in the main package (differs in the `evaluation/` copy). +* `delete_by_entity` cannot delete hyperedge vectors (field mismatch), no document-level deletion, no index manifest; incremental re-chunking is unsafe. +* Context can reach ~24k tokens (six 4000-token budgets); no reranking of chunks beyond order/degree heuristics. +* Inherited LightRAG code paths (`insert_custom_kg`, node2vec, non-default DBs) are untested with the `role`-based schema; `chunks_vdb` embeddings are computed but never queried. +* Evaluation harness hard-codes a paid third-party API proxy and Terabox downloads; the `evaluation/hypergraphrag` copy diverges from the main package, so paper numbers may not match the library defaults. +* No tests, no packaging, squashed history, typos in prompt keys (`entiti_continue_extraction`, `MilvusVectorDBStorge`). + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +Choose HyperGraphRAG when your corpus is dominated by **dense, multi-participant factual statements** — clinical guidelines, regulations, contracts, technical specs — where you want the retrieved unit to be the full proposition and you are already comfortable with a LightRAG-style stack (OpenAI models, JSON/GraphML files, modest corpus size). It is also the right starting point if you plan to build Graph-R1-style agentic retrieval over a hypergraph. Avoid it for large corpora (brute-force vector search over every extracted sentence), for workloads that need deletion/updates, or for production use without first adding structured-output parsing and tests. + +## 14. Core idea in one paragraph + +KAG treats RAG as "knowledge base + logical reasoning", not vector search. At build time it runs a configurable **builder chain** (scanner → reader → splitter → one or more extractors → vectorizer → post-processor → writer) that turns documents into `SubGraph`s conforming to an **SPG schema** (typed entities, events, concepts with properties and indexed fields), always attaching a `Chunk` node and `source` edges so graph and text are **mutually indexed**. Extraction can be schema-free (LLM NER/standardisation/triples into a generic ontology), schema-constrained (NER, relations and events restricted to your domain schema), or one of several lighter "index" extractors (chunk-only, summary, outline, atomic query, knowledge unit, table). Everything is written to the OpenSPG server (Neo4j + its own vector/text index) or, for benchmarks, to an in-memory igraph/torch graph. At query time a **planner** LLM turns the question into a DAG of tasks expressed either as executor calls or as a **logical form** (`Retrieval(s=..., p=..., o=...)`, `Math(...)`, `Deduce(...)`, `Output(...)`); the hybrid retrieval executor resolves each `Retrieval` step through a flow of components — exact graph lookup (`kg_cs`), fuzzy graph + Personalised-PageRank chunk retrieval (`kg_fr`), vector chunk retrieval (`rc`), plus summary/outline/atomic-query/table retrievers — merges and summarises them, while Math (LLM-generated Python) and Deduce (judgement/entailment/extract/choice prompts) executors handle computation and inference; a generator produces a thought-then-answer with `` citations. Static mode plans once (with optional retry if the answer is "unknown"); iterative mode re-plans after each step; `kag_model_planner` targets the fine-tuned KAG-Thinker model. + +## 3. Graph / tree data model + +- **Schema (SPG)**: declared per project in a `.schema` DSL file (`kag/templates/schema/{{default}}.schema.tmpl`, `kag/examples/*/schema/*.schema`) and committed with `knext schema commit`. Each property declares a type (`Text`, `Integer`, another entity type for relations-as-properties) and optionally `index: Text | Vector | TextAndVector` and `constraint: MultiValue`. The default template ships 17 generic entity types (`Person`, `Organization`, `GeographicLocation`, `Works`, `Event`, `Medicine`, `Keyword`, `Others`, ...) each with `desc` (TextAndVector), `semanticType → SemanticConcept`, `synonyms`, `officialName`. +- **SubGraph** (`kag/interface/common/model/sub_graph.py`): `Node(id, name, label, properties)` and `Edge(from_id, from_type, to_id, to_type, label, properties)`; `to_dict()` is what the writer sends. Generation / answer synthesis + +- Generators: `llm_generator`, `llm_index_generator` (adds `chunk_reranker`), `kag_model_generator`, `mock_generator`. +- Prompts (`kag/solver/prompt/`): `default_multi_hop_generator` ("Thought: ... Answer: ..." over documents + step-by-step breakdown), `default_refer_generator_prompt` (answer with citations ``, ids must exist in the reference list), `default_without_reference_generator`, `default_thought_then_answer` (per-sub-question summary), `context_select_prompt`, `resp_generator`/`resp_reflector`/`resp_verifier`/`resp_judge` (older reflect-verify loop, now mostly unused by default configs), `solve_question*`, `summary_question`, `sub_question_summary`, `question_ner`. +- Reasoning loops: (1) planner-level – static re-plan when `finish_judger` says the answer is invalid (`max_iteration`); iterative pipeline re-plans each step; (2) executor-level – `Deduce` ops and `Math` code with error-feedback retries; `fuzzy_one_hop_select` uses an LLM to pick relations. Thought traces are emitted in `` (KAG-Thinker) or "Thought:" sections. +- Citations: yes, chunk-level ids in the reference prompt, resolved by the product UI to original documents ("linking generated content to original references" in 0.7 notes). The multi-hop benchmark prompt does not emit citations. +- Bilingual prompts (`template_zh`/`template_en`) selected by `project.language`; `biz_scene` (`default`, `medical`, ...) selects domain prompt variants via `init_prompt_with_fallback`. + +## 8. LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +**Indexing, per chunk** (default 500-token chunks): +- `schema_free_extractor`: 3 LLM calls (NER, triples, standardisation; the async path runs triples and std in parallel) + table-chunk calls. `schema_constraint_extractor`: 4 (NER, events, relations, std). `knowledge_unit_extractor`: 3 (NER, knowledge units, triples) with the KU prompt producing large structured JSON. `naive_rag_extractor`/`chunk_extractor`: 0 LLM calls (vectors only) – the "lightweight build". `summary_extractor`, `atomic_query_extractor`, `outline_extractor`: +1 each if stacked. `outline_splitter`/`semantic_splitter` add per-document LLM calls. +- Embedding: one vector per `Vector`/`TextAndVector` property per node (name always; `desc`, `content`), batched 32 at a time; entity linking in the post-processor issues a vector search per node. +- Examples use `qwen2.5-72b-instruct` for extraction and a 7B `ner_llm` for fuzzy path selection; `BAAI/bge-m3` (1024-d) embeddings. + +**Query** (static LF pipeline with hybrid executor, typical 2–3 hop question): +- 1 planning call (+1 per re-plan); per Retrieval task: 1 rewrite call (if it references parents), `fuzzy_one_hop_select` LLM call(s) in `kg_fr`, 1 `context_select` call (if `with_llm_select`), 1 `thought_then_answer` summary (if `enable_summary`); per Math task 1–3 code-generation calls; per Deduce task 1 call; 1 final generation call; optional `finish_judger` call. Expect roughly **6–15 LLM calls** for a 3-step plan. Iterative pipeline: +1 planning call per step. +- Embedding calls: question + each sub/rewritten query (linking, `rc`, rerank). +- Graph ops: entity-linking vector searches, one-hop expansions and a PPR per Retrieval step – server-side on OpenSPG/Neo4j; igraph in memory mode. + +## 9. Configuration and extension points + +- **Everything is a registry** (`kag/common/registry/registrable.py::Registrable`): components declare `@X.register("name")` and are built from YAML/HOCON via `from_config({"type": ...})`. Project config `kag_config.yaml` (sections `llm`, `vectorize_model`, `vectorizer`, `project.{namespace, host_addr, id, biz_scene, language, ckpt_dir}`, `log`, `kag_builder_pipeline.{chain, scanner, num_chains, num_threads_per_chain}`, `kag_solver_pipeline.{type, planner, executors, generator, max_iteration}` plus arbitrary YAML anchors such as `kg_cs: &kg_cs`). `!ENV VAR` resolves secrets. `KAG_CONFIG` / `KAGConfigAccessor` give access at runtime; multiple task configs can coexist (`KAG_QA_TASK_CONFIG_KEY`). +- **Swap LLM / embeddings**: change `type` to `openai|maas|vllm|azure_openai|ollama` and `vectorize_model.type`; per-component overrides (`llm`, `ner_llm`, `llm_client`, `vectorize_model`) are supported since every component takes them as constructor args. +- **Swap prompts**: register a `PromptABC` subclass with `template_en/zh`, `template_variables`, `parse_response`, and reference it by `type`; `init_prompt_with_fallback(name, biz_scene)` resolves `example__` → `default_`. +- **Schema**: edit `schema/.schema`, `knext schema commit`; `knext project create/restore/update/list` (`knext/command/sub_command/project.py`). Changing the schema requires re-extraction for affected types. +- **Storage**: `writer.type` (`kg_writer` vs `memory_graph_writer`), `search_api.type` / `graph_api.type` (`openspg_*` vs `memory_*`). +- **Retrieval**: compose `retrievers:` lists and `merger`, or the `flow` string for the legacy executor; `kag/indexer/kag_index_manager.py` auto-builds matching extractor+retriever configs per index type. +- **Incremental update**: chunk-level resumability via checkpoints; the writer is an **upsert** (`AlterOperationEnum.Upsert`) so re-running the builder on new files adds to the existing OpenSPG graph without rebuilding (entities are keyed by name, so the same name merges). Deletion is supported by `KGWriter(delete=True)` / `operation=DELETE` on a subgraph. There is no automatic re-summarisation layer to invalidate (no communities), which makes incremental ingestion simpler than community-based GraphRAGs. The memory-graph path is rebuilt from the checkpoint directory on load. +- **CLI**: `knext` (`project`, `schema`, `builder`, `reasoner`, `thinker`) and `kag` (`builder`, `benchmark`, `info`, `mcp_server`). +- **Templates**: `kag/templates/project` scaffolds `builder/indexer.py`, `solver/`, `schema/`, prompts. + +## 10. Benchmarks reported by the authors + +- Repo (`docs/release_notes.md`, Oct 2024 release): KAG "significantly better than NaiveRAG, HippoRAG": **F1 relatively improved by 19.6 on HotpotQA and 33.5 on 2Wiki**. 0.7 notes: `open_benchmark/` "comparing various RAG methods under the same base to achieve SOTA"; "Lightweight Build" reduces construction token cost by 89%. +- Paper (arXiv:2409.13731; these tables are not reproduced anywhere in the repo, so verify against the current arXiv version before quoting): KAG reports end-to-end EM/F1 in the region of HotpotQA ~62/76, 2WikiMultiHopQA ~69/77, MuSiQue ~36/49, which it presents as several F1 points above HippoRAG+IRCoT and far above NaiveRAG with the same base model, together with retrieval-recall ablations showing the mutual-index and knowledge-alignment components each contribute. Two in-house Ant Group deployments (E-Government and E-Health Q&A) are reported with large "professionalism" gains over NaiveRAG as judged by human/LLM raters. Treat all of these as author-reported. +- Reproduction kits: `kag/open_benchmark/{hotpotqa,2wiki,musique}` (subsets `data/sub_corpus.json`, `qa_sub.json`, configs for `chunk`, `graph`, `summary`, `atomic_query`, `knowledge_unit`, `simple` index variants, `benchmark.sh`, EM/F1 via `kag/common/benchmarks/evaluate.py` and an LLM judger), plus `AffairQA` (government affairs, Chinese) and `prqa`. +- Third-party: GraphRAG-Bench / HippoRAG2 / other 2025 papers report KAG as competitive but expensive to run; results vary widely with the LLM used and are not in this repo. + +## 11. Strengths + +- **Schema-aware, typed knowledge**: real SPG schema with entity/event/concept types, property indexes, constraints, and schema-constrained extraction – suitable for regulated or expert domains where open IE noise is unacceptable. +- **Mutual indexing of graph and text** built into every extractor (Chunk nodes + `source` edges), with retrieval that moves both ways (entity linking → PPR → chunks; chunks → one-hop graph). +- **Logical-form planning** gives explicit, inspectable multi-step plans mixing retrieval, computation (real Python) and deduction; DAG execution runs independent sub-questions in parallel. +- **Multiple index types** (chunk, summary, outline, atomic query, knowledge unit, table, SPO graph) selectable per knowledge base with matching retrievers; lightweight modes exist when you cannot afford full extraction. +- **Production features**: resumable checkpointed builds, upsert/delete writes, product UI with streaming reasoning and citations, MCP server, Ollama/vLLM/Azure support, bilingual prompts, Docker deployment. +- Apache-2.0, versioned releases, active maintenance by a large org. + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +- **Deployment weight**: requires the OpenSPG Java server stack (OpenSPG + Neo4j + MySQL + MinIO via Docker Compose, ~several GB) even for schema loading in the Python toolkit; project/schema lifecycle is managed through `knext` REST calls. No standalone pure-Python mode except the benchmark-oriented `memory_graph` path, which still expects a server for schema. +- **Complexity and churn**: two generations of solver (0.7 `flow` components registered as `*_legacy`, 0.8 `retrievers`+`merger`), many near-duplicate prompts (`solve_question`, `solve_question_without_docs`, `resp_*`), config files with dozens of anchors; the learning curve is steep and docs live mainly on Yuque (partly Chinese). +- **LLM cost**: 3–4 extraction calls per chunk in graph modes; query-time plans trigger many calls (rewrite, fuzzy path select, context select, summaries, generation). Full-graph build of a large corpus is expensive; the authors added lightweight modes for this reason. +- **Vector search tied to OpenSPG/Neo4j**: no Milvus/Qdrant/pgvector; Neo4j vector/text indexes limit scale and multi-tenancy. +- **Entity identity by name**: `SubGraph` node ids are entity names; no global entity resolution beyond standardisation prompts and similarity linking at threshold 0.9. +- **KAG-Thinker weights are not open** in this repo; `kag_model_planner` is only usable with the model served elsewhere. +- **English support is secondary**: prompts have `template_en`, but examples, Yuque docs, logs, and some comments are Chinese-first; `biz_scene` prompt packs exist mainly for Chinese medical/government scenes. +- Error handling often falls back silently (e.g. `finish_judger` returns False on exception, `mock` components) and several code paths print debugging output. +- No community/global-summary layer, so "summarise the whole corpus" questions depend on the `summary`/`outline` indexes rather than hierarchical community reports. + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +- Enterprise, vertical-domain knowledge bases (finance, government, healthcare, telecom – the `examples/` set) where you own a schema, need typed facts, numerical/logical reasoning steps, citations, and can run a server stack. +- Multi-hop factual QA with explicit planning and mixed retrieval/calculation, where exact-match graph lookups (IDs, codes, regulations) matter alongside text retrieval. +- Teams already in the Ant/Alibaba ecosystem (DashScope, ODPS, SLS scanners) or needing Chinese-language strength. +- Not a fit for: lightweight or embedded use, laptops without Docker, quick prototypes, corpora without a meaningful schema, or teams wanting a single-process Python library (compare LightRAG/nano-graphrag). If you only need chunk retrieval with summaries, its lightweight modes work but do not justify the server. + +## 14. The version documented here is far ahead of that snapshot: the monolithic `lightrag.py` was split into mixins (`_RoleLLMMixin`, `_StorageMigrationMixin`, `_PipelineMixin`), the extraction prompt moved to a system/user split with record caps, multimodal parsing (MinerU/Docling/native DOCX) was added, and the query pipeline was rewritten as a four-stage search/truncate/merge/build architecture. + +## 2. Core idea in one paragraph + +LightRAG chunks documents, has an LLM extract `(entity, type, description)` and `(source, target, keywords, description)` records from each chunk, merges those records into a single entity-relation graph (descriptions concatenated and, when they pile up, re-summarised by the LLM), and embeds three things into vector stores: entities, relations and raw chunks. At query time one small LLM call turns the question into *low-level keywords* (specific entities) and *high-level keywords* (themes); low-level keywords are matched against the entity vector index (local), high-level keywords against the relation vector index (global), and in `mix` mode the raw query is also matched against chunks. The graph is then used only one hop out: entities pull their incident edges, edges pull their endpoint nodes, and both pull the chunks recorded in their `source_id` provenance field. Everything is token-budgeted, optionally reranked, serialised to JSON blocks and handed to a single answer-generation LLM call that must cite `[n]` reference ids. + +## 3. Indexing pipeline, step by step + +### 3.1 Ingestion and document status + +- Entry points: `LightRAG.ainsert()` (`lightrag/lightrag.py:2310`) and the REST `/documents/*` routes. Both delegate to the mixin in `lightrag/pipeline.py`: `apipeline_enqueue_documents()` (line 740: hash ids with `compute_mdhash_id(..., prefix="doc-")`, dedupe, write `DocStatus.PENDING` rows) then `apipeline_process_enqueue_documents()` (line 1724), which runs a feeder plus three worker pools: `_parse_worker` → `_analyze_worker` (VLM) → `_process_worker` → `process_single_document()` (line 4991). +- `DocStatus` (`lightrag/base.py:1317`): `PENDING → PARSING → ANALYZING → PROCESSING → PROCESSED | FAILED`. +- Parsing engines (`lightrag/parser/routing.py`): `legacy`, `native` (markdown + DOCX with "smart heading" detection, `parser/docx/`), `mineru`, `docling` (HTTP adapters in `parser/external/`). Build the system prompt from `PROMPTS["entity_extraction_system_prompt"]` (or the `_json_` variant when `entity_extraction_use_json` / `ENTITY_EXTRACTION_USE_JSON=true`).
