Core idea in one paragraph + +fast-graphrag keeps the LLM-built entity/relationship graph but drops communities and community reports entirely. Retrieval is HippoRAG-style: the LLM extracts named and generic entities from the query, those are matched to graph nodes with an HNSW cosine search, the resulting node weights seed a **personalized PageRank** over the whole igraph graph, and PageRank mass is propagated through two sparse matrices (entities -> relationships -> chunks) to rank relationships and source chunks. The answer is generated from a tabular context of top entities, relationships, and chunks. Index cost is one or two LLM calls per chunk plus occasional description/edge-merge calls; there is no per-community summarization, which is where the "6x cheaper than graphrag" claim comes from. The extraction prompt is "promptable" via a user-supplied `domain`, `example_queries`, and `entity_types`. + +## 3. Indexing pipeline, step by step + +Entry: `GraphRAG.insert(content, metadata)` -> `BaseGraphRAG.async_insert` (`fast_graphrag/_graphrag.py`). `GraphRAG` (`fast_graphrag/__init__.py`) wires the default services through a nested `GraphRAG.Config` dataclass. + +1. **Checkpoint/open**: `state_manager.insert_start()` opens all storages inside `Workspace.with_checkpoints` (`_storage/_namespace.py`); with `n_checkpoints > 0` each insert writes to a new timestamped sub-directory and old ones are pruned. +2. **Chunking** (`_services/_chunk_extraction.py::DefaultChunkingService`): regex split on `DEFAULT_SEPARATORS` (paragraph breaks and CJK/Latin sentence punctuation), merged greedily to `chunk_token_size 800` with `chunk_token_overlap 100`, **measured in characters using `TOKEN_TO_CHAR_RATIO = 4`** (`_utils.py`), not a tokenizer. Chunk id = `xxhash.xxh3_64_intdigest(content) // 2`. Input bytes are sanitized. Chunks carry the document `metadata` dict. +3. **Dedup**: `DefaultStateManagerService.filter_new_chunks` masks chunks whose hash already exists in `chunk_storage` (`PickleIndexedKeyValueStorage`). +4. **Information extraction** (`_services/_information_extraction.py::DefaultInformationExtractionService.extract`), one asyncio task per document: + - Per chunk: `format_and_send_prompt("entity_relationship_extraction", response_model=TGraph)`. The system prompt `entity_relationship_extraction_text` (`_prompt.py`) is parameterized by `{domain}`, `{example_queries}`, `{entity_types}` and asks for strictly valid JSON with `entities[{name,type,desc}]`, `relationships[...]`, `other_relationships[...]`; it also instructs the model to connect isolated entities. The pydantic `TGraph.Model` (`_types.py`) upper-cases names and types and parses JSON via `instructor` (`Mode.JSON`) with `json_repair` as a dependency. + - **Gleaning**: `_gleaning` runs `max_gleaning_steps` rounds (`_services/_base.py` default **0**, so off by default) of `entity_relationship_continue_extraction` plus a `TGleaningStatus` done/continue check. Note: the check compares `gleaning_status.status == Literal["done"]`, which is always false in Python, so when enabled gleaning always runs the full number of steps. + - Entity types not in `entity_types` (after stripping spaces/underscores and upper-casing) are relabelled `UNKNOWN`. Each relationship gets `chunks = [chunk.id]`. + - `_merge`: per-document chunk graphs are upserted into a temporary `IGraphStorage` using the `information_extraction_upsert_policy` = `DefaultGraphUpsertPolicy(NodeUpsertPolicy_SummarizeDescription, EdgeUpsertPolicy_UpsertIfValidNodes)`. +5. **Graph upsert into the main store** (`_services/_state_manager.py::DefaultStateManagerService.upsert`): + - Nodes: `NodeUpsertPolicy_SummarizeDescription` (`_policies/_graph_upsert.py`) groups by name, appends the existing node, joins descriptions with newlines, and if the result exceeds `max_node_description_size` (512 chars) calls the LLM with `PROMPTS["summarize_entity_descriptions"]` (`TEntityDescription`); type = most common. + - Edges: `EdgeUpsertPolicy_UpsertValidAndMergeSimilarByLLM`: edges are grouped by `(source, target)`; if existing + new edges between a pair exceed `edge_merge_threshold` (5), the LLM is asked with `PROMPTS["edges_group_similar"]` (`TEditRelationList`) to group duplicate facts into merged descriptions; chunk lists are unioned, merged-away edges deleted. Otherwise edges are simply inserted (multi-edges between the same pair are allowed). + - **Entity embeddings**: `embedding_service.encode([entity.to_str()])` where `to_str()` = `"[TYPE] NAME\n[DESCRIPTION] desc"`; upserted into `HNSWVectorStorage` keyed by node index. + - **Entity deduplication by similarity**: `entity_storage.get_knn(embeddings, top_k=3)`; pairs with cosine score >= `insert_similarity_score_threshold` (0.9) that are not already neighbours get an **identity edge** with description `"is"` and no chunks. Nodes are not merged, only linked, so PageRank flows between duplicates. + - Chunks are stored (`chunk_storage.upsert`). +6. **Commit** (`insert_done`): builds and pickles two sparse matrices via `PickleBlobStorage`: `map_e2r` (entities x relationships incidence from `IGraphStorage.get_entities_to_relationships_map`) and `map_r2c` (relationships x chunks from edge `chunks` attributes). All storages are flushed (igraph pickle, hnswlib index + metadata, KV pickle). + +```mermaid +flowchart TB + IN[insert text + metadata] --> CH[DefaultChunkingService
separator split, 800 tok as chars/4, overlap 100, xxhash ids] + CH --> NEW[filter_new_chunks] + NEW --> EX[entity_relationship_extraction
domain / example_queries / entity_types
instructor JSON -> TGraph] + EX -. optional max_gleaning_steps .-> GL[continue_extraction] + EX --> DOCG[per-document IGraphStorage merge] + DOCG --> NU[NodeUpsertPolicy_SummarizeDescription

Graph data model + +Defined in `fast_graphrag/_types.py` as dataclasses with paired pydantic `Model`s for LLM I/O. + +- **Node** `TEntity`: `name` (upper-cased, is the node id), `type` (upper-cased, constrained to user `entity_types` or `UNKNOWN`), `description`. Context fields `F_TO_CONTEXT = ["name", "description"]`. No degree, no community, no source chunk list on nodes. +- **Edge** `TRelation`: `source`, `target`, `description`, `chunks: List[THash]` (provenance lives on edges, not nodes). Graph is undirected (`ig.Graph(directed=False)`), multi-edges allowed, plus synthetic identity edges (`description="is"`, `chunks=[]`) between near-duplicate entities. +- **Chunk** `TChunk`: `id` (xxh3 64-bit), `content`, `metadata` dict (surfaced in context via `F_TO_CONTEXT = ["content", "metadata"]`). +- **Derived matrices**: `map_e2r` (entities x relationships), `map_r2c` (relationships x chunks), rebuilt on every `insert_done`. +- **Context/response**: `TContext` holds scored lists of entities, relations, chunks; `TQueryResponse` = `response` + `context`, with `to_dict()` for serialization. +- No communities, reports, claims, or documents table. Document identity is not preserved beyond chunk metadata. + +Working directory layout: `Workspace.make_for(namespace)` creates namespaces `graph`, `entities`, `chunks`, `map_e2r`, `map_r2c` under `working_dir` (or `working_dir//` when `n_checkpoints > 0`). Query / retrieval modes + +There is exactly one retrieval mode. `GraphRAG.query(query, QueryParam, response_model=None)` -> `BaseGraphRAG.async_query` (`_graphrag.py`). `QueryParam`: `with_references` (False), `only_context` (False), `entities_max_tokens` 4000, `relations_max_tokens` 3000, `chunks_max_tokens` 9000 (converted to characters x4 for truncation). + +1. **Query entity extraction** (`DefaultInformationExtractionService.extract_entities_from_query`): 1 LLM call with `PROMPTS["entity_extraction_query"]` returning `TQueryEntities{named: [...], generic: [...]}` (named entities are upper-cased and written as `[TYPE] NAME`; generic concepts such as "film director"). +2. **Embedding**: one `encode` call for `named + "[NONE] " + generic + [query]`. +3. **Vector scoring** (`DefaultStateManagerService.get_context` -> `_score_entities_by_vectordb`): + - named entities: `score_all(top_k=1, threshold=query_similarity_score_threshold=0.7)`; + - generic entities and the raw query: `score_all(top_k=20, threshold=0.5)`; + - each row is normalized to sum 1, rows are max-combined into a single `(1, #entities)` sparse seed vector. Generation / answer synthesis + +- Prompts are entries in `fast_graphrag/_prompt.py::PROMPTS`: `entity_relationship_extraction_system/_prompt`, `entity_relationship_continue_extraction_*`, `entity_relationship_gleaning_done_extraction_*`, `entity_extraction_query`, `summarize_entity_descriptions`, `edges_group_similar`, `generate_response_query_with_references`, `generate_response_query_no_references`, `fail_response`. `format_and_send_prompt` (`_llm/_base.py`) looks up `_system` / `_prompt` pairs or a single key. +- Answer prompt instructs the model to use Entities/Relationships as a map and read Sources for detail, to be concise, and to say no relevant information was found rather than invent. With `with_references=True` it must append `[]` after each sentence, where ids index the `## Sources` list; `TQueryResponse.context.chunks` carries the same order so callers can resolve ids to chunk content and metadata (`examples/query_parameters.ipynb`). +- Structured output: responses are parsed into `TAnswer{answer}` or any pydantic `response_model` passed to `query()`, enabling typed answers. +- Single-shot generation only; no map-reduce, no streaming, no conversation history. + +## 8. LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +- Default LLM: `OpenAILLMService` (`_llm/_llm_openai.py`) with `model="gpt-4o-mini"`, `instructor.Mode.JSON`, `AsyncOpenAI` (any OpenAI-compatible `base_url`), tenacity retries on rate-limit/connection/timeout. Concurrency: semaphore `max_requests_concurrent` from env `CONCURRENT_TASK_LIMIT` (default 1024), optional `aiolimiter` per-minute/per-second limiters (`rate_limit_per_minute`, `rate_limit_per_second`). Also `GeminiLLMService`/`GeminiEmbeddingService` (`_llm/_llm_genai.py`, google-genai and Vertex AI) and `VoyageAIEmbeddingService` (`_llm/_llm_voyage.py`). +- Default embedder: `OpenAIEmbeddingService` `text-embedding-3-small` (dim 1536), per-minute limiter on by default. +- No response cache in the OSS code (unlike the other two frameworks); repeated inserts of identical chunks are skipped by hash instead. +- Index-time LLM calls: 1 per chunk (gleaning off by default); +1 per entity whose merged description exceeds 512 chars; +1 per entity pair whose edge count exceeds 5 (edge grouping). Embedding calls: one batch per insert over all upserted entities. No community-level calls at all. README: *The Wizard of Oz* costs $0.08 vs $0.48 for graphrag (6x). +- Query-time: 1 LLM call (query entity extraction) + 1 embedding batch + 1 LLM call (answer) = 2 completions per query, plus CPU-side PPR over the full graph (igraph, fast for 10^5-10^6 nodes). +- Chunk sizes are estimated by characters (ratio 4), so actual token counts vary by language. + +Worked example: *A Christmas Carol* (~160k characters) becomes ~55 chunks of 3 200 characters; indexing is ~55 extraction calls with gpt-4o-mini (each roughly 2.5k prompt tokens including the long JSON-example system prompt) plus a handful of summarization/edge-merge calls and one embedding batch for a few hundred entities, which is consistent with the README's $0.08 figure. Querying costs two small completions regardless of corpus size; the graph walk is local CPU. + +## 9. Configuration and extension points + +- Constructor: `GraphRAG(working_dir, domain, example_queries, entity_types, n_checkpoints=0, config=GraphRAG.Config(...))`. `domain`, `example_queries`, `entity_types` are mandatory and are injected into the extraction prompt, which is the primary "tuning" mechanism. +- `GraphRAG.Config` fields (`fast_graphrag/__init__.py`): `chunking_service_cls`, `information_extraction_service_cls`, `information_extraction_upsert_policy`, `state_manager_cls`, `llm_service`, `embedding_service`, `graph_storage`, `entity_storage`, `chunk_storage`, `entity_ranking_policy`, `relation_ranking_policy`, `chunk_ranking_policy`, `node_upsert_policy`, `edge_upsert_policy`. Example in `examples/custom_llm.py`: `config=GraphRAG.Config(llm_service=OpenAILLMService(model=..., base_url=..., api_key=...), embedding_service=OpenAIEmbeddingService(...))`. +- Service/policy tunables: `DefaultChunkingServiceConfig(separators, chunk_token_size, chunk_token_overlap)`; `max_gleaning_steps` on the extraction service; `NodeUpsertPolicy_SummarizeDescription.Config(max_node_description_size, node_summarization_prompt, is_async)`; `EdgeUpsertPolicy_UpsertValidAndMergeSimilarByLLM.Config(edge_merge_threshold)`; `DefaultStateManagerService.insert_similarity_score_threshold` (0.9), `query_similarity_score_threshold` (0.7); `IGraphStorageConfig.ppr_damping`; `HNSWVectorStorageConfig(ef_construction, M, ef_search, num_threads)`; ranking policy configs. +- Prompts: mutate `fast_graphrag._prompt.PROMPTS[...]` before constructing. +- **Incremental updates**: first-class. Each `insert` only extracts new chunks (hash dedup), merges nodes/edges into the persistent igraph graph via the upsert policies, re-embeds only upserted nodes, adds identity edges, and rebuilds the two sparse maps. No global recomputation (no clustering exists), so cost is proportional to the delta. Strengths + +- Lowest indexing cost of the three: one LLM call per 800-token chunk by default, no community summarization, no per-entity summary unless descriptions grow large. +- Query retrieval is graph-native (personalized PageRank from HippoRAG) rather than "embed query, grab neighbours", which is well suited to multi-hop factoid questions; the author benchmark shows large gains on 2WikiMultihopQA multihop queries. +- True incremental updates proportional to the delta, with checkpointing. +- Embedding-based entity deduplication (identity edges) and LLM-based edge fact merging keep the graph from fragmenting as data accumulates. +- Structured-output everywhere (`instructor` + pydantic), typed `response_model` on queries, and an explicit `TContext` with scores returned alongside the answer. +- Domain/example-query/entity-type driven prompt makes the ontology steerable without editing prompt text. +- Small, well-typed code base with unit tests; policies and services are swappable dataclasses. + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +- No global / summarization mode: without communities or reports it cannot answer "what are the main themes across the corpus" style questions; retrieval always bottoms out in top-8 chunks. +- Single-process file storage only (igraph pickle, hnswlib, pickles); no database backends, no multi-tenant workspaces in OSS, the whole graph and index are loaded into memory per process. +- Chunk sizing by characters/4 rather than tokens; no tokenizer-aware truncation (tiktoken is a dependency but not used for budgeting in the reviewed code). +- Gleaning is off by default and the done-check (`== Literal["done"]`) is a bug, so enabling it always runs all steps. +- `node_specificity` and `RankingPolicy_WithConfidence` are stubs raising `NotImplementedError`. +- No LLM response cache; no per-document delete; document identity is only preserved through chunk `metadata`. +- Citations are chunk indexes within the returned context, not stable ids; nodes have no provenance (only edges carry `chunks`), so entity-only facts are not traceable to sources. +- Identity edges link near-duplicate entities but never merge them, so duplicate nodes persist in the entities table shown to the LLM. +- Version 0.0.5, no documentation site, roadmap unclear; the team's effort is on the managed service. + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +Choose fast-graphrag when you need cheap, incrementally updated graph indexing and precise multi-hop retrieval over facts (QA, agents, support/knowledge bases), you are happy with a single mode of query, and you can run everything in one process on local files. It is a good fit for OpenAI-compatible or Gemini endpoints and for workloads where index cost dominates. Prefer Microsoft GraphRAG when corpus-level summarization (global/DRIFT search) or Azure backends matter, and nano-graphrag when you want a hackable reference GraphRAG with community reports and pluggable graph/vector databases. + +## 14. Core idea in one paragraph + +Graph-R1 treats GraphRAG as a **multi-turn agent problem**: a small policy LLM (Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B/7B-Instruct) repeatedly emits `…{"query": …}`, an external retrieval server answers inside `…`, and the loop ends when the policy emits `……` (or `max_turns` is hit). The knowledge base is HyperGraphRAG's n-ary hypergraph (hyperedge sentences + member entities, extracted once with GPT-4o-mini); retrieval is dual-channel dense matching (BGE-large over entity descriptions and over hyperedge sentences via FAISS) followed by one-hop bipartite expansion and **reciprocal-rank fusion** of the two channels. The policy is trained **end-to-end with GRPO** (also PPO and REINFORCE++ scripts) using a purely outcome-based reward: `-1 + format_reward (0..1) + answer_F1` where the F1 term is only awarded when the format is perfect. Retrieved `` tokens are masked out of the policy-gradient loss, so the model learns *when and what to query* and *how to compose answers*, not to imitate retrieved text. + +## 3. LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +**Offline (once per corpus)** +* Hypergraph extraction: same as HyperGraphRAG — ~3 (max 5) `gpt-4o-mini` calls per 1200-token chunk plus occasional description summaries. For the six FlashRAG corpora (Wikipedia-derived, tens of thousands of passages each) this is the dominant API cost; the authors distribute pre-built graphs for this reason. +* Embedding: BGE-large-en-v1.5 over every entity (name+description) and every hyperedge sentence (and chunks, unused). Runs on whatever device FlagEmbedding picks (GPU if available at build time; CPU at serve time). + +**Training (per run)** +* GRPO: 128 prompts x 5 samples x up to 10 turns of vLLM generation per step, plus a retrieval HTTP call per active trajectory per turn, plus actor/ref log-prob passes. README: 4 x 48 GB GPUs for 3B; `max_prompt_length=4096` bounds the context (long multi-turn histories are left-truncated, which can drop the question — unclear whether the authors guard against this; I found no guard). +* The retrieval server runs BGE on **CPU** by default, which can bottleneck rollouts; batched calls mitigate this. +* No reward model GPU: rewards are rule-based. + +**Inference (per question)** +* 1 to `max_turns` policy generations (paper reports ~2-3 turns on average after training), each followed by one BGE encode + two FAISS Flat searches + graph lookups. No API LLM needed at inference; the 3B policy fits on one GPU. + +## 9. Configuration and extension points + +* **Hydra config**: `verl/trainer/config/ppo_trainer.yaml` (data lengths, actor/critic/rollout, `algorithm.adv_estimator`, `tool.*`: `max_turns`, `use_batch_tool_calls`, tag strings, `tool_custom_response_template`, `env`). Override on the CLI as in `run_*.sh`. +* **Swap the tool / knowledge source**: implement `agent/tool/tool_base.py::Tool` (`execute`, `batch_execute`, `calculate_reward`, `validate_args`) and register in `agent/tool/tools/__init__.py::_default_tools` (`search` -> hypergraph server, `wikisearch`, `calculator` exist). The policy prompt is fixed in `script_process.py`; changing tags requires editing `tool.*` YAML, `qa_em_and_format.py` regexes and `_create_loss_mask` tag strings together. +* **Swap retrieval behaviour**: `script_api.py` (k per channel = 5, `top_k=10`, embedding model) and `graphr1/operate.py::_build_query_context` (fusion rule). Returning chunk text instead of hyperedge sentences is a two-line change (commented code present). +* **Swap extraction LLM / embeddings for graph building**: `GraphR1(llm_model_func=…, embedding_func=…)` as in HyperGraphRAG (embedding_func is effectively unused because vdbs are KV); dense indexes are built separately by `embed_knowledge()`. +* **Swap reward**: `verl/trainer/main_ppo.py::RewardManager` calls `_default_compute_score_format_answer`; edit `qa_em_and_format.py` or pass a different function. `NaiveRewardManager`/`PrimeRewardManager` in `verl/workers/reward_manager/` are unused. +* **Base policy**: `-p ` in the run scripts; chat template assumptions (`<|im_start|>`, `<|im_end|>`) are Qwen-specific and baked into the reward parser, loss mask and response template — other model families need those strings changed. +* **Incremental update**: none. The hypergraph can be appended via `GraphR1.insert()` (HyperGraphRAG semantics), but `embed_knowledge()` rebuilds all FAISS indexes from scratch and the API server loads indexes once at startup. There is no deletion. Policy retraining is not required for new knowledge (the policy learns a querying behaviour, not the facts), which is the practical upside of the design. + +## 10. Benchmarks reported by the authors + +* **Datasets** (FlashRAG splits, Terabox download): 2WikiMultiHopQA, HotpotQA, MuSiQue, NQ, PopQA, TriviaQA. Training on each dataset's train split; test on its test split; corpus = that dataset's passages. +* **Metrics**: EM, F1 (`evaluation/eval.py`), LLM-judge generation score (`eval_g.py`, 7 rubrics x 0-100 blended with F1), average retrieval turns and response length (README figures `*_turn.png`, `*_res.png`). +* **Reported comparisons** (README figures; numbers from the paper, not in the repo — verify before quoting): (1) RL algorithms — GRPO > REINFORCE++ > PPO on F1/EM with Qwen2.5-3B; (2) across GraphRAG baselines — Graph-R1 (3B, GRPO) is reported to beat NaiveGeneration, StandardRAG, GraphRAG, LightRAG, PathRAG, HippoRAG2 and HyperGraphRAG *as well as* RL-RAG methods Search-R1 and R1-Searcher on average F1, with the abstract citing an average F1 of about 57.8 for the 7B setting (3B around the low 50s) versus roughly 40 or below for prompt-only GraphRAG baselines on the same splits; (3) scaling — 1.5B < 3B < 7B monotonically, with 1.5B sometimes failing to learn the format. Average turns settle around 2-3 and responses get longer than non-RL baselines. +* **Ablations** in the paper (not reproducible from repo scripts alone): removing the hypergraph (plain chunk retrieval), removing multi-turn (single query), and removing the format reward each reduce F1; hypergraph retrieval has higher per-query cost than chunk retrieval but higher answer quality. +* **Third-party**: none found in repo. Note Graph-R1's baseline numbers for HippoRAG2 / LightRAG use the same FlashRAG corpora and their own re-runs, so they are not directly comparable to those methods' own papers. + +## 11. Strengths + +* Clean separation: the **knowledge store is frozen and external** (HTTP), the **policy learns to use it**; new facts do not require retraining, and any retrieval backend speaking the `/search` contract can be swapped in. +* Outcome-only reward with format gating is simple, rule-based (no reward model) and demonstrably teaches small models (3B) a stable think -> query -> knowledge -> answer protocol. +* Loss masking of retrieved tokens (`_create_loss_mask`) is correctly implemented, so the policy is not trained to regurgitate knowledge blocks. +* Multi-turn querying gives genuine multi-hop behaviour without PPR or graph algorithms; the agent decomposes the question itself. +* Hypergraph sentences are a good retrieval unit for an agent: short, self-contained, readable, already de-contextualised by the extractor. +* Full veRL/Ray/vLLM/FSDP training stack vendored with working GRPO, PPO and REINFORCE++ scripts; wandb logging of F1/EM/format/turns. +* Inference needs no API LLM. + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +* **Heavy and brittle environment**: pinned `torch 2.4 + vllm<=0.6.3 + flash-attn + ray`, 4 x 48 GB GPUs, hard-coded ports/paths, OpenAI key file, Terabox-only datasets and graphs; `verl` is vendored, not pip-installable from upstream. +* Qwen chat-template strings are hard-coded in reward parsing, loss masking and the tool-response template; other model families need code edits in three places. +* Retrieval quality is capped by **5 + 5 FAISS neighbours** and the unbounded one-hop expansion from entities (no token truncation in `_get_node_data`), then RRF to 10; hub entities bias the list toward high-degree hyperedges. Hyperedge FAISS scores are discarded (`rank = weight`). +* `SearchTool.execute` is a stub; only batched execution works. `PENALTY_FOR_INVALID=0` and tool rewards are 0, so all shaping comes from the format regex. +* Format reward counts 0.5 per well-formed query turn but is clamped at 1.0, so after one query there is no incentive difference between 1 and 10 queries other than context length; the paper's "turns" curves show it settles at 2-3 by F1 pressure, but that is emergent, not designed. +* Rollout context is left-truncated to 4096 tokens including the prompt; with 4096-token tool responses a single large `` block can push the question out of context. I found no safeguard. +* No incremental/delete path; FAISS indexes rebuilt wholesale; server loads everything into RAM; BGE runs on CPU at serve time. +* Graph building inherits all HyperGraphRAG issues (positional entity-to-hyperedge parsing, string-keyed nodes, no entity resolution, dead LightRAG code paths). +* No tests, squashed history, Chinese/English mixed comments, evaluation depends on a paid LLM judge. +* Reported gains are on Wikipedia QA with gold short answers; nothing in the repo evaluates long-form or domain corpora. + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +Choose Graph-R1 when you (a) own a GPU training budget and want a **small, self-hosted policy model** that has learned to interrogate a knowledge base over multiple turns, (b) have gold short answers for your domain to drive the F1 reward, and (c) are comfortable running a veRL/Ray/vLLM stack. It is the right reference implementation for "RL-trained agentic GraphRAG" and for reusing its environment/reward/loss-mask code with your own retriever. It is the wrong choice for a drop-in RAG library, for corpora that change often, for long-form answers, or for teams without RL infrastructure — in those cases take the HyperGraphRAG retrieval server idea alone and drive it with a prompted frontier model. + +## 14. Core idea in one paragraph + +GraphRAG-SDK v1 is a single-database GraphRAG framework: FalkorDB holds the lexical layer (Document and Chunk nodes), the knowledge layer (typed entity nodes joined by a single `RELATES` edge type whose original predicate lives in a `rel_type` property), the vector indexes and full-text indexes, and even the ontology itself (stored as a sibling graph `__ontology`). Ingestion is a fixed nine-step strategy pipeline (`ingestion/pipeline.py:IngestionPipeline`) in which a local GLiNER NER model proposes entities, one LLM call per chunk verifies them and extracts relationships, entities are pruned against an ontology and deduplicated, and everything is written with batched `UNWIND ... MERGE`. Retrieval (`retrieval/strategies/multi_path.py:MultiPathRetrieval`) fans a question out over RELATES-edge vector search, entity name/full-text discovery, 1- and 2-hop relationship expansion, four chunk-retrieval paths and an optional text-to-Cypher path, reranks chunks locally with stored embeddings, assembles a sectioned context and asks the LLM to answer from it only. The design thesis stated in the README is that "the retrieval harness matters more than the model", with grounding/abstention (`return_context=True`, `MENTIONED_IN` provenance) as a first-class concern. + +## 3. Indexing pipeline, step by step + +Entry point: `GraphRAG.ingest()` (`api/main.py:1778`), which builds an `IngestionPipeline` with defaults and calls `IngestionPipeline.run()` (`ingestion/pipeline.py:217`). The pipeline docstring says it is "intentionally *not* a generic DAG". + +Defaults chosen by the facade (`api/main.py`, `ingest()` docstring and `_default_extractor` / `_default_ingest_resolver`): +- Loader: picked from extension (`ingestion/loaders/`: `TextLoader`, `pdf_loader.PdfLoader` (pypdf; PyMuPDF optional), `markdown_loader` (structure-preserving, heading breadcrumbs), `record_loader.CsvRecordLoader` for `.csv/.tsv/.psv/.tab`). +- Chunker: `SentenceTokenCapChunking(max_tokens=384, overlap_sentences=2)` (`ingestion/chunking_strategies/sentence_token_cap.py`). 384 is the GLiNER window. Alternatives: `FixedSizeChunking(chunk_size=1000, chunk_overlap=100)`, `ContextualChunking` (one LLM call per chunk to prepend document context, `_CONTEXT_PROMPT`), `StructuralChunking` (Markdown headings), `CallableChunking`. +- Extractor: `GraphExtraction(llm, entity_types=)`. +- Resolver: `ExactMatchResolution` (zero LLM calls). +- `max_concurrency=3` parallel documents. + +Steps as logged in `IngestionPipeline.run()`: + +1. **Load** (`Step 1/9`) - `LoaderStrategy.load(source, ctx)` returns `DocumentOutput(text, document_info, elements)`. A SHA-256 `content_hash` of the text is compared with the stored `DocumentRecord`; unchanged content is skipped (`metadata["skipped_unchanged"]`). +2. **Chunk** - `ChunkingStrategy.chunk_document()` -> `TextChunks`; chunk uids are made deterministic from the document uid (`_assign_deterministic_chunk_uids`). +3. **Lexical graph** - `_build_lexical_graph()` (mixin `LexicalGraphWriter`) MERGEs `Document` and `Chunk` nodes, `PART_OF` and `NEXT_CHUNK` edges. Mandatory, not a strategy. +4. **Extract** - `GraphExtraction.extract(chunks, ontology, ctx)` (`ingestion/extraction_strategies/graph_extraction.py:561`). Two sub-steps: + - 4a. Optional coreference resolution (`coref_resolvers.FastCorefResolver`, extra `fastcoref`). + - 4b. NER via a pluggable `EntityExtractor` (`entity_extractors.py`): `GLiNERExtractor` (default, local model `urchade/gliner_medium-v2.1`, threshold 0.75, sub-threshold band labelled `Unknown`), `LLMExtractor` (uses `NER_PROMPT`, batched through `LLMInterface.abatch_invoke`), `SpacyExtractor`, `CompositeExtractor`. + - 4c. One LLM call per chunk with `VERIFY_EXTRACT_RELS_PROMPT` ("VERIFY the entities ... EXTRACT all relationships"). The prompt lists entity types and, when no ontology relations are declared, offers `DEFAULT_RELATION_TYPES` (31 UPPER_SNAKE_CASE labels such as `LOCATED_IN`, `EMPLOYED_AT`, `AUTHORED`) as a *preferred* vocabulary. A long code comment documents the measurement behind this (447 distinct labels without a default list; +2x triple F1 with one). Output is JSON parsed into `ExtractedEntity` / `ExtractedRelation` / `EntityMention` and aggregated into `GraphData` (`core/models.py`). Entity ids are deterministic: `compute_entity_id(name, type)` -> `"alice__person"`. + - `GraphData.extraction_failed` and per-chunk failure counts are carried into `IngestionResult.metadata["extraction"]`. +5. **Quality filter + Prune** - `_filter_quality()` then `_prune(graph_data, ontology)`: drops entities whose label is not in `Ontology.entities` and relations whose `(source_label, rel_type, target_label)` pattern is not declared in `Ontology.relations[].patterns`. Skipped entirely in open-schema mode (empty `Ontology()`). +6. **Resolve** - `ResolutionStrategy.resolve(graph_data, ctx)` -> `ResolutionResult(nodes, relationships, remap)`. `ExactMatchResolution` groups by `(normalized name, label)`; `LLMVerifiedResolution` (`resolution_strategies/llm_verified_resolution.py:423`) adds embedding-ANN candidate pairs, hard-merges above `hard_threshold`, sends the ambiguous band to a YES/NO LLM batch (`_VERIFY_PROMPT_INTRO`), re-asks cross-label pairs with A/B swapped (`cross_label_vote`), then Union-Find. Strengths + +- Everything lives in one database: graph, vectors, full-text and the ontology. Operationally simple (one Docker container), one connection, one backup. +- Grounding is designed in: `MENTIONED_IN` provenance, document attribution in every passage, `return_context=True`, prompt-injection hardening of the context block, abstention example. +- Mature incremental-update story (hash short-circuit, cached chunk extraction, crash-safe cutover, orphan cleanup, batch API) - rare among GraphRAG frameworks. +- Low extraction cost: local GLiNER NER plus one LLM call per chunk; zero-LLM resolution by default; reranking from stored vectors. +- Serious entity resolution: three-tier within-document resolver, cross-document LLM judge with double-vote, acronym folding, `SAME_AS`/`DISTINCT_FROM` audit edges, near-miss reporting. +- Ontology lifecycle: discovery (LLM or DBpedia-grounded), persistence in the DB, evolution with LLM backfill, structured CSV ingestion with typed columns that feed text-to-Cypher. +- Strict, well-commented code with measurement notes explaining design decisions; `mypy --strict`, Pydantic everywhere. + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +- **FalkorDB lock-in**: no other graph or vector backend; Cypher dialect specifics (`vecf32`, `db.idx.*`) are baked into `GraphStore`/`VectorStore`. +- **Breaking rewrite**: v1 is API-incompatible with v0.x; the v0.x `KnowledgeGraph`, `ChatSession`, `Orchestrator` and multi-agent features are gone. Projects that depended on them must pin 0.8.2. +- `finalize()` is O(graph size) and must be remembered; skipping it leaves cross-document duplicates and no entity/edge vector indexes (the SDK only warns). +- Text-to-Cypher is explicitly "experimental", off by default, weakest path in isolation (53%), and adds 1-3 LLM calls and ~1.5 s. +- No community detection / global summarisation mode, so corpus-level "what are the main themes" questions rely on vector+fact retrieval alone. +- `gliner` (and therefore torch/transformers) is a *hard* dependency, making the install heavy even if you use `LLMExtractor`. +- Single `RELATES` edge type means native Cypher queries by predicate need property filters rather than typed edges; schema-driven tooling that expects typed relationships will not see them. +- PDF ingestion is described as incomplete on the roadmap ("complete PDF ingestion" 2026-Q3); `pdf-fast` uses AGPL PyMuPDF. +- Facade is large (`api/main.py` ~5,200 lines) and not re-entrant as an async context manager. +- Vendor-reported benchmarks only. + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +Choose GraphRAG-SDK when you want a single-process Python library with one lightweight database, care about provenance/abstention and low per-chunk LLM cost, need documents to be re-synced incrementally (CI-driven doc sites, knowledge bases), or need to join CSV/tabular facts with prose into one graph and ask aggregate questions via text-to-Cypher. Core idea in one paragraph + +HippoRAG 2 builds a cheap, LLM-extracted *provenance graph* over a corpus — passage nodes, entity ("phrase") nodes, and three edge kinds (fact co-occurrence, passage-contains-entity, embedding synonymy) — and at query time it does **not** ask the LLM to reason over the graph. Instead it (1) embeds the query and dense-retrieves *triple facts* (`query_to_fact`), (2) optionally lets a small LLM "recognition memory" filter (`DSPyFilter`) prune the candidate facts, (3) converts the surviving facts' subject/object phrases into personalised reset weights on entity nodes, adds a small dense-passage prior (`passage_node_weight=0.05`) on every passage node, and (4) runs **Personalized PageRank** (igraph `prpack`, damping 0.5) on the undirected weighted graph. The PPR mass that lands on passage nodes is the final ranking; the top-k passages are handed to a plain reading-comprehension prompt. The design goal is "memory-like" multi-hop associativity with a single embedding call plus one small LLM call per query, and a *continual* index that can be grown or shrunk without re-running extraction. + +## 3. Indexing pipeline, step by step + +Entry point: `HippoRAG.index(docs)` in `HippoRAG.py` (line ~499). The method is idempotent over chunk hashes and incremental by design. + +### 3.1 Chunking / preprocessing +* `preprocessing.py` defines `BaseTextPreprocessor` and the default `TextPreprocessor`, which **does not split documents**: it keeps one `Chunk` per input string (`Chunk(content, source_id, metadata)` dataclass in `utils/misc_utils.py`). You are expected to chunk upstream or inject your own preprocessor (`text_preprocessor=` constructor arg; `text_preprocessor_class_name`, `preprocess_chunk_max_token_size`, `preprocess_chunk_overlap_token_size=128`, `preprocess_chunk_func` exist in `BaseConfig` but the default class ignores them). +* Chunk IDs are `compute_mdhash_id(content, prefix="chunk-")` (MD5 of content). Chunk metadata (`source_id`, user metadata) is persisted separately in `chunk_metadata.json`. + +### 3.2 OpenIE: two LLM calls per chunk +Module: `information_extraction/openie_openai.py`, class `OpenIE` (used for any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint; `openie_vllm_offline.py` / `openie_transformers_offline.py` are the local variants selected via `openie_mode`). + +1. **NER** — `OpenIE.ner(chunk_key, passage)` renders prompt template `ner` (`prompts/templates/ner.py`): a one-shot system/user/assistant exchange ("Radio City" example) asking for `{"named_entities": [...]}`. Output cap `openie_ner_max_tokens=2048`. +2. **Triple extraction** — `OpenIE.triple_extraction(chunk_key, passage, named_entities)` renders template `triple_extraction` (`prompts/templates/triple_extraction.py`): "construct an RDF graph … each triple should contain at least one, but preferably two, of the named entities … resolve pronouns". Output `{"triples": [[s, p, o], ...]}`. Output cap `openie_triple_max_tokens=4096`. +3. `OpenIE.batch_openie(chunks)` runs all NER calls on a `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=openie_max_workers)` (default 8), fails hard if any NER call errored, then runs all triple calls. Responses are parsed by `_extract_json_list_field` / `_parse_bare_json_string_list` with tolerant JSON extraction. +4. Results are merged into `all_openie_info` (list of `{idx, passage, extracted_entities, extracted_triples}`) and persisted to `openie_results_ner_.json` in `save_dir` (`save_openie_results`). `load_existing_openie()` means re-indexing only extracts for chunks without stored OpenIE output. `openie_mode='offline'` runs `pre_openie()` which extracts, saves, then deliberately raises so you can rerun online with cached results. + +All LLM calls go through `llm/openai_gpt.py::CacheOpenAI`, which caches responses in an SQLite file (`save_dir/llm_cache/_cache.sqlite`) guarded by `filelock`, and *fails closed* if the endpoint does not return `usage` token counts. + +### 3.3 Normalisation and node/fact extraction +* `utils/misc_utils.py::text_processing()` casefolds, strips non-alphanumerics to spaces, collapses whitespace. All triples are normalised this way before becoming graph keys (so "Radio City" and "radio city" collapse). +* `extract_entity_nodes(chunk_triples)` yields the set of subject/object phrases; `flatten_facts()` yields the set of unique triples. + +### 3.4 Embeddings: three stores +`embedding_store.py::get_embedding_store()` creates three namespaces, each keyed by MD5 hash with prefix: + +| Store | Namespace / prefix | Text embedded | +|---|---|---| +| `chunk_embedding_store` | `chunk-` | raw passage text | +| `entity_embedding_store` | `entity-` | normalised phrase | +| `fact_embedding_store` | `fact-` | `str((s, p, o))` tuple string | + +`insert_strings()` only embeds hashes not already present (`get_missing_string_hash_ids`). Default backend is Parquet (`vdb_.parquet` under `save_dir/_/`). Embedding model is selected by `embedding_model/__init__.py::_get_embedding_model_class()` (NV-Embed-v2 default, GritLM, Contriever, OpenAI `text-embedding-*`, Cohere, `Transformers/`, `VLLM/`, or explicit `embedding_provider`). Instruction-tuned models get task instructions from `prompts/linking.py::get_query_instruction()`. + +### 3.5 Graph construction (igraph) +Graph lives in `self.graph` (`igraph.Graph`, undirected by default `is_directed_graph=False`), pickled to `graph.pickle`. + +1. `add_fact_edges(chunk_ids, chunk_triples)` — for each triple adds an entity–entity edge key `(entity-hash(s), entity-hash(o))`, weight incremented by 1 per occurrence, and records `_fact_edge_source_counts[edge][chunk_id]` for provenance. Also fills `ent_node_to_chunk_ids`. +2. `add_passage_edges(chunk_ids, chunk_triple_entities)` — for each *new* chunk adds `(chunk-id, entity-id)` edges with weight 1.0 (`_passage_edge_sources`). +3. `add_synonymy_edges(query_node_keys)` — KNN (`utils/embed_utils.py::retrieve_knn`, batched dot products) of **new** entity embeddings against all entity embeddings, `k=synonymy_edge_topk` (2047), keep neighbours with cosine >= `synonymy_edge_sim_threshold` (0.8), max 100 per node, skip phrases shorter than 3 alphanumerics. Edge weight = similarity score. Only new entities are queried, so incremental cost is `O(new x all)`. +4. `augment_graph()` -> `add_new_nodes()` (vertices from entity + chunk stores, attribute `name` = hash id, plus `content`) and `add_new_edges()`, which merges contributions by logical `(source_key, target_key)` so re-indexing never creates parallel edges. Edge attributes: `weight`, `edge_kind` (`fact`, `synonym`, `fact+synonym`, `passage`), `fact_source_counts`, `synonym_score`, `passage_source`, `source_key`, `target_key`. Graph-level attribute `hipporag_edge_schema=1` marks the source-aware schema; older pickles are rejected for further indexing/deletion. +5. `save_igraph()` pickles. `index_manifest.json` (`utils/state_utils.py::validate_or_create_index_manifest`) binds the index to LLM name, embedding model/endpoint/normalisation, OpenIE token limits, synonymy settings and `index_identity`; mismatches raise `StateConsistencyError` rather than silently mixing state. + +### 3.6 Flowchart + +```mermaid +flowchart TD + A[docs: str or Chunk] --> B[TextPreprocessor.preprocess
one Chunk per doc by default] + B --> C[chunk_embedding_store.insert_strings
MD5 chunk- ids, embed passages] + C --> D{OpenIE cached for chunk?} + D -- no --> E[OpenIE.ner prompt 'ner'] + E --> F[OpenIE.triple_extraction prompt 'triple_extraction'] + F --> G[openie_results_ner_LLM.json] + D -- yes --> G + G --> H[text_processing normalise triples] + H --> I[entity_embedding_store.insert_strings
fact_embedding_store.insert_strings] + I --> J[add_fact_edges entity-entity w+=1
add_passage_edges chunk-entity w=1] + J --> K[add_synonymy_edges KNN cos>=0.8
only new entities] + K --> L[augment_graph: add_new_nodes / add_new_edges
merge by logical key] + L --> M[save_igraph graph.pickle + index_manifest.json] +``` + +## 4. Graph data model + +| Element | Key | Attributes | Notes | +|---|---|---|---| +| Passage node | `chunk-` | `name`, `content` | one per chunk; also row in chunk Parquet store with embedding; metadata in `chunk_metadata.json` | +| Phrase (entity) node | `entity-` | `name`, `content` | from triple subjects/objects only (NER entities not in any triple are *not* nodes) | +| Fact | `fact-` | stored in fact embedding store only | **not** a graph node; facts are the dense-retrieval unit at query time and map back to entity nodes through `(s, o)` | +| Fact edge | entity–entity | `weight` = #supporting (chunk, triple) occurrences, `fact_source_counts {chunk_id: n}`, `edge_kind='fact'` | predicate text is **not** stored on the edge | +| Passage edge | chunk–entity | `weight=1.0`, `passage_source=chunk_id`, `edge_kind='passage'` | provenance for PPR mass to flow into passages | +| Synonymy edge | entity–entity | `weight = cosine sim`, `synonym_score`, `edge_kind='synonym'` or `'fact+synonym'` when it coincides with a fact edge | weight = `max(sum(fact counts), synonym_score)` after merge | + +Auxiliary in-memory maps built in `prepare_retrieval_objects()`: `node_name_to_vertex_idx`, `passage_node_idxs`, `entity_node_idxs`, `ent_node_to_chunk_ids`, `proc_triples_to_docs` (normalised triple -> chunk ids), plus dense matrices `entity_embeddings`, `passage_embeddings`, `fact_embeddings` loaded fully into RAM. + +## 5. Storage backends supported + +| Concern | Options | Default | +|---|---|---| +| Graph | igraph pickle only (`graph.pickle`). No external graph DB. | igraph | +| Vectors | `vector_store_type` in `{"parquet","qdrant","chroma","milvus"}` (`vector_stores/qdrant_store.py`, `chroma_store.py`, `milvus_store.py`; all subclass `BaseEmbeddingStore`) | `parquet` (local pandas/pyarrow) | +| Remote collection naming | `vector_stores/naming.py`; per-index `vector_store_namespace`, endpoint fingerprinted in `index_manifest.json` | derived from `save_dir` | +| Milvus | `milvus_uri`, `milvus_token`, `milvus_db_name`, `milvus_consistency_level`; Milvus Lite file if no URI | Milvus Lite | +| Qdrant / Chroma | `qdrant_url`/`qdrant_api_key`; `chroma_host`/`chroma_port` | local | +| OpenIE results | JSON file in `save_dir` | — | +| LLM cache | SQLite in `save_dir/llm_cache/` | enabled | + +Note that even with a remote vector store, retrieval still pulls **all** embeddings into numpy arrays (`prepare_retrieval_objects`) and scores by full dot product; the vector DB is persistence, not ANN search. + +## 6. Query / retrieval modes + +### 6.1 Main mode: `HippoRAG.retrieve(queries, num_to_retrieve)` (HippoRAG 2 retrieval) + +1. `get_query_embeddings()` encodes each query twice (or once if the embedding model is instruction-agnostic): with `query_to_fact` and `query_to_passage` instructions. +2. `get_fact_scores(query)` -> min-max-normalised dot products against **all** fact embeddings. +3. `rerank_facts(query, scores)`: take top `linking_top_k` (default **5**) facts, then `DSPyFilter` (`rerank.py`) — the "recognition memory" step. It renders a DSPy-compiled prompt (`prompts/filter_default_prompt.py::best_dspy_prompt`, or a JSON file via `rerank_dspy_file_path`, e.g. `prompts/dspy_prompts/filter_llama3.3-70B-Instruct.json`) with ten few-shot demos; instruction: "select up to 4 relevant facts … only use facts from the candidate list … return `{"fact": [...]}`". Output facts are mapped back to candidate indices. Exceptions degrade to an empty list. +4. If no facts survive -> fall back to `dense_passage_retrieval(query)` (pure DPR ranking). +5. Else `graph_search_with_fact_entities(query, link_top_k, query_fact_scores, top_k_facts, ...)`: + * For each surviving fact, add its score to `phrase_weights[subject]` and `[object]`, **divided by the number of chunks that mention that entity** (`len(ent_node_to_chunk_ids[phrase])`) — a specificity/IDF-style damping of hub entities; then average over occurrences. + * `get_top_k_weights(link_top_k, ...)` zeroes everything but the top `linking_top_k` phrases. + * `dense_passage_retrieval(query)` -> min-max normalised scores x `passage_node_weight` (0.05) assigned to *every* passage node. + * `node_weights = phrase_weights + passage_weights` -> `run_ppr(node_weights, damping=0.5)` -> `igraph.personalized_pagerank(directed=False, weights='weight', reset=..., implementation='prpack')`. + * Passage node PPR scores sorted descending = result. `retrieval_top_k` default 200 (`num_to_retrieve`). +6. `_build_retrieval_result()` returns `QuerySolution(question, docs, doc_scores, doc_metadata, graph_seeds=top_k_facts)`. + +Timing counters (`rerank_time`, `ppr_time`) are logged. Retrieval evaluation (`RetrievalRecall@k`, k in `[1,2,5,10,20,30,50,100,150,200]`) runs if `gold_docs` are passed. + +### 6.2 Other modes +* `retrieve_dpr` / `rag_qa_dpr` — pure dense baseline inside the same class; `StandardRAG.py` is the standalone DPR baseline used by `main.py --rag_type standard`. +* `retrieve_ircot` / `answer_with_ircot` — iterative IRCoT-style multi-step retrieval (`max_qa_steps`, templates `ircot_hotpotqa|musique|2wikimultihopqa`). Default `max_qa_steps=1` disables iteration. +* MCP tools (`mcp_server.py`): `retrieve`, `rag_qa`, `index`, `delete`, `index_stats`; resource `hipporag://config`. + +### 6.3 Sequence diagram (main mode) + +```mermaid +sequenceDiagram + participant U as Caller + participant H as HippoRAG.retrieve + participant E as EmbeddingModel + participant F as fact_embedding_store + participant R as DSPyFilter (LLM) + participant G as igraph PPR + U->>H: retrieve([query], k) + H->>E: encode(query, query_to_fact) / encode(query, query_to_passage) + H->>F: dot(fact_embeddings, q) -> min-max normalise + H->>H: top linking_top_k=5 facts + H->>R: filter facts (<=4, JSON) + R-->>H: surviving facts + alt no facts + H->>H: dense_passage_retrieval -> ranking + else facts found + H->>H: phrase_weights = fact score / #chunks per entity + H->>H: passage_weights = DPR score * 0.05 + H->>G: personalized_pagerank(reset=phrase+passage, damping=0.5) + G-->>H: scores for passage nodes + end + H-->>U: QuerySolution(docs, doc_scores, graph_seeds) +``` + +### 6.4 Parameters that matter +`linking_top_k` (5), `passage_node_weight` (0.05), `damping` (0.5), `retrieval_top_k` (200), `qa_top_k` (5), `synonymy_edge_sim_threshold` (0.8), `synonymy_edge_topk` (2047), `rerank_dspy_file_path`, `embedding_return_as_normalized=True`. + +## 7. Generation / answer synthesis + +`HippoRAG.rag_qa(queries, gold_docs, gold_answers)` = `retrieve()` + `qa()`. + +`qa()` takes the top `qa_top_k` (5) passages, formats each as `Wikipedia Title: \n\n` (the literal prefix is hard-coded and somewhat misleading for non-Wikipedia corpora), appends `Question: … \nThought: `, and renders template `rag_qa_` (only `rag_qa_musique.py` exists; everything else falls back to it). The prompt is a one-shot chain-of-thought reader: system prompt "advanced reading comprehension assistant … start after 'Thought:' … conclude with 'Answer:'". The predicted answer is `response.split('Answer:')[1]`. QA evaluation uses `evaluation/qa_eval.py::QAExactMatch` and `QAF1Score` when `gold_answers` are provided. + +The QA LLM can differ from the extraction LLM (`qa_llm=` / `extraction_llm=` constructor injection). No training is involved anywhere in HippoRAG; the only "learned" component is the DSPy-compiled filter prompt shipped as JSON. + +## 8. LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +**Indexing, per chunk** +* 2 chat completions (NER + triple extraction), run with 8 threads; both cached in SQLite so re-runs are free. +* 1 embedding of the passage; plus embeddings for each *new* entity phrase and each *new* fact string (typically 10-30 strings per chunk). Embedding cost dominates with local 7B encoders (NV-Embed-v2, GritLM-7B), which need a GPU. +* Synonymy KNN is CPU numpy; scales as new_entities x all_entities. + +**Query, per question** +* 1-2 embedding calls (query under two instructions). +* 1 chat completion for `DSPyFilter` (short prompt, ~10 demos + 5 facts). +* 1 PPR over the whole graph (prpack; milliseconds to seconds depending on graph size; the whole fact matrix dot product is also O(#facts x dim)). +* 1 chat completion for QA if `rag_qa` is used. + +So HippoRAG 2 is roughly "2 LLM calls per chunk offline, 1-2 LLM calls per query online", which is why the paper claims indexing is far cheaper than GraphRAG/RAPTOR/LightRAG style summarisation pipelines. No GPU is required if you use OpenAI embeddings (`text-embedding-3-small`) and an API LLM, but the paper results use NV-Embed-v2 (7B, GPU). + +Memory: all three embedding matrices plus the igraph live in RAM at query time. + +## 9. Configuration and extension points + +* **Config object**: `utils/config_utils.py::BaseConfig` dataclass (~70 fields). Constructor kwargs of `HippoRAG(...)` (`llm_model_name`, `llm_base_url`, `embedding_model_name`, `embedding_base_url`, Azure fields, `embedding_provider`, `llm_api_key_env`, `embedding_api_key_env`, `index_identity`) override the config; MCP accepts `--config KEY=VALUE`. +* **Swap LLM**: `llm/__init__.py::_get_llm_class()` routes by model name prefix: gateway prefixes (`orcarouter/`, `atlascloud/` in `llm/gateways.py`), `bedrock-mantle/` (`BedrockMantleLLM`), `bedrock/` (LiteLLM `BedrockLLM`), `Transformers/` (`TransformersLLM`), else `CacheOpenAI` (OpenAI, Azure, vLLM, any OpenAI-compatible base URL). Or inject any `BaseLLM` subclass via `extraction_llm=` / `qa_llm=`. +* **Swap embeddings**: name-based routing or `embedding_provider` (`openai|transformers|vllm|gritlm|nvembed|contriever|cohere`), or inject `embedding_model=BaseEmbeddingModel`. +* **Swap storage**: `vector_store_type`; graph is igraph only. +* **Prompts**: `prompts/prompt_template_manager.py::PromptTemplateManager` loads every module in `prompts/templates/` exposing a `prompt_template` list; add a file to add a template (see `templates/README.md`). Filter prompt via `rerank_dspy_file_path`. +* **Chunking**: inject `text_preprocessor=`. +* **Incremental update**: `index()` can be called repeatedly; chunk hashes, OpenIE results and embeddings are reused, synonymy KNN only runs for new entities, `add_new_edges` merges weights. `delete(docs)` removes chunks, decrements `fact_source_counts`, drops facts/entities that no longer have any source, and deletes vertices — all guarded by `StateConsistencyError` checks (missing provenance, legacy schema). `force_index_from_scratch` rebuilds the graph from stored embeddings/OpenIE; `force_openie_from_scratch` is only allowed in an empty index. +* **Serving**: `hipporag-mcp` (stdio or Streamable HTTP, `--read_only`), Claude Code plugin under `plugins/hipporag/`. + +## 10. Benchmarks reported by the authors + +The repository itself contains no result tables; numbers below are from the HippoRAG 2 paper (ICML 2025) as summarised in the README figure and from recollection of the paper — treat exact decimals as "verify against the paper". + +* **Setup**: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct as LLM, NV-Embed-v2 as retriever, datasets grouped as *factual memory* (NaturalQuestions, PopQA), *sense-making* (NarrativeQA), *associativity* (MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, HotpotQA, LV-Eval). 1,000-question samples; QA F1 and passage recall@5. +* **Headline claim**: HippoRAG 2 beats NV-Embed-v2 dense retrieval, GraphRAG, LightRAG, RAPTOR and HippoRAG 1 on average, with the largest gains on multi-hop sets (roughly +7 F1 average over the strongest dense baseline on associativity tasks) while *not* regressing on simple factual QA where HippoRAG 1 and other graph methods did regress. Reported average F1 across the seven sets is about 60 for HippoRAG 2 vs mid-50s for NV-Embed-v2; LightRAG and GraphRAG were below dense retrieval on most QA sets in their runs. +* **Efficiency claim**: offline indexing ~2 LLM calls per passage vs. community-summarisation pipelines; online cost comparable to dense retrieval plus one small filter call. +* Repo-side evaluation tooling: `main.py --dataset {sample,musique,2wikimultihopqa,hotpotqa,...}` under `reproduce/dataset`, HF dataset `osunlp/HippoRAG_2`; metrics via `evaluation/retrieval_eval.py` and `evaluation/qa_eval.py`. +* **Third-party**: Graph-R1's paper (LHRLAB) uses HippoRAG2 as a baseline and reports it as the strongest non-RL GraphRAG baseline on its six QA sets; LightRAG/GraphRAG-bench style comparisons generally reproduce HippoRAG 2 as competitive on multi-hop QA but note its reliance on a strong instruction-tuned embedding model. (Not read from this repo; flagged as external.) + +## 11. Strengths + +* Very low indexing cost for a graph method (two short extraction prompts per chunk, no community summarisation, no entity description merging). +* Retrieval is deterministic and cheap: one embedding, one small LLM filter, one PPR; latency is sub-second on mid-sized corpora once objects are loaded. +* Principled multi-hop behaviour through PPR over fact/passage/synonym edges, with dense retrieval as a floor (`passage_node_weight`) and as a fallback. +* Genuinely incremental and deletable index with provenance counts, manifests and consistency checks — unusual among research GraphRAG codebases. +* Broad provider support (OpenAI, Azure, Bedrock, Bedrock Mantle, gateways, vLLM, Transformers; OpenAI/Cohere/NV-Embed/GritLM/Contriever embeddings) and four vector stores. +* MCP server and Claude Code plugin make it directly usable as an agent memory tool. +* Tests exist and encode real regressions. + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +* **No chunker**: default preprocessor treats each document as one passage; long documents must be chunked by the caller. +* **Full in-memory scoring**: fact/passage/entity matrices are loaded into numpy and scored by dense dot product; the vector DB backends are only persistence. Memory and per-query cost grow linearly with corpus size. +* **Graph stored as a single pickle**; no concurrent writers; MCP serialises tool calls on one worker thread. +* **Predicates are dropped from the graph** — edges carry only counts/weights; relation semantics live only in fact embeddings. Queries that hinge on relation type rely on the fact-embedding stage. +* `linking_top_k=5` and "up to 4 facts" filter is aggressive; recall for questions with many relevant facts depends on the DSPy filter being right. Filter exceptions silently fall back to DPR. +* Entity nodes come only from triples; NER output is otherwise unused. +* QA prompt hard-codes `Wikipedia Title:` prefix and is tuned for MuSiQue-style short answers; no long-form or summarisation ("global") mode. +* Alpha versioning: `2.0.0a5` changed on-disk identity rules (`index_manifest.json`) — older indexes must be rebuilt. +* Heavy pinned dependencies (`torch==2.5.1`, `transformers==4.45.2`, `litellm==1.73.1`) make it awkward to co-install with other stacks. +* The headline results depend on a 7B instruction-tuned embedder (NV-Embed-v2); with `text-embedding-3-small` expect lower numbers (not quantified in repo). + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +Choose HippoRAG 2 when you need **multi-hop retrieval over a growing factual corpus** (docs, wikis, tickets, agent memory), want graph-level associativity *without* paying for GraphRAG-style summarisation, and can afford a decent embedding model. It is a good fit for an "agent long-term memory" component (MCP server, incremental `index`/`delete`). It is a poor fit for corpus-wide summarisation / thematic questions (no community or global mode), for very large corpora that cannot be held in RAM, or where relation semantics must be queried explicitly. + +## 14. Core idea in one paragraph + +HyperGraphRAG keeps LightRAG's whole pipeline (token chunking, one LLM extraction prompt with "gleaning", description merging, NetworkX + nano-vectordb storage, keyword-driven dual-level retrieval, CSV-table context, a single "rag_response" generation prompt) but changes the **unit of knowledge**: instead of extracting binary `(entity, relation, entity)` triples, the LLM is asked to split each chunk into *knowledge segments* — complete natural-language sentences ("hyper-relations") with a 0-10 completeness score — and then list the entities participating in each segment with a 0-100 importance score. Each segment becomes a **hyperedge node** (`role="hyperedge"`, name prefixed ``), each participant an **entity node** (`role="entity"`), and the hypergraph is stored as a **bipartite graph** hyperedge-node <-> entity-node in NetworkX. Retrieval runs the *same extraction prompt on the query* to get entity names (low-level keywords) and hyper-relation sentences (high-level keywords), vector-matches them against the entity and hyperedge vector stores, expands one hop across the bipartite graph, collects source chunks, and feeds entity/hyperedge/chunk tables to the LLM. The claim is that n-ary facts preserve complete context (e.g. a clinical guideline sentence with 4 participants) that binary triples fragment. + +## 3. Indexing pipeline, step by step + +Entry: `HyperGraphRAG.insert(string_or_strings)` -> `ainsert()` in `hypergraphrag/hypergraphrag.py` (lines ~270-340). Everything is `asyncio` with `limit_async_func_call` concurrency caps. + +### 3.1 Document and chunk dedup (LightRAG-inherited) +* Each document -> `doc-`; skipped if already in `full_docs` KV. +* `operate.py::chunking_by_token_size(content, overlap_token_size=100, max_token_size=1200, tiktoken_model="gpt-4o-mini")` — sliding tiktoken windows; chunk id `chunk-` with `{tokens, content, chunk_order_index, full_doc_id}`. Chunks already in `text_chunks` KV are skipped. +* `chunks_vdb.upsert(inserting_chunks)` embeds every chunk (namespace `chunks`), although the hybrid query path never reads `chunks_vdb` (it is only used by LightRAG's `naive` mode, which is no longer wired into `aquery`). + +### 3.2 Extraction: one prompt per chunk + gleaning (LightRAG mechanics, new schema) +`operate.py::extract_entities(chunks, knowledge_graph_inst, entity_vdb, hyperedge_vdb, global_config)`: + +1. Builds `PROMPTS["entity_extraction"]` (`hypergraphrag/prompt.py`) with delimiters `tuple_delimiter="<|>"`, `record_delimiter="##"`, `completion_delimiter="<|COMPLETE|>"`, language (`addon_params.language`, default English) and three long few-shot examples (`PROMPTS["entity_extraction_examples"]`, adapted from LightRAG's "Alex/Taylor/Jordan" and "Operation: Dulce" passages). The `entity_types` list (`DEFAULT_ENTITY_TYPES = organization, person, geo, event, category`) is computed but **commented out of the prompt context**, so the prompt text never mentions them; the model picks its own types (examples use `person`, `object`, `concept`, `role`, `location`, `event`, `action`). +2. Prompt steps: (1) "Divide the text into several complete knowledge segments … Format each as `("hyper-relation"<|><|>)`"; (2) "Identify all entities in each knowledge segment … `("entity"<|><|><|><|>)`"; (3) list everything separated by `##`; (4) end with `<|COMPLETE|>`. +3. **Gleaning loop** (`entity_extract_max_gleaning=2`): after the first completion, send `PROMPTS["entiti_continue_extraction"]` ("MANY knowdge fragements with entities were missed…") with the chat history, append output; then ask `PROMPTS["entiti_if_loop_extraction"]` ("Answer YES | NO …") and stop unless the reply is `yes`. Worst case 1 + 2x2 = 5 LLM calls per chunk; typical 3. +4. Parsing: records are split on `##`/`<|COMPLETE|>`, the parenthesised body split on `<|>`. `_handle_single_hyperrelation_extraction` turns a `"hyper-relation"` record into `{hyper_relation: ""+segment, weight: completeness (default 1.0), source_id: chunk}` and sets `now_hyper_relation`; each subsequent `"entity"` record (`_handle_single_entity_extraction`) is attached to that current hyper-relation with `weight = key_score` (default 50.0), `entity_name = clean_str(name).upper()`, `entity_type`, `description`. **Membership is purely positional**: an entity belongs to the most recent hyper-relation line above it. Entities emitted before any hyper-relation line are dropped (`now_hyper_relation == ""`). + +Concrete shape of one chunk's LLM output (delimiters as in the prompt; types are free-form): + +``` +("hyper-relation"<|>"Radio City is India's first private FM radio station and was started on 3 July 2001."<|>9)## +("entity"<|>"Radio City"<|>"organization"<|>"India's first private FM radio station."<|>95)## +("entity"<|>"India"<|>"geo"<|>"Country where Radio City operates."<|>80)## +("entity"<|>"3 July 2001"<|>"event"<|>"Launch date of Radio City."<|>70)## +("hyper-relation"<|>"It plays Hindi, English and regional songs."<|>7)## +("entity"<|>"Radio City"<|>"organization"<|>"Plays Hindi, English and regional songs."<|>90)## +<|COMPLETE|> +``` +This yields two hyperedge nodes (3 and 1 member entities), three entity nodes, and four incidence edges; the second description of `RADIO CITY` is appended to the first with ``. + +### 3.3 Merge and upsert (three passes) +* `_merge_hyperedges_then_upsert(hyperedge_name, …)` — graph node keyed by the full `sentence` string; attributes `role="hyperedge"`, `weight = sum(completeness scores)` (accumulates across re-extractions), `source_id` = ``-joined chunk ids. No LLM call. +* `_merge_nodes_then_upsert(entity_name, …)` — graph node keyed by upper-cased entity string; `role="entity"`, majority `entity_type`, `description` = ``-joined distinct descriptions, `source_id` union. If the joined description exceeds `entity_summary_to_max_tokens=500` tokens, `_handle_entity_relation_summary` calls the LLM with `PROMPTS["summarize_entity_descriptions"]` (LightRAG). The hyper-relation *weights* carried on entity records are not stored on the entity node. +* `_merge_edges_then_upsert(entity_name, …)` — for each `(hyper_relation, entity)` pair, upserts a bipartite edge `hyper_relation -> entity_name` with `weight = sum(key_score)` and `source_id`. Edge weights accumulate on repeated insertion of the same chunk content only if chunk dedup is bypassed; normally each pair is seen once. + +### 3.4 Vector stores +* `hyperedges_vdb` (namespace `hyperedges`, id `rel-`, `content = hyperedge_name` i.e. the ``-prefixed sentence, meta `hyperedge_name`). +* `entities_vdb` (namespace `entities`, id `ent-`, `content = entity_name + description`, meta `entity_name`). +* Embedding function default `llm.py::openai_embedding` (`text-embedding-3-small`, 1536-d) wrapped by `limit_async_func_call(embedding_func_max_async=16)`, batched by `embedding_batch_num=32`. Stored by `NanoVectorDBStorage` (`storage.py`) in `vdb_.json` under `working_dir`. + +### 3.5 Persistence +`_insert_done()` calls `index_done_callback()` on every storage: `JsonKVStorage` writes `kv_store_full_docs.json`, `kv_store_text_chunks.json`, `kv_store_llm_response_cache.json`; `NetworkXStorage` writes `graph_chunk_entity_relation.graphml`; nano-vectordb saves its JSON. + +On-disk layout of a `working_dir` after one insert (default backends): + +| File | Written by | Content | +|---|---|---| +| `kv_store_full_docs.json` | `JsonKVStorage` | `doc-: {content}` | +| `kv_store_text_chunks.json` | `JsonKVStorage` | `chunk-: {tokens, content, chunk_order_index, full_doc_id}` | +| `kv_store_llm_response_cache.json` | `JsonKVStorage` | prompt-hash -> LLM response (extraction, gleaning, summaries, answers) | +| `graph_chunk_entity_relation.graphml` | `NetworkXStorage` | bipartite hypergraph with `role` on nodes | +| `vdb_entities.json` | `NanoVectorDBStorage` | `ent-` vectors + `entity_name` | +| `vdb_hyperedges.json` | `NanoVectorDBStorage` | `rel-` vectors + `hyperedge_name` | +| `vdb_chunks.json` | `NanoVectorDBStorage` | `chunk-` vectors (never queried by `hybrid`) | +| `hypergraphrag.log` (cwd) | `set_logger` | run log | + +### 3.6 Flowchart + +```mermaid +flowchart TD + A[insert docs] --> B[doc-md5 dedup via full_docs KV] + B --> C[chunking_by_token_size 1200/100 tiktoken] + C --> D[chunks_vdb.upsert embed chunks] + C --> E[extract_entities per chunk

continue + YES/NO check} + F --> G[parse records on ## and <|>

LLM summary if >500 tokens] + G --> J[_merge_edges_then_upsert
