Graph data model + +Single NetworkX undirected graph (`NetworkXStorage`, namespace `chunk_entity_relation`) holding two node roles — the hypergraph is encoded as its **bipartite incidence graph**. + +| Node type | Node id | Attributes | +|---|---|---| +| Hyperedge node | `"" + knowledge segment text` | `role="hyperedge"`, `weight` (sum of completeness scores, 0-10 each), `source_id` (chunk ids joined by ``) | +| Entity node | upper-cased, `clean_str`'d entity name (the raw string, not a hash) | `role="entity"`, `entity_type`, `description` (``-joined, LLM-summarised past 500 tokens), `source_id` | + +| Edge | Endpoints | Attributes | +|---|---|---| +| Incidence edge | hyperedge node — entity node | `weight` (entity key_score, 0-100, summed), `source_id` | + +There are **no entity-entity edges** and no typed relations; the "relation" is the free-text sentence itself. Arity is unbounded (an entity list under one hyper-relation line). Entities are keyed by exact normalised string, so no entity resolution beyond upper-casing is performed. Because hyperedge node ids are whole sentences, two near-identical segments produce two hyperedges. + +Vector-side records: `ent-` and `rel-` in nano-vectordb, `chunk-` in `chunks_vdb` (unused in query), text chunks in KV. + +## 5. Storage backends supported + +Inherited verbatim from LightRAG (`hypergraphrag/kg/*`), selected by string name in `HyperGraphRAG(kv_storage=…, vector_storage=…, graph_storage=…)` via `_get_storage_class()`: + +| Role | Implementations | Default | +|---|---|---| +| KV (docs, chunks, LLM cache) | `JsonKVStorage`, `OracleKVStorage`, `MongoKVStorage`, `TiDBKVStorage` | `JsonKVStorage` (one JSON file per namespace) | +| Vector (entities, hyperedges, chunks) | `NanoVectorDBStorage`, `OracleVectorDBStorage`, `MilvusVectorDBStorge` (sic), `ChromaVectorDBStorage`, `TiDBVectorDBStorage` | `NanoVectorDBStorage` (`nano-vectordb`, brute-force cosine, `cosine_better_than_threshold=0.2`) | +| Graph | `NetworkXStorage`, `Neo4JStorage`, `OracleGraphStorage` | `NetworkXStorage` (GraphML file) | + +Caveats seen in code: `NanoVectorDBStorage.delete_relation()` filters records by `src_id`/`tgt_id` fields that hyperedge records do not have (they have `content`/`hyperedge_name`), so `delete_by_entity()` will not remove hyperedge vectors — a LightRAG leftover. `node2vec` embedding hooks exist on `NetworkXStorage` but `base.py` raises `NotImplementedError("Node embedding is not used in hypergraphrag.")`. The non-default backends were not adapted for the `role` attribute and were not exercised by the authors (no examples/tests). + +## 6. Query / retrieval modes + +Entry: `HyperGraphRAG.query(query, QueryParam)` -> `aquery()` -> `operate.py::kg_query()`. Only `mode="hybrid"` is dispatched in `aquery` (LightRAG's `local`, `global`, `naive` branches were removed; `QueryParam.mode` still lists them and `_build_query_context` still contains the branching, but `aquery` never calls `kg_query` for anything but `hybrid`, so non-hybrid modes silently return `None`). The `evaluation/` copy relaxes this to `["hybrid","global","local"]`. + +### 6.1 Steps in `kg_query` +1. **Cache check** via `handle_cache(hashing_kv, args_hash, query, mode)` (LightRAG; optional embedding-similarity cache governed by `embedding_cache_config`, off by default). +2. **Query decomposition with the extraction prompt** — the very same `PROMPTS["entity_extraction"]` is applied to the *question* text (1 LLM call, no gleaning). Parsed `"hyper-relation"` records become **high-level keywords** (`"" + segment`), `"entity"` records become **low-level keywords** (upper-cased names). If either list is empty the function returns `PROMPTS["fail_response"]` ("Sorry, I'm not able to provide an answer…"). Note this replaces LightRAG's `keywords_extraction` JSON prompt; that prompt is still present in `prompt.py` but unused. +3. **Context building** `_build_query_context([ll_keywords, hl_keywords], …)`: + * **Entity side** `_get_node_data(ll_keywords, …)`: `entities_vdb.query(ll_keywords_joined, top_k=QueryParam.top_k=60)` (one embedding of the comma-joined names), fetch node data + `node_degree` as `rank`; `_find_most_related_text_unit_from_entities` collects chunks from the entities' `source_id`s, boosting chunks also referenced by one-hop neighbour nodes (`relation_counts`), ordered by (entity rank order, -relation_counts), truncated to `max_token_for_text_unit=4000` tokens; `_find_most_related_edges_from_entities` gathers all incident edges, sorts by `(edge_degree, weight)` desc, truncates by `max_token_for_global_context=4000` on the hyperedge text, and for each hyperedge lists all its member entities (`related_nodes = "A|B|C"`). + * **Hyperedge side** `_get_edge_data(hl_keywords, …)`: `hyperedges_vdb.query(hl_keywords_joined, top_k=60)`; fetch hyperedge nodes; `rank = vector distance`; sort by `(distance, weight)`; truncate by hyperedge text length to 4000 tokens; attach member entities; `_find_most_related_entities_from_relationships` pulls those entities (truncated by `max_token_for_local_context=4000` on descriptions); `_find_related_text_unit_from_relationships` pulls source chunks (4000 tokens). + * `combine_contexts` dedups and merges both sides into three CSV tables: `Entities (id, entity, type, description)`, `Relationships (id, hyperedge, related_entities)`, `Sources (id, content)`. +4. `only_need_context=True` returns the CSV context string (used by the evaluation scripts); `only_need_prompt=True` returns the filled system prompt. +5. **Generation** (section 7) and `save_to_cache`. + +### 6.2 Sequence diagram + +```mermaid +sequenceDiagram + participant U as Caller + participant Q as kg_query + participant L as LLM + participant EV as entities_vdb + participant HV as hyperedges_vdb + participant G as NetworkX bipartite graph + participant KV as text_chunks KV + U->>Q: query(text, mode=hybrid) + Q->>L: entity_extraction prompt on the question + L-->>Q: hyper-relation lines (hl) + entity lines (ll) + par low level + Q->>EV: query(ll joined, top_k=60) + EV-->>Q: entity names + Q->>G: get_node, node_degree, get_node_edges + Q->>KV: chunks from entity source_ids + and high level + Q->>HV: query(hl joined, top_k=60) + HV-->>Q: hyperedge names + Q->>G: get_node, get_node_edges -> member entities + Q->>KV: chunks from hyperedge source_ids + end + Q->>Q: truncate each table to 4000 tokens, combine_contexts + Q->>L: rag_response system prompt + query + L-->>U: markdown answer +``` + +### 6.3 Ranking and budgets +* Vector similarity decides the candidate set; graph degree and accumulated weights decide ordering inside the candidate set. There is no PageRank or multi-hop traversal beyond one hop across the bipartite graph (entity -> its hyperedges -> their entities). +* Token budgets (tiktoken, `gpt-4o-mini` encoder): 4000 each for entities, hyperedges, chunks on *each* of the two sides before combination, so the final prompt can reach ~20k+ tokens. +* `top_k=60` on both vector queries. `cosine_better_than_threshold=0.2` filters weak matches. + +## 7. Generation / answer synthesis + +`PROMPTS["rag_response"]` (LightRAG's, unchanged): "You are a helpful assistant responding to questions about data in the tables provided … Generate a response of the target length and format … incorporating any relevant general knowledge. If you don't know the answer, just say so … Style the response in markdown." `response_type` default `"Multiple Paragraphs"`. The LLM call is `llm_model_func(query, system_prompt=sys_prompt, stream=…)`; the response is post-processed by stripping the prompt text if it was echoed (an `hf_model` artefact). A commented-out alternative prompt tuned for "semantic alignment with expected answers" is left in `prompt.py`, suggesting the paper's evaluation used stricter wording in the `evaluation/` copy (not verified here). + +The evaluation harness (`evaluation/script_hypergraphrag.py`) retrieves context only (`QueryParam(only_need_context=True)`) and `evaluation/get_generation.py` generates with `gpt-4o-mini` using its own prompt, so paper generation quality is decoupled from the library's `rag_response` prompt. + +No training anywhere. + +## 8. LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +| Phase | LLM calls | Embedding calls | +|---|---|---| +| Index, per 1200-token chunk | 1 extraction + up to 2 gleaning + up to 1 YES/NO check = 3 typical, 5 max; plus occasional `summarize_entity_descriptions` when an entity's merged description exceeds 500 tokens | 1 chunk embedding + 1 per new hyperedge + 1 per new/updated entity (dozens per chunk; every hyperedge sentence is embedded) | +| Query | 1 (extraction prompt on question) + 1 (answer) | 2 (entity keywords string, hyperedge keywords string) | + +Defaults: `gpt_4o_mini_complete` and `openai_embedding` (`text-embedding-3-small`); `llm_model_max_async=16`, `embedding_func_max_async=16`; LLM cache (`enable_llm_cache=True`) keyed by prompt hash in `kv_store_llm_response_cache.json`. The extraction prompt is long (three multi-hundred-token examples) so input tokens per chunk are ~4-5k on top of the chunk. Compared with LightRAG the per-chunk cost is similar; compared with HippoRAG it is noticeably higher (more and longer calls, many more embedded strings). No GPU needed with API models; `hf_model_complete`/`hf_embedding`/`ollama_*`/`lmdeploy` paths exist for local models. + +## 9. Configuration and extension points + +* All settings are fields of the `HyperGraphRAG` dataclass (`working_dir`, `chunk_token_size=1200`, `chunk_overlap_token_size=100`, `tiktoken_model_name`, `entity_extract_max_gleaning=2`, `entity_summary_to_max_tokens=500`, `embedding_func`, `embedding_batch_num`, `embedding_func_max_async`, `llm_model_func`, `llm_model_name` (only used by HF path), `llm_model_max_token_size=32768`, `llm_model_max_async`, `llm_model_kwargs`, `enable_llm_cache`, `addon_params` (`language`, `entity_types`, `example_number`), `embedding_cache_config`, `vector_db_storage_cls_kwargs`). +* **Swap LLM**: pass any `async def f(prompt, system_prompt=None, history_messages=[], **kwargs) -> str` as `llm_model_func`; ready-made: `gpt_4o_complete`, `gpt_4o_mini_complete`, `azure_openai_complete`, `bedrock_complete`, `hf_model_complete`, `ollama_model_complete`, `zhipu_complete`, `nvidia_openai_complete`, `lmdeploy_model_if_cache`, plus `MultiModel` round-robin (all in `llm.py`, LightRAG). +* **Swap embeddings**: `embedding_func=EmbeddingFunc(embedding_dim, max_token_size, func)`; providers `openai_embedding`, `azure_openai_embedding`, `bedrock_embedding`, `hf_embedding`, `ollama_embedding`, `jina_embedding`, `zhipu_embedding`, `siliconcloud_embedding`, `nvidia_openai_embedding`. +* **Swap storage**: string names in section 5; `vector_db_storage_cls_kwargs` for backend params; env vars for Neo4j/Oracle/Milvus/Mongo/TiDB as in LightRAG. +* **Prompts**: edit `PROMPTS` dict in `prompt.py` (module-level, no injection API). +* **Custom KG**: `insert_custom_kg(custom_kg)` (LightRAG) still exists but expects binary `relationships` with `src_id/tgt_id`, not hyperedges — unclear whether it produces a consistent hypergraph; treat as unsupported. +* **Incremental update**: `insert()` is append-only and idempotent at doc/chunk hash level; new chunks' entities merge into existing nodes (description concatenation + summarisation), hyperedges with identical text merge weights. `delete_by_entity(name)` removes an entity node and its vector (and, buggy, attempts to remove hyperedge vectors); there is no document-level delete and no removal of orphaned hyperedge nodes. Changing the chunk size or prompt after indexing silently mixes schemas. + +## 10. Benchmarks reported by the authors + +From `evaluation/README.md` and the paper (numbers not stored in the repo): + +* **Domains / datasets**: five corpora built by the authors — `hypertension` (medicine: clinical guideline text), `agriculture`, `cs`, `legal`, and `mix`; contexts and question sets are distributed via Terabox, not in the repo. Questions are LLM-generated QA pairs with gold answers. +* **Baselines**: NaiveGeneration (no retrieval), StandardRAG (chunk dense retrieval), GraphRAG, LightRAG, PathRAG, HippoRAG2 (listed in the paper; only `script_standardrag.py` and `script_naivegeneration.py` are in the repo). +* **Metrics** (`evaluation/get_score.py`, `eval_r.py`, `eval_g.py`): answer F1 (`cal_f1`), **R-Sim** (SimCSE `princeton-nlp/sup-simcse-roberta-large` cosine between retrieved knowledge and gold answer), and a **G-E generation score** = average of an LLM-judge 0-100 rating over seven rubrics (`comprehensiveness, knowledgeability, correctness, relevance, diversity, logical_coherence, factuality`) blended with F1 (`(score + f1)/2`). Judge is `gpt-4o-mini` via the apiyi proxy. +* **Headline**: the paper reports HyperGraphRAG as best on average across the five domains on F1, R-Sim and the generation score, with the largest margins over LightRAG/GraphRAG in medicine and legal (multi-entity guideline sentences), and shows that retrieval cost per query is in the same range as LightRAG hybrid mode. Exact table values are in the NeurIPS paper; the repo stores none, and the figure `figs/F1.png` referenced by the README is not in this clone. +* **Third-party**: Graph-R1 (same group) reuses this exact extraction schema and reports HyperGraphRAG-style retrieval as a strong non-RL baseline. Independent reproductions were not found in the repo. Strengths + +* **n-ary knowledge units**: a whole sentence with all participants is retrievable as one object, so multi-entity constraints (dose + population + condition + outcome) are not broken into lossy binary triples. +* Dual retrieval channel: entity-side (specific names) and hyperedge-side (whole propositions) are matched independently and combined, similar to LightRAG local+global but with semantically richer "global" units. +* Reuses LightRAG's mature plumbing: async batching, LLM cache, pluggable KV/vector/graph backends, multilingual `addon_params.language`. +* Simple on-disk artefacts (JSON + GraphML) that are easy to inspect and post-process; `kv_store_hyperedges.json` is directly reusable (Graph-R1 does exactly that). +* Query-time cost is bounded (2 LLM calls, 2 embeddings, one-hop graph lookups). + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +* **Positional membership parsing**: hyperedge membership depends on the LLM listing entities immediately after each hyper-relation line; any reordering silently reassigns entities. No JSON/structured output. +* Hyperedge node ids are the raw sentence string — no dedup/merging of paraphrases, so the hyperedge store grows ~linearly with chunk count and vector search over it dominates query cost at scale (`nano-vectordb` is brute force). +* No entity resolution beyond upper-casing; descriptions grow by concatenation then get LLM-summarised (lossy, extra cost). +* The query-time "keyword" extraction uses the full document-extraction prompt (with three long examples) on a one-line question; it returns `fail_response` if the model produces no hyper-relation or no entity for the question — brittle for short factoid queries. +* Only `hybrid` mode is reachable from `aquery()`; `local`/`global`/`naive` are dead code in the main package (differs in the `evaluation/` copy). +* `delete_by_entity` cannot delete hyperedge vectors (field mismatch), no document-level deletion, no index manifest; incremental re-chunking is unsafe. +* Context can reach ~24k tokens (six 4000-token budgets); no reranking of chunks beyond order/degree heuristics. +* Inherited LightRAG code paths (`insert_custom_kg`, node2vec, non-default DBs) are untested with the `role`-based schema; `chunks_vdb` embeddings are computed but never queried. +* Evaluation harness hard-codes a paid third-party API proxy and Terabox downloads; the `evaluation/hypergraphrag` copy diverges from the main package, so paper numbers may not match the library defaults. +* No tests, no packaging, squashed history, typos in prompt keys (`entiti_continue_extraction`, `MilvusVectorDBStorge`). + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +Choose HyperGraphRAG when your corpus is dominated by **dense, multi-participant factual statements** — clinical guidelines, regulations, contracts, technical specs — where you want the retrieved unit to be the full proposition and you are already comfortable with a LightRAG-style stack (OpenAI models, JSON/GraphML files, modest corpus size). It is also the right starting point if you plan to build Graph-R1-style agentic retrieval over a hypergraph. Avoid it for large corpora (brute-force vector search over every extracted sentence), for workloads that need deletion/updates, or for production use without first adding structured-output parsing and tests. + +## 14. Core idea in one paragraph + +KAG treats RAG as "knowledge base + logical reasoning", not vector search. At build time it runs a configurable **builder chain** (scanner → reader → splitter → one or more extractors → vectorizer → post-processor → writer) that turns documents into `SubGraph`s conforming to an **SPG schema** (typed entities, events, concepts with properties and indexed fields), always attaching a `Chunk` node and `source` edges so graph and text are **mutually indexed**. Extraction can be schema-free (LLM NER/standardisation/triples into a generic ontology), schema-constrained (NER, relations and events restricted to your domain schema), or one of several lighter "index" extractors (chunk-only, summary, outline, atomic query, knowledge unit, table). Everything is written to the OpenSPG server (Neo4j + its own vector/text index) or, for benchmarks, to an in-memory igraph/torch graph. At query time a **planner** LLM turns the question into a DAG of tasks expressed either as executor calls or as a **logical form** (`Retrieval(s=..., p=..., o=...)`, `Math(...)`, `Deduce(...)`, `Output(...)`); the hybrid retrieval executor resolves each `Retrieval` step through a flow of components — exact graph lookup (`kg_cs`), fuzzy graph + Personalised-PageRank chunk retrieval (`kg_fr`), vector chunk retrieval (`rc`), plus summary/outline/atomic-query/table retrievers — merges and summarises them, while Math (LLM-generated Python) and Deduce (judgement/entailment/extract/choice prompts) executors handle computation and inference; a generator produces a thought-then-answer with `` citations. Static mode plans once (with optional retry if the answer is "unknown"); iterative mode re-plans after each step; `kag_model_planner` targets the fine-tuned KAG-Thinker model. + +## 3. Graph / tree data model + +- **Schema (SPG)**: declared per project in a `.schema` DSL file (`kag/templates/schema/{{default}}.schema.tmpl`, `kag/examples/*/schema/*.schema`) and committed with `knext schema commit`. Each property declares a type (`Text`, `Integer`, another entity type for relations-as-properties) and optionally `index: Text | Vector | TextAndVector` and `constraint: MultiValue`. The default template ships 17 generic entity types (`Person`, `Organization`, `GeographicLocation`, `Works`, `Event`, `Medicine`, `Keyword`, `Others`, ...) each with `desc` (TextAndVector), `semanticType → SemanticConcept`, `synonyms`, `officialName`. +- **SubGraph** (`kag/interface/common/model/sub_graph.py`): `Node(id, name, label, properties)` and `Edge(from_id, from_type, to_id, to_type, label, properties)`; `to_dict()` is what the writer sends. Generation / answer synthesis + +- Generators: `llm_generator`, `llm_index_generator` (adds `chunk_reranker`), `kag_model_generator`, `mock_generator`. +- Prompts (`kag/solver/prompt/`): `default_multi_hop_generator` ("Thought: ... Answer: ..." over documents + step-by-step breakdown), `default_refer_generator_prompt` (answer with citations ``, ids must exist in the reference list), `default_without_reference_generator`, `default_thought_then_answer` (per-sub-question summary), `context_select_prompt`, `resp_generator`/`resp_reflector`/`resp_verifier`/`resp_judge` (older reflect-verify loop, now mostly unused by default configs), `solve_question*`, `summary_question`, `sub_question_summary`, `question_ner`. +- Reasoning loops: (1) planner-level – static re-plan when `finish_judger` says the answer is invalid (`max_iteration`); iterative pipeline re-plans each step; (2) executor-level – `Deduce` ops and `Math` code with error-feedback retries; `fuzzy_one_hop_select` uses an LLM to pick relations. Thought traces are emitted in `` (KAG-Thinker) or "Thought:" sections. +- Citations: yes, chunk-level ids in the reference prompt, resolved by the product UI to original documents ("linking generated content to original references" in 0.7 notes). The multi-hop benchmark prompt does not emit citations. +- Bilingual prompts (`template_zh`/`template_en`) selected by `project.language`; `biz_scene` (`default`, `medical`, ...) selects domain prompt variants via `init_prompt_with_fallback`. + +## 8. LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +**Indexing, per chunk** (default 500-token chunks): +- `schema_free_extractor`: 3 LLM calls (NER, triples, standardisation; the async path runs triples and std in parallel) + table-chunk calls. `schema_constraint_extractor`: 4 (NER, events, relations, std). `knowledge_unit_extractor`: 3 (NER, knowledge units, triples) with the KU prompt producing large structured JSON. `naive_rag_extractor`/`chunk_extractor`: 0 LLM calls (vectors only) – the "lightweight build". `summary_extractor`, `atomic_query_extractor`, `outline_extractor`: +1 each if stacked. `outline_splitter`/`semantic_splitter` add per-document LLM calls. +- Embedding: one vector per `Vector`/`TextAndVector` property per node (name always; `desc`, `content`), batched 32 at a time; entity linking in the post-processor issues a vector search per node. +- Examples use `qwen2.5-72b-instruct` for extraction and a 7B `ner_llm` for fuzzy path selection; `BAAI/bge-m3` (1024-d) embeddings. + +**Query** (static LF pipeline with hybrid executor, typical 2–3 hop question): +- 1 planning call (+1 per re-plan); per Retrieval task: 1 rewrite call (if it references parents), `fuzzy_one_hop_select` LLM call(s) in `kg_fr`, 1 `context_select` call (if `with_llm_select`), 1 `thought_then_answer` summary (if `enable_summary`); per Math task 1–3 code-generation calls; per Deduce task 1 call; 1 final generation call; optional `finish_judger` call. Expect roughly **6–15 LLM calls** for a 3-step plan. Iterative pipeline: +1 planning call per step. +- Embedding calls: question + each sub/rewritten query (linking, `rc`, rerank). +- Graph ops: entity-linking vector searches, one-hop expansions and a PPR per Retrieval step – server-side on OpenSPG/Neo4j; igraph in memory mode. + +## 9. Configuration and extension points + +- **Everything is a registry** (`kag/common/registry/registrable.py::Registrable`): components declare `@X.register("name")` and are built from YAML/HOCON via `from_config({"type": ...})`. Project config `kag_config.yaml` (sections `llm`, `vectorize_model`, `vectorizer`, `project.{namespace, host_addr, id, biz_scene, language, ckpt_dir}`, `log`, `kag_builder_pipeline.{chain, scanner, num_chains, num_threads_per_chain}`, `kag_solver_pipeline.{type, planner, executors, generator, max_iteration}` plus arbitrary YAML anchors such as `kg_cs: &kg_cs`). `!ENV VAR` resolves secrets. `KAG_CONFIG` / `KAGConfigAccessor` give access at runtime; multiple task configs can coexist (`KAG_QA_TASK_CONFIG_KEY`). +- **Swap LLM / embeddings**: change `type` to `openai|maas|vllm|azure_openai|ollama` and `vectorize_model.type`; per-component overrides (`llm`, `ner_llm`, `llm_client`, `vectorize_model`) are supported since every component takes them as constructor args. +- **Swap prompts**: register a `PromptABC` subclass with `template_en/zh`, `template_variables`, `parse_response`, and reference it by `type`; `init_prompt_with_fallback(name, biz_scene)` resolves `example__` → `default_`. +- **Schema**: edit `schema/.schema`, `knext schema commit`; `knext project create/restore/update/list` (`knext/command/sub_command/project.py`). Changing the schema requires re-extraction for affected types. +- **Storage**: `writer.type` (`kg_writer` vs `memory_graph_writer`), `search_api.type` / `graph_api.type` (`openspg_*` vs `memory_*`). +- **Retrieval**: compose `retrievers:` lists and `merger`, or the `flow` string for the legacy executor; `kag/indexer/kag_index_manager.py` auto-builds matching extractor+retriever configs per index type. +- **Incremental update**: chunk-level resumability via checkpoints; the writer is an **upsert** (`AlterOperationEnum.Upsert`) so re-running the builder on new files adds to the existing OpenSPG graph without rebuilding (entities are keyed by name, so the same name merges). Deletion is supported by `KGWriter(delete=True)` / `operation=DELETE` on a subgraph. There is no automatic re-summarisation layer to invalidate (no communities), which makes incremental ingestion simpler than community-based GraphRAGs. The memory-graph path is rebuilt from the checkpoint directory on load. +- **CLI**: `knext` (`project`, `schema`, `builder`, `reasoner`, `thinker`) and `kag` (`builder`, `benchmark`, `info`, `mcp_server`). +- **Templates**: `kag/templates/project` scaffolds `builder/indexer.py`, `solver/`, `schema/`, prompts. + +## 10. Benchmarks reported by the authors + +- Repo (`docs/release_notes.md`, Oct 2024 release): KAG "significantly better than NaiveRAG, HippoRAG": **F1 relatively improved by 19.6 on HotpotQA and 33.5 on 2Wiki**. 0.7 notes: `open_benchmark/` "comparing various RAG methods under the same base to achieve SOTA"; "Lightweight Build" reduces construction token cost by 89%. +- Paper (arXiv:2409.13731; these tables are not reproduced anywhere in the repo, so verify against the current arXiv version before quoting): KAG reports end-to-end EM/F1 in the region of HotpotQA ~62/76, 2WikiMultiHopQA ~69/77, MuSiQue ~36/49, which it presents as several F1 points above HippoRAG+IRCoT and far above NaiveRAG with the same base model, together with retrieval-recall ablations showing the mutual-index and knowledge-alignment components each contribute. Two in-house Ant Group deployments (E-Government and E-Health Q&A) are reported with large "professionalism" gains over NaiveRAG as judged by human/LLM raters. Treat all of these as author-reported. +- Reproduction kits: `kag/open_benchmark/{hotpotqa,2wiki,musique}` (subsets `data/sub_corpus.json`, `qa_sub.json`, configs for `chunk`, `graph`, `summary`, `atomic_query`, `knowledge_unit`, `simple` index variants, `benchmark.sh`, EM/F1 via `kag/common/benchmarks/evaluate.py` and an LLM judger), plus `AffairQA` (government affairs, Chinese) and `prqa`. +- Third-party: GraphRAG-Bench / HippoRAG2 / other 2025 papers report KAG as competitive but expensive to run; results vary widely with the LLM used and are not in this repo. + +## 11. Strengths + +- **Schema-aware, typed knowledge**: real SPG schema with entity/event/concept types, property indexes, constraints, and schema-constrained extraction – suitable for regulated or expert domains where open IE noise is unacceptable. +- **Mutual indexing of graph and text** built into every extractor (Chunk nodes + `source` edges), with retrieval that moves both ways (entity linking → PPR → chunks; chunks → one-hop graph). +- **Logical-form planning** gives explicit, inspectable multi-step plans mixing retrieval, computation (real Python) and deduction; DAG execution runs independent sub-questions in parallel. +- **Multiple index types** (chunk, summary, outline, atomic query, knowledge unit, table, SPO graph) selectable per knowledge base with matching retrievers; lightweight modes exist when you cannot afford full extraction. +- **Production features**: resumable checkpointed builds, upsert/delete writes, product UI with streaming reasoning and citations, MCP server, Ollama/vLLM/Azure support, bilingual prompts, Docker deployment. +- Apache-2.0, versioned releases, active maintenance by a large org. + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +- **Deployment weight**: requires the OpenSPG Java server stack (OpenSPG + Neo4j + MySQL + MinIO via Docker Compose, ~several GB) even for schema loading in the Python toolkit; project/schema lifecycle is managed through `knext` REST calls. No standalone pure-Python mode except the benchmark-oriented `memory_graph` path, which still expects a server for schema. +- **Complexity and churn**: two generations of solver (0.7 `flow` components registered as `*_legacy`, 0.8 `retrievers`+`merger`), many near-duplicate prompts (`solve_question`, `solve_question_without_docs`, `resp_*`), config files with dozens of anchors; the learning curve is steep and docs live mainly on Yuque (partly Chinese). +- **LLM cost**: 3–4 extraction calls per chunk in graph modes; query-time plans trigger many calls (rewrite, fuzzy path select, context select, summaries, generation). Full-graph build of a large corpus is expensive; the authors added lightweight modes for this reason. +- **Vector search tied to OpenSPG/Neo4j**: no Milvus/Qdrant/pgvector; Neo4j vector/text indexes limit scale and multi-tenancy. +- **Entity identity by name**: `SubGraph` node ids are entity names; no global entity resolution beyond standardisation prompts and similarity linking at threshold 0.9. +- **KAG-Thinker weights are not open** in this repo; `kag_model_planner` is only usable with the model served elsewhere. +- **English support is secondary**: prompts have `template_en`, but examples, Yuque docs, logs, and some comments are Chinese-first; `biz_scene` prompt packs exist mainly for Chinese medical/government scenes. +- Error handling often falls back silently (e.g. `finish_judger` returns False on exception, `mock` components) and several code paths print debugging output. +- No community/global-summary layer, so "summarise the whole corpus" questions depend on the `summary`/`outline` indexes rather than hierarchical community reports. + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +- Enterprise, vertical-domain knowledge bases (finance, government, healthcare, telecom – the `examples/` set) where you own a schema, need typed facts, numerical/logical reasoning steps, citations, and can run a server stack. +- Multi-hop factual QA with explicit planning and mixed retrieval/calculation, where exact-match graph lookups (IDs, codes, regulations) matter alongside text retrieval. +- Teams already in the Ant/Alibaba ecosystem (DashScope, ODPS, SLS scanners) or needing Chinese-language strength. +- Not a fit for: lightweight or embedded use, laptops without Docker, quick prototypes, corpora without a meaningful schema, or teams wanting a single-process Python library (compare LightRAG/nano-graphrag). If you only need chunk retrieval with summaries, its lightweight modes work but do not justify the server. + +## 14. The version documented here is far ahead of that snapshot: the monolithic `lightrag.py` was split into mixins (`_RoleLLMMixin`, `_StorageMigrationMixin`, `_PipelineMixin`), the extraction prompt moved to a system/user split with record caps, multimodal parsing (MinerU/Docling/native DOCX) was added, and the query pipeline was rewritten as a four-stage search/truncate/merge/build architecture. + +## 2. Core idea in one paragraph + +LightRAG chunks documents, has an LLM extract `(entity, type, description)` and `(source, target, keywords, description)` records from each chunk, merges those records into a single entity-relation graph (descriptions concatenated and, when they pile up, re-summarised by the LLM), and embeds three things into vector stores: entities, relations and raw chunks. At query time one small LLM call turns the question into *low-level keywords* (specific entities) and *high-level keywords* (themes); low-level keywords are matched against the entity vector index (local), high-level keywords against the relation vector index (global), and in `mix` mode the raw query is also matched against chunks. The graph is then used only one hop out: entities pull their incident edges, edges pull their endpoint nodes, and both pull the chunks recorded in their `source_id` provenance field. Everything is token-budgeted, optionally reranked, serialised to JSON blocks and handed to a single answer-generation LLM call that must cite `[n]` reference ids. + +## 3. Indexing pipeline, step by step + +### 3.1 Ingestion and document status + +- Entry points: `LightRAG.ainsert()` (`lightrag/lightrag.py:2310`) and the REST `/documents/*` routes. Both delegate to the mixin in `lightrag/pipeline.py`: `apipeline_enqueue_documents()` (line 740: hash ids with `compute_mdhash_id(..., prefix="doc-")`, dedupe, write `DocStatus.PENDING` rows) then `apipeline_process_enqueue_documents()` (line 1724), which runs a feeder plus three worker pools: `_parse_worker` → `_analyze_worker` (VLM) → `_process_worker` → `process_single_document()` (line 4991). +- `DocStatus` (`lightrag/base.py:1317`): `PENDING → PARSING → ANALYZING → PROCESSING → PROCESSED | FAILED`. +- Parsing engines (`lightrag/parser/routing.py`): `legacy`, `native` (markdown + DOCX with "smart heading" detection, `parser/docx/`), `mineru`, `docling` (HTTP adapters in `parser/external/`). Build the system prompt from `PROMPTS["entity_extraction_system_prompt"]` (or the `_json_` variant when `entity_extraction_use_json` / `ENTITY_EXTRACTION_USE_JSON=true`). Graph data model + +- **Node** (one per entity name; `operate.py:2254`, `3166`): `entity_id`, `entity_type` (string from the guidance list or `UNKNOWN`), `description` (``-joined or summarised), `source_id` (``-joined chunk ids), `file_path` (``-joined), `created_at`, `truncate` marker. Backends that support labels (Neo4j, Memgraph) use `entity_type` as a label. +- **Edge** (undirected in intent; stored once per sorted pair): `weight` (float, summed relationship strength / defaults 1.0), `description`, `keywords`, `source_id`, `file_path`, `created_at`. `utils_graph.py` enforces `validate_relation_weight`, `apply_relation_weight_floor`, rejects self-loops. +- **No chunk nodes, no community nodes, no document nodes.** Chunks are linked to entities/relations only through the `source_id` attribute and the `entity_chunks` / `relation_chunks` KV tables. This is what keeps the graph cheap, and also what limits traversal to one hop in practice. +- Node and edge descriptions are capped and tagged when truncated (`_truncate_vdb_content`). +- Graph is exported/visualised with `aexport_data()`, `get_knowledge_graph` (BFS capped at `MAX_GRAPH_NODES=1000`), and the WebUI. + +## 5. Storage backends supported + +Registry: `lightrag/kg/__init__.py` (`STORAGE_IMPLEMENTATIONS`, `STORAGES`, `STORAGE_ENV_REQUIREMENTS`), resolved by `kg/factory.py::get_storage_class()`. Four storage *types*, selected via the `LightRAG(kv_storage=..., vector_storage=..., graph_storage=..., doc_status_storage=...)` fields or `KV_STORAGE` / `VECTOR_STORAGE` / `GRAPH_STORAGE` / `DOC_STATUS_STORAGE` env vars. + +| Type | Default | Other implementations | +|---|---|---| +| KV (`full_docs`, `text_chunks`, `llm_response_cache`, `entity_chunks`, `relation_chunks`, …) | `JsonKVStorage` | `RedisKVStorage`, `PGKVStorage`, `MongoKVStorage`, `OpenSearchKVStorage` | +| Vector (`entities`, `relationships`, `chunks`) | `NanoVectorDBStorage` | `MilvusVectorDBStorage`, `PGVectorStorage` (pgvector), `FaissVectorDBStorage`, `QdrantVectorDBStorage`, `MongoVectorDBStorage` (Atlas Vector Search), `OpenSearchVectorDBStorage`, `NoopVectorDBStorage` (Chroma is commented out) | +| Graph (`chunk_entity_relation`) | `NetworkXStorage` (GraphML on disk) | `Neo4JStorage`, `PGTableGraphStorage` (plain tables + JSONB, recommended for Postgres), `PGGraphStorage` (Apache AGE), `MongoGraphStorage`, `MemgraphStorage`, `OpenSearchGraphStorage` | +| Doc status (`doc_status`) | `JsonDocStatusStorage` | `RedisDocStatusStorage`, `PGDocStatusStorage`, `MongoDocStatusStorage`, `OpenSearchDocStatusStorage` | + +Notes from the docs (`docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md` "Storage Types Supported"): the four defaults are in-memory with file persistence and are "not suitable for production"; PostgreSQL, MongoDB or OpenSearch can each serve all four types. `PGTableGraphStorage` is reported ~28x faster than AGE for `get_knowledge_graph` (PR #3103). `kg/shared_storage.py` provides cross-process locks and shared pipeline status for Gunicorn multi-worker deployments. `storage_migrations.py` and `tools/migrate_graph_storage.py` handle schema/backend migrations. Vector stores honour `cosine_better_than_threshold` (`COSINE_THRESHOLD`, default 0.2). + +## 6. Query / retrieval modes + +`QueryParam` (`lightrag/base.py:90`): `mode ∈ {local, global, hybrid, naive, mix, bypass}` (default **`mix`**), `top_k` (40), `chunk_top_k` (20), `max_entity_tokens` (6000), `max_relation_tokens` (8000), `max_total_tokens` (30000), `hl_keywords` / `ll_keywords` (pre-supplied keywords skip the LLM), `conversation_history`, `user_prompt`, `enable_rerank` (default true via `RERANK_BY_DEFAULT`), `include_references`, `only_need_context`, `only_need_prompt`, `stream`, `response_type`. + +Dispatch is in `LightRAG.aquery_llm()` (`lightrag.py:5114`): `local/global/hybrid/mix → operate.kg_query()`, `naive → operate.naive_query()`, `bypass → LLM only, no retrieval`. `aquery_data()` returns the structured retrieval result without generation. + +### 6.1 Keyword extraction + +`get_keywords_from_query()` → `extract_keywords_only()` (`operate.py:4975/5112`) calls the **keyword** role with `PROMPTS["keywords_extraction"]`, which must return `{"high_level_keywords": [...], "low_level_keywords": [...]}`. Results are cached (`cache_type="keywords"`). If both lists are empty and the query is < 50 chars, the query itself becomes the low-level keyword; otherwise `fail_response` is returned. + +### 6.2 Search stage (`_perform_kg_search`, `operate.py:5280`) + +- Embeds the query, the joined LL keywords and the joined HL keywords in **one batched embedding call**. +- `local`: `_get_node_data(ll_keywords)` → `entities_vdb.query(top_k)` → batch-load nodes and degrees → `_find_most_related_edges_from_entities()` (all incident edges, sorted by `(edge degree, weight)` desc). +- `global`: `_get_edge_data(hl_keywords)` → `relationships_vdb.query(top_k)` → load edges + degrees → `_find_most_related_entities_from_relationships()` (endpoint nodes). +- `hybrid`: both; results are **round-robin interleaved** (local[0], global[0], local[1], …) and deduplicated by entity name / sorted pair. +- `mix`: hybrid plus `_get_vector_context()` = `chunks_vdb.query(query, top_k=chunk_top_k)`; vector chunks are tracked with `source="C"`. +- Entities are ranked by vector similarity (order preserved from the VDB); relations by `(rank=degree, weight)`. + +### 6.3 Truncate stage (`_apply_token_truncation`, line 5501) + +Entities are serialised (name, type, description, created_at, file_path) and truncated to `max_entity_tokens`; relations to `max_relation_tokens`. The surviving ordered lists (`filtered_entities`, `filtered_relations`) are what drive chunk selection, so truncation also prunes which chunks are considered. + +### 6.4 Chunk merge stage (`_merge_all_chunks`, line 5765) + +- `_find_related_text_unit_from_entities()` / `_find_related_text_unit_from_relations()` split every surviving node's/edge's `source_id` and pick chunks per entity group using `kg_chunk_pick_method` (`KG_CHUNK_PICK_METHOD`): `VECTOR` (default; rerank the candidate chunk ids by cosine similarity to the query embedding) or `WEIGHT` (linear-gradient weighted polling by occurrence count). Quota per group comes from `related_chunk_number` (`DEFAULT_RELATED_CHUNK_NUMBER=5`) via `_vector_chunk_quota`. +- Entity chunks, relation chunks and vector chunks are merged and deduplicated; `chunk_tracking` records `source` (`E`/`R`/`C`), `frequency`, `order` for debugging and the `raw_data` payload. + +### 6.5 Build stage (`_build_context_str`, line 5873) + +- Computes the system prompt token count, subtracts entity+relation context, query tokens and a 200-token buffer from `max_total_tokens`, and gives the remainder to chunks (`available_chunk_tokens`). +- `process_chunks_unified()` (`utils.py:7055`): dedupe → `chunk_top_k` cap → **rerank** (`apply_rerank_if_enabled`, provider in `lightrag/rerank.py`: Cohere, Jina, Ali/DashScope, generic OpenAI-style; `min_rerank_score`) → token truncation. +- `generate_reference_list_from_chunks()` assigns `[n]` reference ids per file path; `_attach_content_headings()` adds heading paths when `ENABLE_CONTENT_HEADINGS=true`. +- Final context uses `PROMPTS["kg_query_context"]`: three JSON blocks (`entities_str`, `relations_str`, `text_chunks_str`) plus a `Reference Document List`. + +### 6.6 Naive mode + +`naive_query()` (`operate.py:6852`): `chunks_vdb.query(query, top_k=chunk_top_k)` → `process_chunks_unified` (rerank + truncate against `max_total_tokens`) → `PROMPTS["naive_query_context"]` → `PROMPTS["naive_rag_response"]`. + +### 6.7 Sequence for `mix` mode + +```mermaid +sequenceDiagram + participant U as Caller + participant Q as kg_query + participant K as KEYWORD LLM + participant E as Embedding + participant V as Vector stores + participant G as Graph store + participant R as Reranker + participant L as QUERY LLM + U->>Q: aquery(query, mode=mix) + Q->>K: keywords_extraction prompt + K-->>Q: {high_level_keywords, low_level_keywords} + Q->>E: embed [query, ll_keywords, hl_keywords] (1 batch) + Q->>V: entities.query(ll_emb, top_k=40) + Q->>V: relationships.query(hl_emb, top_k=40) + Q->>V: chunks.query(query_emb, top_k=chunk_top_k) + Q->>G: get_nodes_batch / node_degrees_batch / get_nodes_edges_batch + Q->>G: get_edges_batch / edge_degrees_batch + Q->>Q: interleave local+global, dedupe, token-truncate entities (6k) and relations (8k) + Q->>V: pick chunks per entity/relation (VECTOR method) from source_id lists + Q->>R: rerank merged chunks (optional) + Q->>Q: fit chunks into max_total_tokens - prompt - KG context - 200 + Q->>L: rag_response system prompt + context + history + user_prompt + L-->>U: Markdown answer with "### References" [n] list +``` + +## 7. Generation / answer synthesis + +- `PROMPTS["rag_response"]` (KG modes) and `PROMPTS["naive_rag_response"]` (naive) are system prompts. Instructions: use only the provided context, respond in the query's language, Markdown, `{response_type}` (default "Multiple Paragraphs"), track `reference_id` per chunk, emit a `### References` section with at most 5 `[n] Document Title` entries, and treat `{user_prompt}` as "Additional Instructions". `USER_PROMPT_PREFIX` / `USER_PROMPT_PREFIX_FILE` let operators prepend global instructions (`resolve_user_prompt`). +- Conversation history (`conversation_history`) is passed as prior messages. +- Streaming is supported (`QueryResult.response_iterator`); the REST layer also exposes an Ollama-compatible `/api/chat` so Open WebUI and similar clients can talk to LightRAG. +- `fail_response` = "Sorry, I'm not able to provide an answer to that question.[no-context]" when nothing is retrieved; `llm_generated=False` lets the UI avoid labelling it as AI output. +- Query results (and keyword extractions) are cached in `llm_response_cache` keyed by query + mode + model identity (`get_llm_cache_identity`), controllable with `ENABLE_LLM_CACHE`. + +## 8. LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +Four LLM **roles** (`lightrag/llm_roles.py::ROLES`): `extract`, `keyword`, `query`, `vlm`. Each can be bound to a different provider/model via `role_llm_configs` or `EXTRACT_*` / `KEYWORD_*` / `QUERY_*` / `VLM_*` env vars (`docs/RoleSpecificLLMConfiguration.md`); `llm_model_func` is the fallback for all. + +Indexing, per chunk: +- 1 extraction call + 1 gleaning call (default `entity_extract_max_gleaning=1`) = **2 calls/chunk**. Set gleaning to 0 for 1 call/chunk. +- Summarisation calls only when an entity/relation accumulates ≥ 8 description fragments or > 1200 tokens (`force_llm_summary_on_merge`, `summary_max_tokens`); on a fresh corpus most entities never trigger it, on a large corpus hub entities do (map-reduce can mean several calls each). +- VLM calls per image/table/equation when `VLM_PROCESS_ENABLE=true`. +- Embeddings: every chunk, every entity, every relation (re-embedded on each merge update). +- Extraction results are cached per chunk, so re-indexing or rebuilding after deletion is almost free (`enable_llm_cache_for_entity_extract`). + +Query, per request: 1 keyword-LLM call (skipped if `hl_keywords`/`ll_keywords` supplied or cached) + 1 batched embedding call (+ per-entity chunk-ranking uses the same query embedding) + optional reranker call + 1 answer LLM call. `bypass` = 1 call, `naive` = 1 embedding + 1 LLM. + +The README recommends a cheap non-thinking model for `extract` and `keyword` (e.g. Haiku/mini-class; locally Qwen3-30B-A3B minimum), a stronger model for `query`, and `bge-m3` + `bge-reranker-v2-m3` locally. Prompts are long (the extraction system prompt alone is ~1.3k tokens) so prompt caching on the provider side matters. + +## 9. Configuration and extension points + +- **LLM/embedding**: pass any `async def (prompt, system_prompt=None, history_messages=[], **kwargs) -> str` as `llm_model_func`; built-in bindings in `lightrag/llm/` (OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, Bedrock, NVIDIA, Zhipu, Jina, VoyageAI, LMDeploy, LlamaIndex, lollms). Embeddings are an `EmbeddingFunc(embedding_dim, max_token_size, func)`; asymmetric query/passage embeddings supported (`docs/AsymmetricEmbedding.md`, `context="query"`). +- **Prompts**: edit `PROMPTS` dict in `lightrag/prompt.py`, or drop YAML files under `PROMPT_DIR/entity_type/*.yaml` to swap the entity-type profile (`get_default_entity_extraction_prompt_profile`, `addon_params['entity_types_guidance']`, `entity_extraction_examples`). `SUMMARY_LANGUAGE` controls output language. +- **Storage**: implement `BaseKVStorage` / `BaseVectorStorage` / `BaseGraphStorage` / `DocStatusStorage` (`lightrag/base.py`) and register in `kg/__init__.py`. `initialize_storages()` must be awaited after construction. +- **Incremental insert**: yes — content-hash dedupe at doc and chunk level, status queue, resumable `FAILED`/`PROCESSING` recovery (`apipeline_reset_failed_for_scan`), `track_id` for batch tracking, `ainsert_custom_chunks` to patch chunks, `ainsert_custom_kg` to inject a pre-built graph. +- **Delete**: `adelete_by_doc_id()` (`lightrag.py:6727`) removes chunks, then for every entity/relation that still has surviving chunks calls `rebuild_knowledge_from_chunks()` (`operate.py:1102`), which re-derives descriptions from the **cached extraction results** of the remaining chunks (no new LLM calls unless summarisation is needed). Uses a purge protocol with recovery anchors (`KG_PURGE_*` constants) so a mid-delete crash does not orphan graph objects. `adelete_by_entity`, `adelete_by_relation`, `aedit_entity`, `aedit_relation`, `acreate_entity`, `acreate_relation`, `amerge_entities` live in `utils_graph.py`. +- **Multi-tenant / workspace**: `workspace` field or `WORKSPACE` env (`[A-Za-z0-9_]`) isolates data per backend (sub-directory, collection prefix, or `workspace` column). The server runs one workspace per process; multiple instances share a backend safely. `kg/shared_storage.py` coordinates multi-worker Gunicorn. +- **Server**: `lightrag/api/lightrag_server.py` with routers `document_routes.py`, `query_routes.py`, `graph_routes.py` (entity/relation CRUD, merge, label search), `ollama_api.py`; API key or JWT auth (`AUTH_ACCOUNTS`, `TOKEN_SECRET`), rate limiting, body limits, admission control, `/webui` admin console and `/workspace` end-user chat. +- **Evaluation**: `lightrag/evaluation/eval_rag_quality.py` (RAGAS), `offline_retrieval_check.py`, `reproduce/batch_eval.py`. + +## 10. Benchmarks reported by the authors and third-party results + +Paper / `docs/Reproduce.md` (UltraDomain dataset, 125 LLM-generated high-level questions per domain, GPT-4o-mini as judge, pairwise win rates on Comprehensiveness / Diversity / Empowerment / Overall): + +| Baseline | Agriculture | CS | Legal | Mix | +|---|---|---|---|---| +| vs NaiveRAG (Overall) | 67.6% | 61.2% | 84.8% | 60.0% | +| vs RQ-RAG (Overall) | 67.6% | 62.0% | 85.6% | 60.0% | +| vs HyDE (Overall) | 75.2% | 58.4% | 73.6% | 57.6% | +| vs GraphRAG (Overall) | 54.8% | 52.0% | 52.8% | 49.6% | + +The paper also reports much lower indexing token cost than Microsoft GraphRAG (no community reports) and fast incremental updates. Third-party results in the sibling repos: MiniRAG's table (`MiniRAG/README.md`) shows LightRAG beating MiniRAG with gpt-4o-mini on LiHua-World (56.90% vs 54.08% acc) but collapsing with small models (e.g. 19–27% on MultiHop-RAG with 1.5B–4B models); PathRAG's paper claims wins over LightRAG on UltraDomain using five LLM-judged criteria. Benchmarks are LLM-as-judge win rates, which are known to be noisy; there is no retrieval-recall benchmark in the repo beyond `offline_retrieval_check.py`. + +## 11. Strengths + +- Cheapest graph indexing of the GraphRAG family: 2 LLM calls/chunk, no community detection, extraction cache makes re-runs and deletions nearly free. +- True incremental lifecycle: insert, patch chunks, delete documents with graph repair, edit/merge entities, all through a REST API with status tracking. +- Very broad storage matrix with a single-backend production path (PostgreSQL + pgvector + `PGTableGraphStorage`). +- Query pipeline is explicit and budgeted: separate entity/relation/chunk token limits, rerank hook, reference ids, `only_need_context` / `aquery_data` for inspection, bypass and naive modes for A/B testing. +- Role-split LLM configuration (extract/keyword/query/vlm) lets you put a small fast model on indexing and a strong model on answering. +- Multimodal document pipeline (MinerU/Docling/native DOCX, VLM descriptions linked into the graph) and four chunkers including heading-aware paragraph chunking. +- Large, active community; extensive docs; WebUI for graph inspection and query debugging. + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +- The graph is only used one hop deep. Retrieval is "vector search over entity/relation descriptions, then pull neighbours and provenance chunks"; there is no path search, no multi-hop reasoning, no community summaries. Answers to "global" questions depend on relation descriptions, not on an aggregated view of the corpus. +- Entity resolution is by exact normalised name. Aliases ("UN" vs "United Nations") become separate nodes unless merged manually (`amerge_entities`). +- Descriptions of hub entities grow until summarised; the KEEP source-id policy stops updating them after 200 chunks, so later documents may not be reflected in hub descriptions. +- Embedding model cannot be changed after indexing (no re-embed tool, README says so explicitly). +- The codebase is large and moving fast (`lightrag.py` 8.4k lines, `operate.py` 7.1k, `utils.py` 8.3k, `postgres_impl.py` 10k); upgrading across minor versions may require storage migrations (`storage_migrations.py`, `tools/migrate_*`). +- Defaults (JSON/NanoVectorDB/NetworkX) are single-process in-memory; NetworkX writes the whole GraphML on every `index_done_callback`. +- LLM-judge benchmarks only; quality depends heavily on the extraction model following a long, strict format (timeouts and output loops on small local models are called out in the README). +- Prompts are English-centric; `SUMMARY_LANGUAGE` steers output language but the instructions themselves are in English. + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +Choose LightRAG when you need a maintained, deployable graph-RAG service with incremental updates and deletes, a REST API and UI, pluggable production storage, and you are happy with one-hop graph context plus reranked chunks. It is the sensible default of the three frameworks here for team use. Core idea in one paragraph + +GraphRAG turns a corpus into an LLM-authored knowledge graph (entities + relationships with natural-language descriptions), partitions that graph into a hierarchy of communities with Leiden, and has the LLM pre-write a "community report" for every community at every level. At query time, "global" questions are answered by map-reducing over the community reports (the pre-summarized corpus), while "local" questions are answered by embedding the query against entity descriptions, walking out to connected relationships, covariates (claims), text units, and the communities those entities belong to, and stuffing a proportioned context window. The investment is almost entirely at index time; the payoff is the ability to answer corpus-wide, "what are the themes" style questions that chunk-level vector RAG cannot. + +## 3. Indexing pipeline, step by step + +Pipelines are lists of named workflow functions registered in `graphrag/index/workflows/factory.py` (`PipelineFactory`). Four pipelines exist (`IndexingMethod` in `graphrag/config/enums.py`): `standard`, `fast`, `standard-update`, `fast-update`. Each workflow is `async def run_workflow(config: GraphRagConfig, context: PipelineRunContext) -> WorkflowFunctionOutput` and reads/writes named tables through `context.output_table_provider` (parquet/CSV/Cosmos). `graphrag/index/run/run_pipeline.py::run_pipeline` executes them sequentially and persists `stats.json` / `context.json`. + +Standard pipeline order (`_standard_workflows`): + +1. **`load_input_documents`** – `graphrag-input` readers (text, csv, json, jsonl, parquet, markitdown) produce a `documents` table. +2. **`create_base_text_units`** (`index/workflows/create_base_text_units.py`) – `graphrag_chunking.create_chunker` with `config.chunking` (`type: tokens` default, `size: 1200`, `overlap: 100`, `encoding_model: o200k_base`; `sentence` chunker via NLTK also available). Optional `prepend_metadata`. Each chunk row: `id` (sha512 of text), `document_id`, `text`, `n_tokens`. +3. **`create_final_documents`** – links documents to their `text_unit_ids`. +4. **`extract_graph`** (`index/workflows/extract_graph.py` -> `index/operations/extract_graph/graph_extractor.py::GraphExtractor`). + - Prompt: `GRAPH_EXTRACTION_PROMPT` in `graphrag/prompts/index/extract_graph.py`; placeholders `{entity_types}`, `{input_text}`. Output is a delimited text list: `("entity"<|>NAME<|>TYPE<|>DESCRIPTION)` and `("relationship"<|>SRC<|>TGT<|>DESCRIPTION<|>STRENGTH)` separated by `##`, terminated by `<|COMPLETE|>`. Delimiters are hard-coded constants `TUPLE_DELIMITER="<|>"`, `RECORD_DELIMITER="##"`. + - Default `entity_types: [organization, person, geo, event]`. + - **Gleaning**: `max_gleanings` (default 1). After the first response, the loop appends `CONTINUE_PROMPT` ("MANY entities and relationships were missed...") and, if more gleanings remain, asks `LOOP_PROMPT` for a single `Y`/`N` to decide whether to continue. With the default, that is 1 extraction + 1 continuation call per chunk (the Y/N call is skipped on the last glean). + - `_process_result` parses records, upper-cases names/types, `float()`s the strength as `weight` (fallback 1.0). + - `extract_graph.py::_merge_entities` groups by `(title, type)` collecting `description` lists, `text_unit_ids`, `frequency`; `_merge_relationships` groups by `(source, target)` summing `weight`. `filter_orphan_relationships` drops edges whose endpoints were not extracted as entities. + - **Description summarization**: `index/operations/summarize_descriptions/description_summary_extractor.py::SummarizeExtractor`. Docs (`docs/index/methods.md`) estimate graph extraction is ~75% of indexing cost and recommend 50-100 token chunks for this mode. + +```mermaid +flowchart TB + D[documents] --> TU[create_base_text_units

Budget `max_context_tokens` (default 12 000) is split by proportion: `community_prop 0.15`, `text_unit_prop 0.5`, remainder (0.35) to entities/relationships/covariates. + - Community reports: communities containing selected entities, ranked by `(matches, rank)`. + - Local context (`context_builder/local_context.py`): entity table (`rank` = degree), relationships ordered in-network first then out-network by link count and `rank`, limited by `top_k_relationships` (10); covariates for selected entities. + - Text units (`source_context.py`): text units of selected entities, ordered by entity order then number of relationship matches. +4. Generation / answer synthesis + +- All query prompts live in `graphrag/prompts/query/` and are overridable via `*_search.prompt` / `global_search.map_prompt` / `reduce_prompt` / `knowledge_prompt` file paths in `settings.yaml`. +- Citations: local/DRIFT/basic prompts instruct `[Data: (record ids); ...]` with at most 5 ids per reference and `+more`; dataset names are the context table headers (`Reports`, `Entities`, `Relationships`, `Claims`, `Sources`). LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +Model access is through **LiteLLM** (`graphrag-llm/graphrag_llm/completion/lite_llm_completion.py::LiteLLMCompletion`, `embedding/lite_llm_embedding.py`), configured under `completion_models:` / `embedding_models:` with `model_provider`, `model`, `auth_method` (`api_key` or Azure managed identity). Defaults: `gpt-4.1` and `text-embedding-3-large` (`config/defaults.py`). Middleware pipeline adds caching, retries (`exponential`/`immediate`), sliding-window rate limiting (`requests_per_minute`, `tokens_per_minute`), metrics, and `concurrent_requests` (25). Structured output is required of the completion model (community reports use `response_format=` pydantic). + +Index-time LLM calls (standard method): +- Per text unit: 1 extraction + `max_gleanings` continuation calls (+ up to `max_gleanings-1` Y/N calls) = 2 with defaults; +1-2 more per chunk if claims are enabled. +- Per entity / relationship with >1 description: 1 summarization call (more if descriptions exceed 4000 tokens). +- Per community at every level: 1 report call. Number of communities is driven by `max_cluster_size 10`, so a few thousand entities yield hundreds of reports. +- Embeddings: every text unit, entity, and community report. +- The docs put graph extraction at ~75% of total index cost; the README warns indexing is expensive. The `fast` method removes per-chunk and per-entity LLM calls entirely, leaving only community report calls. + +Query-time: +- Local: 1 embedding + 1 completion. Basic: same. +- Global: `ceil(total report tokens / 12k)` map calls + 1 reduce; dynamic selection adds 1 call per rated report. On large corpora this is tens to hundreds of calls per question. +- DRIFT: 1 HyDE + 5 primer + up to 20 local searches x 3 depths + 1 reduce (bounded by `drift_k_followups`, `n_depth`). + +The LLM cache (`cache/`) makes re-runs with unchanged prompts free, which is what makes prompt iteration and incremental runs tractable. + +Worked example (defaults, order-of-magnitude): a 1M-token corpus yields ~900 text units of 1200 tokens. Standard indexing issues ~1 800 extraction/gleaning calls (each ~1.5-2k prompt tokens plus output), a few thousand short summarization calls for entities/edges seen in more than one chunk, and one 8k-token report call per community (often several hundred communities across levels). A single global query at level 2 over, say, 300 reports of ~1k tokens each produces ~25 map calls of 12k tokens plus one reduce, i.e. roughly 300k prompt tokens per question; local search is ~12k prompt tokens. + +## 9. Configuration and extension points + +- `graphrag init --root .` writes `settings.yaml` (`config/init_content.py`) and copies default prompts into `prompts/` as editable text files. The pydantic model is `config/models/graph_rag_config.py::GraphRagConfig`; defaults in `config/defaults.py`. Env vars via `${VAR}` substitution. +- Per-workflow model selection: every stage (`extract_graph`, `summarize_descriptions`, `community_reports`, `extract_claims`, `local_search`, `global_search`, `drift_search`, `basic_search`, `embed_text`) has a `completion_model_id` / `embedding_model_id` key pointing at a named model, enabling asymmetric configs (cheap model for extraction, strong model for query). +- Prompts: `extract_graph.prompt`, `summarize_descriptions.prompt`, `community_reports.graph_prompt`/`text_prompt`, `extract_claims.prompt`, and the query prompts; Jinja templating is available via `graphrag_llm.templating`. +- **Auto prompt tuning**: `graphrag prompt-tune` (`graphrag/prompt_tune/`) samples the corpus, infers domain/persona/entity types/language, and regenerates extraction, summarization, and report prompts (`docs/prompt_tuning/`). +- Custom workflows: `PipelineFactory.register(name, fn)` plus `workflows:` list in config to reorder/replace steps; `graphrag.api.build_index(..., method=..., additional_context=...)` for programmatic use. +- Storage, vector store, cache, chunker, input reader each have a factory with `register()`. +- **Incremental updates**: `graphrag index --method standard-update` (or `fast-update`, or `graphrag update`). `run_pipeline` backs up the previous tables, runs the full pipeline on only the delta documents (`load_update_documents` filters already-indexed ids), then `update_*` workflows merge: `index/update/entities.py::_group_and_resolve_entities` merges by `title`, concatenating descriptions and text_unit_ids (then re-summarizes descriptions via `get_summarized_entities_relationships`); `update/relationships.py` merges edges; `update/communities.py::_update_and_merge_communities` offsets delta community ids by the previous max and concatenates (communities are **not** re-clustered globally; `degree` is carried over with a TODO noting it is not recomputed). Benchmarks reported by the authors and third-party results + +- Paper (arXiv:2404.16130): two datasets of ~1M tokens each (podcast transcripts, news articles), 125 activity-centered sensemaking questions generated by an LLM, head-to-head LLM-judged win rates on *comprehensiveness*, *diversity*, *empowerment*, *directness*. Global search at community levels C0-C3 beat naive RAG on comprehensiveness and diversity (reported roughly 72-83% win rates), with root-level summaries (C0) using far fewer context tokens than lower levels; naive RAG won on directness. Model used: gpt-4-turbo. +- `RAI_TRANSPARENCY.md` describes evaluation on dataset representation, groundedness (claim coverage), injection resilience, and hallucination rates, without numbers. +- DRIFT search blog post (linked in `docs/query/drift_search.md`) reports DRIFT outperforming local search on comprehensiveness/diversity on the AP News dataset; numbers are not in the repo. +- Third-party: nano-graphrag's `docs/benchmark-en.md` reports GraphRAG indexing *A Christmas Carol* in >5 min vs <4 min for nano-graphrag with similar answer quality. fast-graphrag's `benchmarks/README.md` (using the nano-graphrag implementation as a proxy for GraphRAG local mode) reports 0.75 / 0.73 perfect-retrieval rate on 2WikiMultihopQA (51 / 101 queries) and ~40 min insertion for ~800 chunks, with a crash on HotpotQA. Treat competitor-run numbers with caution. + +## 11. Strengths + +- Only one of the three with first-class **global / corpus-wide** question answering (map-reduce over hierarchical community reports) plus local, DRIFT, and basic modes. +- Rich, documented, tabular knowledge model with full provenance (`text_unit_ids` everywhere) and `human_readable_id`-based citations. +- Production plumbing: LiteLLM (100+ providers, Azure AD auth), rate limiting, retries, JSON/SQLite cache, metrics, Azure Blob/Cosmos/AI Search backends, CLI, streaming API, callbacks. +- Auto prompt tuning adapts extraction prompts to the domain. +- `fast` NLP indexing path for a dramatically cheaper graph. +- Incremental update pipeline exists and is exercised in tests. +- Large user base, long changelog, dependency/CVE maintenance. + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +- **Cost**: ~2 LLM calls per 1200-token chunk plus per-entity summaries plus one call per community per level; global search issues dozens of map calls per query. Explicitly warned in README/RAI doc. +- **Maintenance mode**: no new features; design reflects 2024 model capabilities (prompted "Y/N" gleaning, delimiter-parsed text output instead of structured output for extraction). +- No graph database: all graph ops are pandas joins; local search loads every parquet table into memory (`query/factory.py`, `indexer_adapters.py`), which limits corpus size per process. +- Entity resolution is exact-match on upper-cased `title` (`_merge_entities`); no embedding-based deduplication. +- Incremental updates append new Leiden communities with offset ids rather than re-clustering; node `degree` is not recomputed; reports for merged communities can become stale. +- Community detection only on the largest connected component by default (`use_lcc: true`) so disconnected entities get no community/report. +- Requires a model that supports JSON-schema structured outputs for community reports; older/small models struggle (docs note o-series prompts may need rewriting). +- Monorepo split into 8 packages increases install surface; heavy dependencies (graspologic_native, LiteLLM, LanceDB, spaCy for fast mode). + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +Choose Microsoft GraphRAG when you need sensemaking over a bounded corpus ("what are the main themes / risks / actors across these documents"), want citations back to source rows, can afford a large one-time indexing bill, and want Azure-native deployment options. It is also the right reference implementation if you are evaluating the GraphRAG paper faithfully. Avoid it for high-churn data, very large corpora without a graph/vector service, or latency-sensitive factoid QA where basic vector RAG or fast-graphrag's PPR retrieval is cheaper and faster. + +## 14. Core idea in one paragraph + +MiniRAG assumes the LLM is a 1–4B on-device model that cannot be trusted to write good descriptions, follow long prompts, or reason over large contexts. So it makes the *structure* do the work: documents are chunked and a small model extracts typed entities and relations (same prompt family as LightRAG), but the graph is treated as a "semantic-aware heterogeneous graph" in which chunks are first-class citizens attached to entities through provenance ids. At query time the SLM only has to (a) name the entities mentioned in the question and (b) pick, from the list of entity types that actually exist in the graph, which type the answer probably is. Retrieval then becomes a graph problem: find candidate nodes by **name** similarity, walk 2 hops from them, score each path by how many nodes of the predicted answer type it touches and how many retrieved relation edges it contains, and accumulate votes for the chunks those nodes and edges came from, blended with plain chunk vector search. The context handed to the SLM is deliberately tiny (entity table ≤ 500 tokens by default plus the top chunks), which is what lets Phi-3.5-mini/Qwen2.5-3B-class models beat NaiveRAG and LightRAG on the authors' benchmarks. + +## 3. Indexing pipeline, step by step + +Entry: `MiniRAG.insert()` / `ainsert()` (`minirag/minirag.py:340-383`). + +1. **Enqueue** — `apipeline_enqueue_documents()` (`minirag.py:385`): `clean_text`, `compute_mdhash_id(doc, prefix="doc-")` (or caller-supplied `ids`), dedupe against `doc_status.filter_keys()`, write `DocStatus.PENDING` rows with `content_summary`, `content_length`, timestamps. +2. **Process** — `apipeline_process_enqueue_documents()` (`minirag.py:437`): takes `PROCESSING`, `FAILED` and `PENDING` docs in batches of `max_parallel_insert` (env `MAX_PARALLEL_INSERT`, default 2), chunks each with `self.chunking_func` (default `chunking_by_token_size`, `operate.py:36`: tiktoken windows, `chunk_token_size=1200`, `chunk_overlap_token_size=100`, `tiktoken_model_name="gpt-4o-mini"`; `split_by_character` args are accepted but the default chunker ignores them), upserts to `chunks_vdb`, `full_docs`, `text_chunks`, and marks the doc `PROCESSED`. +3. **Re-chunk and extract** — back in `ainsert()`, the code then re-chunks **every document with status `PROCESSED`** (not just the ones just inserted) and calls `extract_entities()` on all of them, with no chunk-level `filter_keys` dedupe. There is no LLM cache to soften this: `llm_response_cache` is instantiated and passed as `hashing_kv`, but every binding in `minirag/llm/*.py` does `kwargs.pop("hashing_kv", None)` and nothing in `operate.py` calls `handle_cache`/`save_to_cache`. So **each `ainsert` re-runs extraction LLM calls for the entire corpus** and re-merges every entity (descriptions are `set()`-deduplicated, so the graph does not grow, but `weight` on edges is re-summed each time). This is the most important operational bug in the repo for incremental use; the reproduction scripts avoid it by inserting the whole dataset in one call. +4. **Extraction** — `extract_entities()` (`operate.py:233`), per chunk, `asyncio.gather` over all chunks (throttled only by `llm_model_max_async=16`): + - Prompt `PROMPTS["entity_extraction"]` (`prompt.py:13`): nano-graphrag format, `{entity_types}` = `PROMPTS["DEFAULT_ENTITY_TYPES"] = ["organization", "person", "location", "event"]` (hard-wired; `addon_params["entity_types"]` is **not** read, unlike LightRAG/PathRAG), delimiters `<|>` / `##` / `<|COMPLETE|>`, three baked-in few-shot examples, output language fixed to English. + - **Gleaning**: `entity_extract_max_gleaning=1` → one `entiti_continue_extraction` call; with more rounds, `entiti_if_loop_extraction` YES/NO decides. A `entiti_continue_extraction_mini` prompt (with an `{omit}` slot for "what was omitted") exists in `prompt.py:144` but is **unused** by `operate.py`. + - Records parsed by `_handle_single_entity_extraction` / `_handle_single_relationship_extraction` (names and types upper-cased via `clean_str(...).upper()`; relation `weight` parsed from the strength field). +5. **Merge** — `_merge_nodes_then_upsert()` (`operate.py:117`) and `_merge_edges_then_upsert()` (`operate.py:166`): same as early LightRAG (majority `entity_type`, `sorted(set(descriptions))` joined with `GRAPH_FIELD_SEP=""`, `source_id` union, summed `weight`, unioned `keywords`), **except the `_handle_entity_relation_summary` calls are commented out**, so descriptions are never summarised by the LLM. `_handle_entity_relation_summary` itself (`operate.py:57`) was gutted to return the description if short and otherwise `None` — do not re-enable it without restoring the body. Edge keys are normalised with `tuple(sorted(k))`. +6. **Vector upserts** (`operate.py:368-411`): + - `entities_vdb` (namespace `entities`): content = name + description. (The same upsert block appears twice back-to-back with slightly different concatenation, a copy-paste leftover; the second write wins.) + - `entity_name_vdb` (namespace `entities_name`, ids `Ename-`): content = **entity name only**. This index is MiniRAG-specific. + - `relationships_vdb` (namespace `relationships`): content = keywords + src + tgt + description. +7. `_insert_done()` flushes all eight storages (`index_done_callback`). + +Where are the "chunk nodes" of the paper's heterogeneous graph? **Not in the graph store.** `upsert_node` is only called for entities (`operate.py:158`, `201`); chunks are linked to entities and edges solely through the `source_id` attribute and the parallel `description` list (the code relies on `len(text_units_node) == len(descriptionlist_node)` to pair each description fragment with its chunk id in `path2chunk`). The heterogeneity is therefore realised as (entity graph + chunk vector index + provenance ids), not as typed nodes. + +```mermaid +flowchart TD + A[rag.ainsert texts] --> B[apipeline_enqueue_documents

Graph data model + +- **Node id** = upper-cased quoted entity name (`"LIHUA"`). Attributes: `entity_type` (upper-cased; one of the four default types or `"UNKNOWN"` for endpoints created by edges), `description` (``-joined raw fragments, one per contributing chunk), `source_id` (``-joined chunk ids). `get_types()` lower-cases `entity_type` to build the "answer type pool". +- **Edge**: `weight` (summed), `description`, `keywords`, `source_id`. Stored undirected in NetworkX (`nx.Graph`); keys sorted at merge time. +- No chunk/document nodes; chunk ids live in `source_id`. Chunks themselves are in `text_chunks` KV (`{tokens, content, full_doc_id, chunk_order_index}`) and `chunks_vdb`. +- Three vector indexes over graph objects (`entities`, `entities_name`, `relationships`) plus `chunks`. +- Graph-store helpers unique to MiniRAG (`kg/networkx_impl.py`): `get_types()` → `(lowercase types, original types)`; `get_node_from_types(type_list)` → all nodes whose type is in the list; `get_neighbors_within_k_hops(node, k)` → list of path tuples of length ≤ k+1 built by `merge_tuples` (`utils.py:362`), which joins edge tuples end-to-end while avoiding immediate back-tracking. Query / retrieval modes + +`QueryParam` (`minirag/base.py:18`): `mode: Literal["light", "naive", "mini"] = "mini"`, `top_k` (env `TOP_K`, default **60**), `max_token_for_text_unit=4000`, `max_token_for_global_context=4000`, `max_token_for_local_context=4000`, **`max_token_for_node_context=500`** ("For Mini, if too long, SLM may fail to generate any response"), `only_need_context`, `only_need_prompt`, `response_type`, `stream`, `hl_keywords`/`ll_keywords` (declared, not used by `mini`), `conversation_history`, `history_turns=3`. + +Dispatch (`minirag.py:537`): `light → hybrid_query` (LightRAG's hybrid: keyword extraction → entity + relation VDB → one-hop context in CSV tables), `naive → naive_query` (chunk VDB only), `mini → minirag_query`. + +### 6.1 `mini` mode — query understanding + +`minirag_query()` (`operate.py:1409`): +1. `TYPE_POOL, TYPE_POOL_w_CASE = await knowledge_graph_inst.get_types()` — the live set of entity types in the graph. +2. One LLM call with `PROMPTS["minirag_query2kwd"]` (`prompt.py:159`), which shows the model an "Answer type pool" dictionary and asks for JSON `{"answer_type_keywords": [...≤3 types from the pool...], "entities_from_query": [...]}`. Few-shot examples use a pool of invented types (PERSONAL LIFE, STRATEGY, FOOD, EMOJI, ...). Parsed with `json_repair.loads`, with a fallback that strips the echoed prompt and extracts the first `{...}` (for HF models that echo input). `entities_from_query` is capped at 5. + +### 6.2 `mini` mode — graph search (`_build_mini_query_context`, `operate.py:1252`) + +1. **Candidate nodes by name**: for each query entity, `entity_name_vdb.query(ent, top_k=60)` → candidate entity names with `Score = distance` (cosine similarity from NanoVectorDB). `ent_from_query_dict[ent]` remembers which candidates came from which query entity. +2. **Reasoning paths**: for every candidate, `get_neighbors_within_k_hops(key, 2)` → all 1- and 2-hop path tuples starting at that node. Candidates with no paths are mostly dropped — only the top 20% by score (`save_p = max(1, int(len * 0.2))`) of isolated nodes are kept. +3. **Answer-type nodes**: `get_node_from_types(type_keywords)` → `maybe_answer_list` (every node whose type matches the predicted answer types). These names are added to `imp_ents`. +4. **Path scoring** `cal_path_score_list()` (`utils.py:404`): each path gets `[count of nodes in path that are in maybe_answer_list]` (`count_elements_in_tuple`). +5. **Edge voting**: `relationships_vdb.query(original_query, top_k = len(entities_from_query) * top_k)`; edges touching any `imp_ents` node are `goodedge`. `edge_vote_path()` (`utils.py:416`) appends, to each path's score list, the number of retrieved good edges that are contiguous sub-sequences of the path, and records those edges in `pairs_append`. +6. **Path → chunk votes** `path2chunk()` (`operate.py:1124`, `max_chunks=3`): for each candidate node and each of its paths, collect chunk ids from (a) the matched edges' `source_id`, (b) the path head node's `source_id`, (c) the other path nodes' `source_id`, where for nodes with > 5 chunks only the top `max(5, n/2)` description fragments by **Levenshtein similarity to the query** (`calculate_similarity(..., method="levenshtein")`) are kept. Each chunk's count is multiplied by `total_score = type_hits + edge_votes + 1`; the node keeps its 3 most-voted chunk ids. +7. **Entity table**: nodes with their `Score` and raw description, sorted by score, truncated to `max_token_for_node_context` (500 tokens), rendered as CSV `(entity, score, description)`. +8. **Chunk fusion** `kwd2chunk()` (`operate.py:1220`): per query entity, iterate its candidate nodes; the first candidate's score is doubled; the first chunk of each node's list gets ×10 if it also appears in `chunks_vdb.query(original_query, top_k=top_k/2)` (plain vector hits); votes are summed and the top `top_k/2` (=30) chunk ids are selected. +9. Early exits: if the last name-VDB query or the relation-VDB query returned nothing, return `None` → `fail_response`. +10. Context = `-----Entities-----` CSV + `-----Sources-----` CSV `(id, content)` of the selected chunks (chunks are **not** token-truncated here; 30 chunks × 1200 tokens can exceed small context windows — `llm_model_max_token_size` is left to the LLM binding to enforce). + +### 6.3 `light` mode + +`hybrid_query()` (`operate.py:918`) = LightRAG hybrid circa Jan 2025: `keywords_extraction` prompt → `_build_local_query_context(ll)` + `_build_global_query_context(hl)` → `combine_contexts` → `rag_response`. Generation / answer synthesis + +`PROMPTS["rag_response"]` (`prompt.py:315`) is the nano-graphrag "data tables" prompt ("summarizing all information in the input data tables... incorporating any relevant general knowledge... If you don't know the answer, just say so"), with `{response_type}` and `{context_data}`. No citation/reference mechanism; chunks are anonymous `(id, content)` rows. `QueryParam.conversation_history` / `history_turns` are declared but no query function in `operate.py` reads them, so there is no multi-turn support in any mode. Query responses are **not cached** in any mode (`operate.py` never calls `handle_cache`/`save_to_cache`, and the LLM bindings discard `hashing_kv`). `fail_response` = "Sorry, I'm not able to provide an answer to that question." + +## 8. LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +- **Indexing**: 2 LLM calls per chunk (extraction + 1 gleaning) and **zero** merge-time summarisation calls. Embeddings: chunks, entities (name+description), entity names, relations. Because `ainsert` re-processes all `PROCESSED` docs and nothing caches LLM output, indexing cost is `2 × (total chunks in corpus)` LLM calls **per `ainsert` call**, not per new document — batch all documents into one `ainsert`. +- **Query (`mini`)**: 1 LLM call for type/entity keywords + 1 answer call; embeddings: one per query entity (≤5) for the name index, one for relations, one for chunks (7 small embedding calls max); CPU: 2-hop expansion of up to 60 candidates per query entity, Levenshtein scoring of description fragments. All graph calls are per-node `await`s (no batching), fine for NetworkX, chatty for remote graph DBs. +- **Small-model friendliness** (the design goal): extraction prompt is the standard long one, but the query-side prompt asks only for entity names and a choice from an enumerated type list (classification rather than abstraction); the entity context is capped at 500 tokens; no description summarisation; `json_repair` and prompt-echo stripping tolerate messy SLM output. `main.py` / `reproduce/` run with `llm_model_max_token_size=200`, HF `hf_model_complete`, and `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384-dim) embeddings — i.e. it is engineered to run fully on-device. +- Bindings (`minirag/llm/`): `hf.py` (transformers, used by the paper), `openai.py`, `azure_openai.py`, `ollama.py`, `bedrock.py`, `zhipu.py`, `nvidia_openai.py`, `siliconcloud.py`, `jina.py`, `lmdeploy.py`, `lollms.py`; `minirag/llm.py` also provides a `MultiModel` round-robin wrapper over several API keys. + +## 9.
