Benchmarks reported by the authors + +Numbers come from the paper (arXiv:2401.18059), not from anything in the repo (the repo has no evaluation scripts): + +- **QuALITY** (long-document multiple choice): with GPT-4, RAPTOR 82.6% overall / 76.2% on the hard subset, which the paper reports as a new SOTA, +20% absolute over the prior best on the hard subset. With UnifiedQA-3B: 62.4%/56.6% vs 53.4%/48.2% for DPR-style chunk retrieval. +- **QASPER** (F1): RAPTOR+GPT-4 55.7 vs BM25 and DPR baselines in the 50–53 range; RAPTOR+UnifiedQA 36.6 vs 32.7. +- **NarrativeQA**: RAPTOR+UnifiedQA ROUGE-L 30.9 / BLEU-1 23.6 / METEOR 19.1, above the BM25/DPR baselines. +- Ablations: collapsed tree beats tree traversal at equal token budgets; retrieving at ~2000 tokens is roughly the sweet spot; roughly 18–57% of retrieved nodes come from non-leaf layers depending on dataset, with higher layers helping on "theme"-style questions. + +Third-party: LlamaIndex (`RaptorPack`), LangChain cookbook, and several GraphRAG papers (e.g. GraphRAG-Bench, HippoRAG2) use RAPTOR as a baseline; results there typically show it competitive on summarisation-style questions and weaker than entity-graph methods on multi-hop fact questions. These are external and not in the repo. + +## 11. Strengths + +- Conceptually simple and model-agnostic; ~2k lines, easy to read and modify in an afternoon. +- Captures document-level and section-level abstractions that flat chunk RAG misses, which helps "what is this document about / compare the themes" questions. +- Collapsed-tree retrieval needs no special query planning: a single vector search over mixed-granularity nodes. +- No extraction schema, no entity resolution, no graph database – low operational surface. +- Soft clustering lets a chunk contribute to several summaries, which is sensible for sections that bridge topics. +- Permissive MIT license; the idea is widely re-implemented (LlamaIndex, LangChain) if you prefer a maintained host. + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +- **Research code, effectively unmaintained**: no tests, pinned 2024 dependencies (`openai==1.3.3`, `transformers==4.38.1`, `numpy==1.26.3`), `text-davinci-003` references, `print(e)` error handling that returns exception objects as answers, racy `next_node_index` in multithreaded tree construction, an O(N²) embedding-equality lookup inside clustering, and a probable inverted comparison in `threshold` selection mode. +- **No incremental indexing**: any corpus change is a full rebuild including all summarisation calls. +- **Single-document mindset**: `add_documents(text)` takes one string; no document ids, no metadata, no per-document boundaries, no filtering at query time, no citations. +- **Scalability**: brute-force cosine in Python at query time, pickled embeddings, and UMAP+BIC-GMM sweeps (up to 50 GMM fits per step) make tens of thousands of chunks slow and memory-heavy. Nothing is persisted to a vector DB. +- **Non-determinism**: UMAP is stochastic; two builds of the same corpus yield different trees and therefore different summaries. +- **Summary hallucination risk**: upper layers are LLM-written; errors propagate upward and are retrieved as if they were source text, with no provenance back to the originating chunks in the context given to the QA model. +- **No multi-hop reasoning**: a single retrieve-then-answer step; no decomposition, no iteration, no graph traversal between entities. +- The FAISS retriever is leaf-only and separate; there is no ANN index for the tree itself. + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +- Long single documents or small homogeneous corpora (books, manuals, reports, transcripts) where questions mix fine detail with "big picture" summarisation. +- Teams that want a hierarchical-summary index without the cost and complexity of entity extraction and a graph store. +- As a component inside a larger stack (e.g. use the tree builder to produce summary nodes that you then store in your own vector DB), rather than as a turnkey system. +- Not a fit for: frequently changing corpora, multi-hop entity questions, provenance/citation requirements, >100k chunks, or production services needing a maintained library. In those cases take the idea and use a maintained re-implementation or a GraphRAG framework. + +## 14. Core idea in one paragraph + +TrustGraph is a distributed knowledge-engineering platform rather than a GraphRAG library: every function (PDF decoding, chunking, each kind of extraction, embeddings, each store writer and reader, each LLM provider, prompt templating, Graph RAG, Document RAG, agents, SPARQL, GraphQL, the API gateway) is a separate long-running processor that consumes and produces typed dataclass messages over Apache Pulsar (or RabbitMQ / Kafka). Knowledge is modelled as **RDF 1.2 quads** (`B/schema/core/primitives.py:Triple(s, p, o, g)` with `Term` supporting IRI / blank / literal / quoted-triple terms) stored in Cassandra (or Neo4j, FalkorDB, Memgraph) with entity-level and chunk-level embeddings in Qdrant (or Pinecone, Milvus). Extraction can be ontology-guided ("OntoRAG": OWL classes/properties are embedded and the relevant subset is retrieved per chunk to steer the LLM), and provenance of every extraction and every query is itself written as W3C PROV-O triples into named graphs. "Flows" (`docs/tech-specs/flow-blueprint-definition.md`) are JSON blueprints that instantiate a wired set of processors and queues per workspace; the API gateway and CLI expose them to applications and agents, and a ReAct / plan / supervisor agent runtime with tool filtering and explainability sits on top. + +## 3. Message types are plain dataclasses in `B/schema/` serialised by the backend (`B/base/async_pulsar_backend.py`, `async_rabbitmq_backend.py`, `async_kafka_backend.py`; selected by `pubsub_backend` in `B/base/pubsub.py:get_async_pubsub`). Topic naming follows `persistent://tg/flow/{workspace}::{id}` for fire-and-forget data and `non-persistent://tg/request|response/{workspace}::{class}` for request/response services. + +1. **Submit** - `T/librarian/` (`librarian` script) stores the blob in S3-compatible storage (Garage/MinIO, path `doc/{object_id}`) and metadata in Cassandra (`T/tables/library.py`: `document`, `processing`, `upload_session`); `add-processing(document_id, flow, collection)` publishes a `Document` (`B/schema/knowledge/document.py`) to the flow's `document-load` (PDF) or `text-load` (text) interface. Graph data model + +- **Primitive**: `Triple(s: Term, p: Term, o: Term, g: str|None)` - an RDF 1.2 quad; `Term(type=IRI|BLANK|LITERAL|TRIPLE, iri, id, value, datatype, language, triple)` so literals carry XSD datatypes or language tags and quoted triples (RDF-star style reification) are first-class. Batched as `Triples(metadata: Metadata(id, root, collection), triples[])`. +- **Vocabulary used by extractors** (`B/rdf.py`): `rdf:type`, `rdfs:label`, `skos:definition`; entity IRIs under `http://trustgraph.ai/e/`; predicates from free-text extraction are also minted as IRIs with `rdfs:label`. With OntoRAG the classes and properties of the loaded OWL ontology are used instead (prefix map in `extract/kg/ontology/extract.py:URI_PREFIXES` covers rdf, rdfs, owl, skos, schema.org, xsd). +- **Named graphs**: `g` separates source knowledge, provenance (`GRAPH_SOURCE`), retrieval explainability (`GRAPH_RETRIEVAL`) and agent traces; `B/provenance/uris.py` mints question / grounding / exploration / focus / synthesis / agent-session URIs. +- **Entity contexts & embeddings**: `EntityContext(entity: Term, context: str, chunk_id)`; `EntityEmbeddings(entity, vector, chunk_id)`; chunk embeddings keyed by librarian `chunk_id`. Entities are therefore addressable both as graph nodes and as vectors. +- **Structured rows**: `RowSchema(name, fields: [Field(name, type, size, primary, required, enum_values, indexed)])` stored in Cassandra tables with GraphQL query (`docs/tech-specs/graphql-query.md`). +- **Ontology handling**: OWL/Turtle ontologies are workspace configuration (`config type "ontology"`, Ontology Workbench in the UI, `T/query/ontology/` answers ontology questions incl. `query_explanation.py`); SHACL is mentioned in README but no SHACL validation processor was found in `trustgraph-flow`. There is no schema enforcement in the free-text extractors; OntoRAG constrains the prompt and normalises entities to ontology terms (`entity_normalizer.py`). +- **Where stored**: triples in the quad store, entity vectors in the vector store, chunk text/pages/documents in S3 via the librarian, document/processing metadata, config, flows, IAM and knowledge-core snapshots in Cassandra keyspaces, keyword index in SQLite FTS5. + +Cassandra quad layout (`T/direct/cassandra_kg.py`): a 7-table scheme, e.g. `spog(collection, s, p, o, g) PRIMARY KEY ((collection, s), p, o, g)`, `posg`, `ospg` for wildcard-graph queries and `gspo`, ... with `g` in the partition key, so every triple-pattern shape resolves to a partition read. `docs/tech-specs/cassandra-consolidation.md`, `cassandra-performance-refactor.md`, `neo4j-user-collection-isolation.md` cover keyspace/collection isolation. + +## 5. Query / retrieval modes + +All query services are request/response processors reachable through the API gateway (`T/gateway/dispatch/*.py`: `graph_rag`, `document_rag`, `agent`, `triples_query`, `graph_embeddings_query`, `document_embeddings_query`, `sparql_query`, `structured_query`, `nlp_query`, `rows_query`, `text_completion`, `prompt`, `embeddings`, `reranker`, `mcp_tool`, import/export of triples, embeddings and cores, librarian, flow, config, iam, ...) over REST and WebSocket (`docs/README.api-docs.md`, `specs/api`, `specs/websocket`), or via the Python API (`docs/python-api.md`) and `tg-*` CLI. + +**(a) Graph RAG** - `T/retrieval/graph_rag/graph_rag.py:GraphRag.query(query, collection, entity_limit=50, triple_limit=30, max_subgraph_size=1000, max_path_length=2, edge_limit=25, max_reranker_input=350, max_reranker_text_length=240, streaming, chunk_callback, explain_callback, save_answer_callback)`: +1. `Query.extract_concepts()` - prompt `extract-concepts` (one LLM call) returns one concept per line; falls back to the raw query. +2. `get_vectors()` - embed each concept (embeddings service). +3. `get_entities()` - for each concept vector, `graph_embeddings_client.query(vector, limit=entity_limit // n_concepts, collection)` against the entity vector index; de-duplicated seed entity IRIs. +4. `hop_and_filter()` - up to `max_path_length` hops: fetch all edges from the frontier via batched triple-pattern queries (`execute_batch_triple_queries`, `triple_limit` per entity, LRU+TTL caches), resolve `rdfs:label`s (`resolve_labels_batch`), render each edge as `"{p} {o}"` text (truncated to 240 chars, at most 350 candidates), score them with the **cross-encoder reranker service** (`reranker-flashrank`, default `ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12-v2`) against the concepts, keep `edge_limit` top edges, and use their targets as the next frontier. This replaced an LLM 1-10 "semantic filter" prompt (`docs/tech-specs/graph-rag-semantic-filter.md` explains why). +5. `trace_source_documents()` - follow PROV-O edges from selected triples back to chunks/documents so the answer can cite sources. +6. Synthesis - prompt `kg-synthesis` with the labelled edge list and question (streaming supported). Token usage from all prompt calls is accumulated. +7. Explainability - at each stage (`question`, `grounding`, `exploration`, `focus`, `synthesis`) PROV-O triples are emitted through `explain_callback` into `GRAPH_RETRIEVAL` (`docs/tech-specs/query-time-explainability.md`), which the UI renders as a DAG. + +**(b) Document RAG** - `T/retrieval/document_rag/document_rag.py:DocumentRag.query(query, collection, doc_limit=20, fetch_limit=0, ...)`: `extract-concepts` prompt -> per-concept vector search over chunk embeddings (and/or FTS5 keyword search; `retrieval_mode` dense / keyword / hybrid fused with `rrf_fuse()` reciprocal-rank fusion), over-fetch `OVERFETCH_FACTOR x doc_limit` when a reranker is wired, optional cross-encoder rerank with MMR diversity (`rerank.py`, `rerank_diversity_mode="mmr"`), then prompt `document-prompt` (`prompt_client.document_prompt(query, documents)`) for synthesis. + +**(c) Structured / NL-to-GraphQL** - `structured-query` (`T/retrieval/structured_query/service.py`) -> `nlp-query` (`T/retrieval/nlp_query/service.py`: phase 1 prompt `schema-selection`, phase 2 GraphQL generation) -> `rows-query-cassandra`. `structured-diag` diagnoses CSV/JSON samples and proposes a `RowSchema`. + +**(d) SPARQL** - `sparql-query` (`T/query/sparql/service.py`) parses SPARQL, decomposes it into triple-pattern lookups against the triples query service and performs joins/filters/projections in memory - works on any backend, at the cost of pulling data client-side. + +**(e) Raw services** - `triples-query` (pattern match `s?/p?/o?/g?` with limits), `graph-embeddings-query`, `document-embeddings-query`, `row-embeddings-query`, `embeddings`, `reranker`, `text-completion`, `prompt`. + +**(f) Agents** - see section 7; the agent's `knowledge-query` tool wraps Graph RAG. + +**API surface.** `api-gateway` (`T/gateway/service.py`) registers one dispatcher per service in `T/gateway/dispatch/` and exposes them as REST (`/api/v1/...`) and WebSocket endpoints; request/response calls are multiplexed over the broker with correlation ids (`dispatch/requestor.py`, `mux.py`), streaming responses are forwarded chunk by chunk, and the gateway enforces IAM (`gateway/auth.py`, bearer API keys or signed tokens, or `no-auth-svc` for development) and audit (`gateway/audit.py`). Import/export endpoints (`triples_import`/`_export`, `graph_embeddings_*`, `document_embeddings_*`, `entity_contexts_*`, `core_import`/`core_export`, `rows_import`) move bulk data without going through extraction. The Python client (`trustgraph-base/trustgraph/api`, `docs/python-api.md`) and every `tg-invoke-*` CLI call the same endpoints, so anything the UI does is scriptable. + +```mermaid +sequenceDiagram + participant Cl as client / gateway + participant GR as graph-rag processor + participant PR as prompt-template -> text-completion + participant EM as embeddings + participant GEQ as graph-embeddings-query (Qdrant) + participant TQ as triples-query (Cassandra) + participant RR as reranker-flashrank + Cl->>GR: GraphRagQuery(question, collection, limits) + GR->>PR: prompt "extract-concepts" + PR-->>GR: concept lines + GR->>EM: embed(concepts) + GR->>GEQ: query(vector, limit) per concept + GEQ-->>GR: seed entity IRIs + loop hop 1..max_path_length + GR->>TQ: batched triple patterns from frontier + GR->>TQ: resolve rdfs:label for new terms + GR->>RR: rerank("{p} {o}" texts vs concepts) + RR-->>GR: top edge_limit edges -> next frontier + end + GR->>TQ: PROV-O trace to source chunks/documents + GR->>PR: prompt "kg-synthesis" (streaming) + PR-->>GR: answer tokens + GR-->>Cl: answer + explainability triples (GRAPH_RETRIEVAL) +``` + +## 7. Generation / answer synthesis + +- **Prompts are data, not code.** `T/prompt/template/service.py` holds per-workspace `PromptManager`s loaded from config type `prompt`; every prompt (`extract-definitions`, `extract-relationships`, `extract-rows`, `extract-with-ontologies`, `agent-kg-extract`, `extract-concepts`, `kg-synthesis`, `document-prompt`, `schema-selection`, `agent-react`, `question`, ...) is a Jinja-style template with a declared response type (text / JSON with schema / JSONL). The default template texts ship in the external seed JSON consumed by `bootstrap/initialisers/template_seed.py` (populating the reserved `__template__` workspace) and are editable at runtime through the Prompt Editor UI or `tg-set-prompt`; they are **not** in this repository, so exact wording cannot be cited here. +- **Citations**: Graph RAG passes labelled edges plus traced source documents to `kg-synthesis`; Document RAG passes chunk texts to `document-prompt`. Whether the answer contains inline citations depends on the template. Structured provenance is delivered separately as explainability triples and, when `save_answer_callback` is set, the answer is saved into the librarian as a `document_type: "answer"` child of the question. +- **Agent loops** (`T/agent/`): + - `agent-manager-react` (`react/service.py`, `agent_manager.py`): classic ReAct - prompt `agent-react` renders question, history and tool list; `streaming_parser.py` parses Thought / Action / Observation / Final Answer; `max_iterations=10`; tools built from config type `tool`/`tool-service` with implementations `KnowledgeQueryImpl` (Graph RAG), `TextCompletionImpl`, `PromptImpl`, `McpToolImpl` (MCP servers via `mcp-tool` processor, bearer-token support), `StructuredQueryImpl`, `RowEmbeddingsQueryImpl`, `ToolServiceImpl` (`docs/tech-specs/tool-services.md`); `tool_filter.py` applies tool groups and state machines (`docs/tech-specs/tool-group.md`). Each thought/observation is streamed to the client and recorded as explainability triples (`agent_iteration_uri`, `docs/tech-specs/agent-explainability.md`). + - `agent-orchestrator` (`orchestrator/service.py`, "drop-in replacement" on the same queues): `meta_router.py` asks the LLM to classify the question and pick `ReactPattern`, `PlanThenExecutePattern` (`plan_pattern.py`: plan once, execute each step as a single-shot tool call) or `SupervisorPattern` (`supervisor_pattern.py`: decompose into sub-goals, fan out as child `AgentRequest`s with `correlation_id`, `aggregator.py` waits for all, then synthesise). `docs/tech-specs/agent-orchestration.md`. + - The README's "policy runtime" (authority / scope / risk checks before execution) is reflected in IAM, audit events (`B/base/audit_publisher.py`, `docs/tech-specs/audit-events.md`) and tool gating; no general policy-evaluation engine (e.g. SHACL/OPA) was found in this tree. +- Streaming LLM responses are supported end to end (`docs/tech-specs/streaming-llm-responses.md`, `rag-streaming-support.md`). + +## 8. LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +**LLM services** (`T/model/text_completion/*`): `openai`, `azure`, `azure_openai`, `claude` (Anthropic), `cohere`, `mistral`, `ollama`, `llamafile`, `lmstudio`, `tgi`, `vllm`; plus `trustgraph-vertexai` and `trustgraph-bedrock` packages. Image-to-text via `image-to-text-openai`. Models are per-flow-class settings (`{workspace}:{class}` service queues), so several flows can share one LLM service or run different ones. `metering` tracks tokens; `LLMResponse`-style results carry `in_token`/`out_token`/`model` which Graph RAG aggregates. + +**Embeddings**: `embeddings-fastembed` (ONNX, default `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, batched - `docs/tech-specs/embeddings-batch-processing.md`), `embeddings-ollama`, `trustgraph-embeddings-hf`. Reranker: `reranker-flashrank` (local cross-encoder). Both default to CPU-local models, so the only paid calls by default are LLM completions. + +**Indexing cost per chunk** (default flow with definitions + relationships extractors): 2 LLM calls (`extract-definitions`, `extract-relationships`); +1 with OntoRAG (`extract-with-ontologies`, with a larger prompt carrying the ontology subset); the agent extractor costs a whole ReAct loop per chunk (several LLM calls). Embeddings: one batch per `EntityContexts` message and one per chunk (local by default). No LLM-based entity resolution or description summarisation; no community detection. + +**Query cost**: Graph RAG = 1 LLM call (`extract-concepts`) + N concept embeddings + up to `max_path_length` rerank batches (local) + 1 LLM call (`kg-synthesis`) = **2 LLM calls**. Document RAG = 2 LLM calls (`extract-concepts`, `document-prompt`). ReAct agent = up to `max_iterations` LLM calls plus any Graph RAG calls inside tools. SPARQL/GraphQL paths use 0-2 LLM calls (`nlp-query` uses 2). + +## 9. Benchmarks + +**Author-reported**: none. No accuracy, latency or cost benchmarks were found in `README.md`, `docs/`, or `docs/tech-specs/` (the only quantitative material is design reasoning, e.g. why the LLM semantic filter was replaced by a cross-encoder). **Third-party**: none found in-tree. The project's claims about reduced hallucination are architectural (ontology grounding, provenance), not measured. + +## 11. Strengths + +- True platform: ingestion, storage, retrieval, agents, IAM, metering, UI, CLI and API gateway in one deployable stack with no mandatory SaaS dependencies ("No API keys required" except LLM providers). +- Standards-based knowledge model: RDF 1.2 quads with datatypes/language tags/quoted triples, OWL ontologies, PROV-O provenance for both extraction and retrieval, Turtle import/export - portable to any RDF system and auditable by design. +- Pluggable everything via pub/sub: 4 triple stores, 3 vector stores, 3 brokers, ~11 LLM back-ends (including self-hosted vLLM/TGI/Ollama/llamafile/LM Studio), multiple decoders and embedders, all selectable per flow. +- Retrieval designed for explainability: concept extraction -> entity vector seeding -> hop-and-filter with a local cross-encoder -> source tracing -> explainability DAG visible in the UI. +- Multiple extraction strategies, including ontology-guided (OntoRAG) and agentic extraction, plus structured-data ingestion with GraphQL/NL query. +- Horizontal scalability and isolation: each processor scales independently, flows are isolated per workspace, Cassandra/Qdrant scale out. +- Rich agent runtime (ReAct, plan-then-execute, supervisor fan-out, MCP tools, tool groups/state machines) with per-step provenance. + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +- **Deployment weight**: minimum stack is Pulsar (plus ZooKeeper/BookKeeper), Cassandra, Qdrant, Garage/MinIO, the gateway, config/flow/IAM services and a dozen processors - heavy for a single developer or small corpus; local development relies on process groups and the dev installer. +- The platform is only configurable through the external `@trustgraph/config` generator and seed files; default flow blueprints and prompt texts are not in the main repository, which makes auditing defaults harder. +- **Knowledge quality controls are thin**: no entity resolution/deduplication beyond identical IRIs minted from the entity string (`to_uri` URL-quotes the surface form, so "Acme" and "Acme Corp" are different nodes), no description merging, no confidence/weights on edges, no schema pruning outside OntoRAG. +- No incremental re-sync or fact retraction; collection-level deletion only. +- SPARQL is executed by client-side decomposition and in-memory joins, which will not scale to analytical queries; GraphQL covers structured rows only. +- No community/global summarisation mode; Graph RAG is entity-seeded local traversal with bounded hops. +- Rapid architectural churn (legacy `ConsumerProducer` processors such as topics extraction still present but unwired; multiple migration specs); API gateway and CLI changed incompatibly between 1.8 and 2.1 (`docs/api-gateway-changes-v1.8-to-v2.1.md`, `cli-changes-v1.8-to-v2.1.md`). +- Python code is largely untyped at the message boundary (dataclasses, hand-rolled serialisation), and many processors share near-duplicate boilerplate. +- No benchmarks; the "policy runtime" marketed in the README is only partially visible in code (IAM, audit, tool gating). + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +Choose TrustGraph when you need an on-prem, multi-tenant knowledge platform rather than a library: regulated environments that require RDF/OWL interoperability and PROV-O-grade provenance for every answer, teams that want to self-host open-weight models end to end, or organisations running agent workloads that must be traced and gated. It is also the only one of the three that ingests office formats, images and structured data into the same graph. Avoid it for prototypes, single-tenant apps with a modest corpus, or when your team is standardised on a property-graph database and wants to write Cypher - the operational cost of the broker-and-processor architecture only pays off at platform scale. + +## 14. Core idea in one paragraph + +Youtu-GraphRAG threads one **graph schema** (a JSON with `Nodes`, `Relations`, `Attributes` type lists) through every stage. At build time an LLM extracts, per chunk, entity attributes, `[s, r, o]` triples and entity types that conform to the schema (and, in "agent" mode, may propose new schema types that get written back to the schema file). The result is a NetworkX graph organised into four levels: attributes (L1), entities/relations (L2), keywords (L3) and LLM-named communities (L4), where communities come from a custom "Tree-Comm" clustering that mixes sentence-embedding similarity of each node's one-hop triples with Jaccard structural similarity. At query time an LLM decomposer reads the same schema to split the question into sub-questions and to predict which schema types are involved; each sub-question is run in parallel through a multi-path FAISS retriever (node/relation/triple/community indices plus chunk embeddings, keyword and path search), results are merged into "Triples + Chunks" context, an initial answer is produced, and an IRCoT loop then alternates LLM reasoning and new retrieval until the model emits "So the answer is:". The pitch is that schema-bounded extraction gives cheaper, cleaner graphs and that schema-aware decomposition plus community/keyword levels give better multi-hop accuracy per token than LightRAG/HippoRAG-style baselines. + +## 3. Indexing pipeline, step by step + +Entry: `main.py::graph_construction()` → `KTBuilder(dataset, schema_path, mode, config).build_knowledge_graph(corpus_path)` (`models/constructor/kt_gen.py`). The web backend (`backend.py::/api/construct-graph`) calls the same builder after turning uploads into a corpus JSON via `utils/document_parser.py`. + +1. **Load schema** – `KTBuilder.load_schema()` reads `schemas/.json` (e.g. `schemas/demo.json`: 10 node types `person, location, organization, event, object, concept, time_period, creative_work, biological_entity, natural_phenomenon`; 12 relations; 11 attribute names). Missing file → empty dict (extraction then runs schema-free). +2. **Load corpus** – `json_repair.load` of a list of docs (`{title, text}` dicts or strings). +3. **Chunking** – `KTBuilder.chunk_text()`. Datasets listed in `construction.datasets_no_chunk` (hotpot, 2wiki, musique, graphrag-bench, demo, ...) are *not* chunked: each doc is one chunk. Otherwise `_split_text_with_overlap()` does fixed token windows (cl100k) with `construction.chunk_size` (default **5000**) and `overlap` 200, merging tails shorter than `min_tail_tokens` 100. Chunk ids are 8-char `nanoid`s; `all_chunks` is later dumped to `output/chunks/.txt` as `id: \tChunk: ` lines – this file is the chunk store used at query time. +4. **Per-chunk LLM extraction** – `process_document()` runs `process_level1_level2_agent()` (mode `agent`, default) or `process_level1_level2()` (mode `noagent`). Prompt selection in `_get_construction_prompt()`: `prompts.construction.general` / `general_agent` (or `novel`, `novel_eng` variants) from `config/base_config.yaml`, formatted with `{schema}` and `{chunk}`. One `LLMCompletionCall.call_api()` call per chunk (`utils/call_llm_api.py`, OpenAI-compatible chat, `temperature=0.3`). Output JSON (`json_repair`-parsed) has `attributes: {entity: ["k: v", ...]}`, `triples: [[s, r, o], ...]`, `entity_types: {entity: type}` and, in agent mode, `new_schema_types: {nodes, relations, attributes}`. +5. **Schema evolution (agent mode only)** – `_update_schema_with_new_types()` appends unseen types to `schemas/.json` on disk and in memory. Note the hard-coded `schema_paths` map only covers `hotpot, 2wiki, musique, novel, graphrag-bench`; for other datasets (including `demo` and user uploads) the function silently returns, so schema evolution does not happen for custom datasets unless you edit that map. +6. **Graph assembly** – `_process_attributes[_agent]` creates one `attribute` node (`attr_`, level 1, `properties={name: "k: v", "chunk id": id}`) per attribute string and an edge `entity --has_attribute--> attr`. `_process_triples[_agent]` creates/looks up `entity` nodes (`entity_`, level 2, `properties={name, "chunk id", schema_type}`) and adds edge `subj ----> obj` on a `nx.MultiDiGraph`. Entity resolution is **exact name match** (`_find_or_create_entity` scans all nodes linearly under a lock – O(V) per lookup). Only the *first* chunk id is kept on an entity. +7. **Concurrency** – `process_all_documents()` uses a `ThreadPoolExecutor` (`construction.max_workers` 32, capped at `cpu_count+4`), one future per document; progress/ETA logging. +8. **Triple dedup** – `triple_deduplicate()` rebuilds the MultiDiGraph keeping one edge per `(u, v, relation)`. +9. **Level 4: communities** – `process_level4()` instantiates `utils/tree_comm.py::FastTreeComm(graph, embedding_model=all-MiniLM-L6-v2, struct_weight=0.3)` and calls `detect_communities(level2_nodes)`: + - Node representation: the concatenation of its one-hop triple strings `"name rel neighbor"` (`_get_triple_strings`), embedded with SentenceTransformer in batches (`get_triple_embeddings_batch`). + - `_fast_clustering`: KMeans with `n_clusters = clamp(N//10, 2, min(N//2, 200))`. + - Clusters larger than 3 are refined (`_refine_cluster`): KMeans again inside, then centres (the top "keyword" node of each sub-cluster) are compared with a fused similarity `0.3 * Jaccard(neighbour sets) + 0.7 * cosine(triple embeddings)` (`_compute_sim_matrix`) and merged greedily when `>= merge_threshold 0.5` and merged size `<= 100`, for `max_iter=1` pass. + - Global cap `tree_comm.max_total_communities` (default 100) – once reached, remaining KMeans clusters are emitted as communities without refinement. + - This is the "dually-perceived community detection" from the paper; it is KMeans + one merge pass, not Leiden/Louvain. +10. **Community naming + Level 3 keywords** – `create_super_nodes_with_keywords(comm_to_nodes, level=4)`: communities with ≥2 members are batched 5 at a time into one LLM prompt (`_build_batch_prompt`: centre name, first 10 member names, size) that returns `{id, name, summary}` per community. A `community` node `comm_4_` (level 4, `properties={name, description, members:[names]}`) is added with `member --member_of--> community` edges. Then `extract_keywords_from_community()` picks top-5 members by `0.3*normalised degree + 0.7*cosine(node, community mean embedding)` and creates `keyword` nodes `kw__` (level 3) with edges `entity --represented_by--> keyword`, `keyword --keyword_of--> community`, and `entity --kw_filter_by--> keyword`. Keywords are therefore *entity names promoted to keywords*, not separately extracted terms. +11. **Serialisation** – `format_output()` flattens to a list of `{start_node:{label, properties}, relation, end_node:{label, properties}}` written to `output/graphs/_new.json` (importable to Neo4j per README). `utils/graph_processor.load_graph_from_json()` rebuilds the MultiDiGraph at query time; GraphML save/load helpers also exist. +12. **Index build (lazy, at first query)** – `KTRetriever.build_indices()` → `DualFAISSRetriever.build_indices()` creates four `faiss.IndexFlatIP` indices with L2-normalised MiniLM vectors under `retriever/faiss_cache_new//`: `node.index` (text = `"name,description"` of every node incl. attributes/keywords/communities), `relation.index` (unique relation strings), `triple.index` (`"head_text,rel,tail_text"` per edge), `comm.index` (`"name,description"` of community nodes), plus `*_map.json` id maps, `node_embeddings.pt/.npy`, `node_embedding_cache.pt`, `dim_transform.pt` (a random `torch.nn.Linear(model_dim, 384)` projection applied only if the embedding model is not 384-d – untrained, so swapping to a larger model degrades search). `KTRetriever` additionally builds a chunk FAISS index (`_precompute_chunk_embeddings`, cached in `chunk_embedding_cache.pt`), a node-text keyword inverted index (`_build_node_text_index` → `node_text_index.pkl`), and a node-text cache. Graph / tree data model + +NetworkX `MultiDiGraph`; every node has `label`, `level`, `properties` (a dict). + +| Level | `label` | id pattern | `properties` | Created by | +|---|---|---|---|---| +| 1 | `attribute` | `attr_` | `name` ("key: value" string), `chunk id` | `_process_attributes` | +| 2 | `entity` | `entity_` | `name`, `chunk id` (first only), `schema_type` | `_find_or_create_entity` | +| 3 | `keyword` | `kw__` | `name` (= an entity's name) | `create_super_nodes_with_keywords` | +| 4 | `community` | `comm_4_` | `name`, `description` (LLM summary), `members` (list of entity names) | `create_super_nodes` | + +Edges (`relation` attribute on the edge): `has_attribute` (entity→attribute), free-text predicates from extraction (entity→entity), `member_of` (entity→community), `represented_by` (entity→keyword), `keyword_of` (keyword→community), `kw_filter_by` (entity→keyword). Communities are flat (one level of L4; no hierarchy of communities despite the "tree" naming). Chunks are **not** nodes: provenance is the `chunk id` property and the sidecar `output/chunks/.txt`. There are no embeddings on the graph itself; vectors live in the FAISS cache directory. No entity descriptions are generated (the `description` field read by `_get_node_text` is only present on community nodes). + +## 5. Query / retrieval modes + +Entry points: CLI `main.py::retrieval()` chooses `no_agent_retrieval` or `agent_retrieval` by `triggers.mode`; the web endpoint `/api/ask-question` always forces agent mode. Both start from `initial_question_decomposition()`. + +### 6.1 Stage A – schema-aware decomposition (`models/retriever/agentic_decomposer.py::GraphQ`) + +One LLM call with `prompts.decomposition.general` (ontology = raw schema file text, question) returning `{"sub_questions": [{"sub-question": ...}], "involved_types": {"nodes": [...], "relations": [...], "attributes": [...]}}`. Simple questions are returned as a single sub-question. On parse/LLM failure the original question is used with empty types. + +### 6.2 Stage B – per-sub-question retrieval (`KTRetriever.process_retrieval_results`) + +If >1 sub-question, `process_subquestions_parallel` runs them in a thread pool (`retrieval.faiss.max_workers` 4). For each: + +- `retrieve_with_type_filtering(question, involved_types)`: if `involved_types.nodes` is non-empty, `_filter_nodes_by_schema_type` restricts candidate entity nodes to those `schema_type`s and runs cosine search on that subset (`_similarity_search_on_filtered_nodes`), then 1-hop triples; otherwise falls back to `retrieve()`. +- `retrieve()` with `recall_paths=2` (default) → `_parallel_dual_path_retrieval`: + - **Path 1 – node/relation retrieval** (`_node_relation_retrieval`), itself parallel: FAISS node search (`search_k = min(3*top_k, 50)`) → re-score candidates with cosine to the question (`_batch_calculate_entity_similarities`); spaCy keyword extraction (`_extract_query_keywords`: NER + NOUN/PROPN/ADJ/VERB tokens) → exact-match lookup in the node-text inverted index (`_keyword_based_node_search`) → same re-scoring, threshold 0.05; FAISS relation search; **chunk FAISS search** (`_chunk_embedding_retrieval`, top_k); merge candidates, keep top `top_k` nodes; expand with `_optimized_neighbor_expansion` (1-hop triples re-scored), `_path_based_search` (DFS to depth 2 from top nodes toward keyword-matching nodes) and `_get_relation_matched_triples` (triples from top nodes whose relation is among the FAISS-matched relations). + - **Path 2 – triple/community retrieval** (`_triple_only_retrieval` → `DualFAISSRetriever.dual_path_retrieval`): FAISS triple search (top_k) → for each hit also collect triples around the 3-hop neighbourhood of head and tail (`_collect_neighbor_triples`, `_get_3hop_neighbors`) → dedupe → `_calculate_triple_relevance_scores` (cosine, threshold 0.1, top_k). Community search (`retrieve_via_communities`: FAISS over community name+summary → expand to member entity ids via `properties.members` and `name_to_id`) also runs here, but **only `scored_triples` is consumed** by `_triple_only_retrieval`; `comm_nodes` are computed and dropped. The L4 community level therefore influences retrieval only indirectly (community nodes are in `node.index` and their keyword nodes are in the node index). +- Chunk ids are gathered from top nodes' `chunk id`, from triple endpoints and from the chunk FAISS hits, capped at `top_k`. +- `process_retrieval_results` then: reranks chunk hits (`_process_chunk_results` → `_rerank_chunks_by_relevance`, average of FAISS score and fresh cosine), collects and scores all triples from both paths (`_collect_all_scored_triples`, `_rerank_triples_by_relevance`), keeps `top_k` (`retrieval.top_k_filter` 20), formats triples as strings (`_format_scored_triples`), and resolves chunk texts from `chunk2id`. + +### 6.3 Stage C – context assembly and initial answer (`main.py::initial_question_decomposition`) + +Union of all sub-question triples and chunks; if more than 20 triples, keep the 20 with most question-word overlap; if more than `top_k_filter` chunks, `rerank_chunks_by_keywords` (keyword overlap). Context string = `"=== Triples ===\n...\n=== Chunks ===\n..."`. One LLM call with `prompts.retrieval.general` → `initial_answer` (retried up to 20 times on empty output). + +### 6.4 Mode `noagent` + +Stops after Stage C; the initial answer is the final answer. `utils/eval.py::Eval` (LLM-as-judge returning "1"/"0") scores against gold when running benchmarks. + +### 6.5 Mode `agent` (IRCoT loop, `main.py::agent_retrieval`) + +Starting from Stage C's triples/chunks/answer (added as "Initial analysis (noagent mode): ..." thought), for `step in 1..retrieval.agent.max_steps` (5): +1. Build context from all accumulated triples/chunks; prompt is the inline IRCoT template in `agent_retrieval` (the YAML `prompts.retrieval.ircot` key exists but the CLI uses its own inline copy that also mentions the initial analysis) with `Previous Thoughts` = all prior thoughts. +2. One LLM call. If the response contains `"So the answer is:"` → stop. Else parse `"The new query is:"` (fallback: the whole response), and if it differs from the current query run `process_retrieval_results(new_query)` (no type filtering here) and merge new triples/chunks. +3. After the loop, one more LLM call with `prompts.retrieval.general` over the final merged context produces the answer. + +"Reflection" in the README maps to this thought-then-requery loop; there is no explicit answer-verification or self-critique prompt beyond the IRCoT instruction text. + +```mermaid +sequenceDiagram + participant U as User + participant D as GraphQ decomposer (LLM) + participant R as KTRetriever + participant F as DualFAISSRetriever / FAISS + participant L as LLM + U->>D: question + schema + D-->>R: sub_questions[], involved_types + par per sub-question (thread pool) + R->>F: node/relation/triple/chunk FAISS search + F-->>R: candidates + R->>R: keyword + path + 1-hop expansion, rerank triples/chunks + end + R-->>L: "=== Triples === ... === Chunks ===" + prompts.retrieval.general + L-->>R: initial_answer + loop IRCoT, max_steps=5 + R->>L: ircot prompt (context + previous thoughts) + alt "So the answer is:" + L-->>R: stop + else "The new query is: q'" + R->>F: process_retrieval_results(q') + F-->>R: new triples/chunks merged + end + end + R->>L: final prompt over merged context + L-->>U: answer (+ sub-questions, reasoning steps, retrieved triples for UI) +``` + +## 7. Generation / answer synthesis + +- Prompts are plain strings in `config/base_config.yaml` under `prompts.construction.*`, `prompts.decomposition.*`, `prompts.retrieval.{general, ircot, novel, novel_eng}`; resolved by `ConfigManager.get_prompt_formatted(section, name, **kwargs)`. Dataset names `novel`/`novel_eng`/`anony_chs` switch to Chinese or novel-specific variants. +- The answer prompt (`retrieval.general`) instructs: use only the provided context, "If the knowledge is insufficient, reject to answer", be concise, give specific entity/date. The novel variants instead allow falling back to model knowledge. +- Reasoning loop: IRCoT as described above, max 5 steps, stop token phrases `So the answer is:` / `The new query is:`. +- Citations: none. Context triples carry entity names but no chunk ids; chunks are inserted as raw text without ids. The web UI returns `sub_questions`, `reasoning_steps`, and `retrieved_triples` for visualisation (`backend.py::prepare_subquery_visualization`, `prepare_retrieved_graph_visualization`), which is the only provenance surface. +- Every generation call is `temperature=0.3` via `LLMCompletionCall.call_api`, with a wrapper that strips code fences; retries are implemented as `for retry in range(20)` loops in `main.py`. + +## 8. LLM and embedding usage, cost profile + +**Indexing** +- LLM: exactly **1 call per chunk** for extraction (attributes + triples + types + optional schema delta in one shot) plus **1 call per 5 communities** for naming/summaries. With `chunk_size=5000` tokens that is few, large calls; with benchmark datasets (no chunking) it is one call per document. The repo's `token_cal` logs total prompt+response tokens. The README claims 33.6% lower token cost than SOTA baselines, attributable to single-pass extraction and no per-entity description generation. +- Embeddings: local MiniLM, no API cost: all nodes (incl. attribute/keyword/community nodes), all unique relations, all triples, all communities, all chunks, plus triple-string embeddings for Tree-Comm. CPU is the default; this is the wall-clock bottleneck for large graphs. +- Also: KMeans/refinement, O(V) linear scans for entity dedup during extraction (quadratic overall in entity count, under a lock – throughput drops on big corpora). + +**Query** (agent mode, `max_steps=5`) +- 1 decomposition call + 1 initial answer call + 1–5 IRCoT calls + 1 final answer call ≈ **4–8 LLM calls** per question (plus 1 judge call when evaluating). Noagent mode: 2 calls. +- Embedding: question (cached per text) and sub-questions; chunk reranking re-encodes each candidate chunk with MiniLM per call. +- Context size: up to 20 triples + up to 20 chunks; with 5000-token chunks the prompt can reach ~100k tokens – `top_k_filter` should be reduced for large-chunk corpora. +- FAISS searches are memoised per (query vector, k) in `faiss_search_cache`. + +## 9. Configuration and extension points + +- **Single YAML**: `config/base_config.yaml`, loaded by `config/config_loader.py::ConfigManager` / `get_config(path)`; `main.py --config` and `--override '{"retrieval.top_k": 10}'` (dotted-key JSON) for runtime overrides. Sections: `construction` (`chunk_size`, `overlap`, `datasets_no_chunk`, `max_workers`, `mode: agent|noagent`, `tree_comm.{embedding_model, struct_weight, max_total_communities, enable_fast_mode}`), `datasets..{corpus_path, qa_path, schema_path, graph_output}`, `embeddings.{model_name, device, batch_size, max_length}`, `nlp.spacy_model`, `retrieval.{top_k, top_k_filter, recall_paths (1|2), similarity_threshold, enable_reranking, enable_query_enhancement, enable_high_recall, enable_caching, cache_dir, faiss.{device, max_workers, search_k}, agent.{enable_ircot, enable_parallel_subquestions, max_steps}}`, `triggers.{constructor_trigger, retrieve_trigger, mode}`, `prompts.*`. +- **LLM**: `.env` only (`LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY`, optional Azure vars). One model for everything; no per-stage model choice without editing `LLMCompletionCall`. +- **Embedding model**: `embeddings.model_name` (any SentenceTransformer). Non-384-d models trigger the untrained `dim_transform` linear layer – effectively you should stay with 384-d models or fix the projection. +- **Schema**: add `schemas/.json` with `Nodes/Relations/Attributes` lists and a `datasets.` entry; the UI exposes `/api/datasets/{name}/schema` upload. Schema evolution write-back is limited to the hard-coded dataset map in `_update_schema_with_new_types`. +- **Prompts**: edit YAML; dataset-name-based routing in `_get_construction_prompt`, `GraphQ.prompt_format`, `KTRetriever.generate_prompt`. +- **Retrieval knobs**: `recall_paths=1` disables Path 2; `involved_types` filtering is automatic from decomposition; `top_k_filter` caps triples/chunks. +- **Document ingestion**: `utils/document_parser.py` (PDF via MinerU/pypdf, DOCX, RTF, Tika fallback) feeding `/api/upload`; CLI expects pre-built corpus JSON. +- **Incremental update**: **not supported.** `graph_construction` calls `clear_cache_files(dataset)` and rebuilds from the corpus; `KTBuilder.save_chunks_to_file` overwrites the chunk file ("fresh start"); the backend's `/api/datasets/{name}/reconstruct` is a full rebuild; FAISS caches are invalidated whenever the node set changes. Adding documents means re-extracting everything (and re-running Tree-Comm, which re-ids communities). +- **Extension**: no plugin registry; swap components by editing `main.py`/`backend.py` wiring (`constructor.KTBuilder`, `decomposer.GraphQ`, `retriever.KTRetriever`). + +## 10. Benchmarks reported by the authors + +From README/paper (the repo has no results tables; `utils/eval.py` is an LLM judge, and `main.py` prints accuracy): + +- Evaluated on six benchmarks including **HotpotQA, MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, GraphRAG-Bench** and the authors' new **AnonyRAG** (Chinese + English; entity names anonymised to defeat pretraining leakage; https://huggingface.co/datasets/Youtu-Graph/AnonyRAG). +- Headline: "33.6% lower token cost and 16.62% higher accuracy over state-of-the-art baselines", presented as moving the accuracy/cost Pareto frontier (figures `assets/performance.png`, `assets/pareto.png`, `assets/radar.png`). Per-dataset numbers are only in the paper (arXiv:2508.19855); they are not reproduced in the repo. +- Tree-Comm is claimed to beat Leiden/Louvain community structure for retrieval, again only in the paper. +- Accuracy is judged by an LLM ("reasonable, not too strict or too lenient"), not EM/F1, which makes cross-paper comparison loose. + +No independent third-party reproductions were found in the repo or its docs. + +## 11. Strengths + +- **Schema-in-the-loop design**: one JSON schema bounds extraction, drives `involved_types` filtering at query time, and (in agent mode) grows itself – a cheap way to adapt to a new domain. +- **Cheap graph construction**: one LLM call per chunk covering attributes, triples and types; no per-entity description generation, no gleaning passes; community summaries are batched 5 per call. +- **Multi-path, parallel retrieval** with many complementary signals (dense nodes/relations/triples/chunks, keyword inverted index, 2-hop path search, 3-hop triple neighbourhoods) and sub-question parallelism. +- **IRCoT loop** gives genuine iterative retrieval for multi-hop questions, with transparent reasoning traces surfaced in the UI. +- **Local, dependency-light storage**: NetworkX + FAISS files + a text file; no graph database or vector DB to operate; Docker image and web UI with upload, build, and graph visualisation. +- Bilingual (EN/CN) prompts and datasets; Azure support. + +## 12. Limitations and known issues + +- **Research-code status**: no tests, no packaging, 2.7k-line retriever with many near-duplicate/legacy methods (`_keyword_based_node_search_original`, `_execute_retrieval_strategies_parallel` vs `_node_relation_retrieval`), commented-out code paths, 20-iteration retry loops, `threading.Lock()` created inline per use (ineffective), and `debug_mode = True` hard-coded. +- **Community level is mostly unused at query time**: `retrieve_via_communities` results are discarded by `_triple_only_retrieval`; the L3/L4 levels mainly add nodes to the node index. The "top-down filtering" the README describes is not wired into the default path. +- **Entity resolution is exact string match** with no normalisation/aliasing and an O(V) scan per lookup under a global lock – both quality (duplicates like "T.I." vs "T.I") and throughput degrade with corpus size. +- **Untrained dimension projection** (`torch.nn.Linear` random init) when using non-384-d embedding models. +- **Schema evolution only for hard-coded datasets**; for uploads the LLM is asked for `new_schema_types` that are then thrown away. +- **No incremental indexing**; full rebuild and cache invalidation on any change. No document-level deletion. +- **No citations / provenance in answers**; chunk ids are stripped from context. +- **Scalability**: in-memory NetworkX graph, flat FAISS indices (`IndexFlatIP`, no ANN), CPU MiniLM; the FULLGUIDE documents FAISS segfault workarounds for large datasets. Chunk default of 5000 tokens makes contexts very large. +- **Single global LLM**; no small-model routing for extraction vs reasoning. +- Spacy `en_core_web_lg` and English-centric keyword extraction; Chinese keyword path depends on the same pipeline. +- License text is MIT-like but bespoke ("Youtu-GraphRAG License"); check with legal if that matters. + +## 13. Best fit / when to choose it + +- Teams with a known domain ontology (or willing to write a short type list) who want a schema-guided, relatively cheap graph build and multi-hop QA with visible reasoning traces, at corpus sizes of thousands (not millions) of chunks. +- Researchers benchmarking against HotpotQA/MuSiQue/2Wiki/GraphRAG-Bench/AnonyRAG with an agentic decomposition + IRCoT baseline. +- Prototyping a self-hosted GraphRAG demo quickly (Docker + UI) without standing up Neo4j/Milvus. +- Not a fit for: production services needing incremental updates, provenance, multi-tenant storage, or a maintained SDK; very large corpora; non-English/Chinese text without re-prompting. For enterprise use the authors point to Tencent Cloud ADP's closed Enterprise Edition. + +## 14.
